description: Secchiello portapopcorn a tema Buzz Lightyear, progettato per la stampa multicolore SENZA necessità di AMS/multi-material unit. Questo modello riproduce Buzz Lightyear in versione secchiello per popcorn, perfetto come pezzo da collezione, decorazione a tema o contenitore per la tua prossima serata cinema Toy Story. 🎨 Stampa multicolore senza AMS Il progetto è stato appositamente suddiviso in 78 parti separate , organizzate su 13 piatti di stampa , in modo da poter cambiare filamento manualmente tra un piatto e l'altro. Questo significa che puoi ottenere un risultato multicolore accurato e dettagliato anche senza sistema AMS , semplicemente cambiando la bobina di filamento prima di avviare ogni piatto. Ogni piatto è organizzato per colore, così da minimizzare i cambi di filamento e rendere il workflow di stampa il più semplice possibile. Colori utilizzati (filamenti Bambu Lab): Grigio, Rosso, Giallo, Verde, Viola, Celeste, Nero, Bianco 🔧 Assemblaggio semplice e guidato Il montaggio è stato pensato per essere il più intuitivo possibile: ogni pezzo ha giunti a incastro (perno e foro) obbligati, progettati con tolleranza di 0.2mm, che permettono di unire le parti in un solo verso corretto, evitando errori di posizionamento. Anche per le ali, i giunti hanno misure diverse tra loro: questo significa che i pezzi non possono essere invertiti per errore, rendendo il montaggio ancora più semplice e guidato anche per chi non ha esperienza di assemblaggio di modelli multi-parte. ⚠️ La colla è necessaria : gli incastri servono principalmente a guidare e allineare correttamente le parti tra loro, ma da soli non garantiscono la tenuta strutturale del modello. Si consiglia di usare colla (es. cianoacrilato o colla a caldo) su ogni giunto per un assemblaggio solido e duraturo. Nota sullo stemma centrale: lo stemma presente al centro della parte celeste del secchiello va stampato in versione piatta (non curva) e poi incollato direttamente sulla superficie celeste, dopo la stampa. 🖨️ Dettagli di stampa consigliati Stampante testata: Bambu Lab A1 Nessun AMS richiesto Cambio filamento manuale tra un piatto e l'altro Layer height e supporti da valutare in base al livello di dettaglio desiderato 📦 Cosa include il file 13 piatti pre-organizzati per colore 78 parti pronte per la stampa Giunti di incastro obbligati (misure diverse per ogni posizione) già integrati nel modello

description: Spin Your Words – Custom Text Grip Fidget Ring This is not just another fidget ring with text on it. This is a fully parametric print-in-place spinner ring where the custom text becomes the actual tactile grip of the rotating outer ring. Instead of using standard grooves, ribs or generic knurling, the external grip is generated directly from your own text, name, brand, nickname, date or message. Your text is not decoration. Your text is the grip. A Personal Message You Can Wear, Touch and Spin Because the grip is generated from custom text, this ring can become much more than a simple fidget toy. It can be a name, a romantic message, a special date, a couple nickname, an inside joke, a maker signature or a short phrase wrapped around a rotating ring. This makes it perfect as a unique personalized gift for someone special. A small object, but with a message built directly into its function. You can turn a name, a date or a love message into a tactile spinning ring. Examples: I LOVE YOU FOREVER YOU & ME MY LOVE ALWAYS LUCA ❤️ SARA SINCE 2024 SPIN MY HEART The message is not hidden inside the model. It is the part you touch, feel and spin. The Key Idea Most fidget rings use a standard external pattern for grip. This model does something different. The outer rotating ring uses raised custom text wrapped around the side surface as the tactile texture. The letters create: the grip the feel the visual identity the personalization So every ring can be different. Minimal, romantic, funny, branded, personal or completely weird: it depends only on the text you choose. Custom Text Becomes Functional Grip The text is placed on the outside of the rotating ring and follows the circular shape of the model. It is not simply stamped on a flat face. It is not just decorative branding. It becomes the surface your fingers touch while spinning the ring. Short texts are automatically repeated around the ring. Longer phrases are repeated only when they fit completely. No broken words. No interrupted messages. Only complete readable text patterns. Main Features Custom text used as tactile grip Print-in-place spinner ring Two-piece rotating structure No assembly required No external knurling Raised side text replaces the grip texture Automatic full-word text repetition No interrupted words or broken phrases Parametric inner diameter Adjustable ring width Adjustable text spacing Adjustable character width Adjustable text relief Adjustable print-in-place clearances Comfort-fit internal profile Chamfered inner edges for easier wearing Supportless design Designed for MakerWorld Customizer Multicolor-ready design Assembly and separate-part export modes What Makes It Different This model combines three things in one object: custom text + functional tactile grip + print-in-place rotating fidget ring The result is a small, simple object with a very clear identity: a personalized spinner ring where the message itself becomes the texture. It is not a ring with a label. It is a ring where the label becomes the grip. Text Ideas You can use names, brands, nicknames, short messages, romantic phrases or maker signatures. Examples: Made by CiCAdesign SPIN YOUR WORDS YOUR TEXT HERE FOCUS RELAX MAKER CREATE CUSTOM I LOVE YOU FOREVER ALWAYS YOU & ME Short words will repeat several times around the ring. Longer phrases will appear only as complete repetitions. Print-in-Place Mechanism The model is made of two separate functional parts printed together: an inner ring that stays fixed an outer ring that rotates around it Both parts rest on the build plate, making the model easier to print without supports. After printing, gently free the outer ring and rotate it gradually until the mechanism becomes smooth. Clearance parameters are available to adapt the model to different printers, materials and calibration levels. Export Modes The Customizer includes different export modes. Use: complete_assembly to generate the full print-in-place ring as one STL. Use the separate modes: inner_ring_only outer_rotating_ring_only text_grip_only to generate the three individual parts separately. The separate-part exports are useful for advanced multicolor workflows where the parts are imported together into the slicer as a single multipart object. Multicolor Printing This model can be printed in two different ways. Single Color Print For a standard single-color print, use the full assembly export and print the STL as it is. No extra steps are required. Select complete_assembly Export STL Import into slicer Print normally This is the simplest option and works like a normal print-in-place fidget ring. Multicolor Print – Single STL Workflow For the quickest multicolor workflow, export the full assembly STL and split it into parts inside Bambu Studio. Recommended workflow: 1. Select complete_assembly 2. Export STL 3. Import the STL into Bambu Studio 4. Right click on the model 5. Select Split 6. Choose Split to Parts 7. Assign a different filament/color to each part 8. Disable Arachne wall generator 9. Use Classic wall generator 10. Slice and print The model is designed to be divided into separate printable parts: inner ring outer rotating ring text grip This allows you to create 2-color or 3-color versions. Examples: outer ring: blue inner ring: light gray text grip: white or: outer ring: black inner ring: gold text grip: ivory or: outer ring: white inner ring: teal text grip: coral Multicolor Print – Separate Part Workflow For the cleanest multicolor setup, you can also export the three parts separately from the same SCAD file. Use: inner_ring_only outer_rotating_ring_only text_grip_only Then import the three generated STL files together into Bambu Studio as a single object with multiple parts. This workflow is useful if you want better control over the three colors and want the slicer to treat each component as a separate part from the beginning. In this workflow, the text grip export is positioned to bond correctly with the outer rotating ring when the parts are imported together. Important Multicolor Note When the complete assembly is split into parts, you may see very thin construction lines connecting the raised letters. These lines are intentional. They are used only to keep the custom text connected as a single selectable text-grip part inside the slicer, instead of having every letter detected as a separate object. These construction lines are necessary for multicolor part detection. They are not intended as visible design details. Do not use Arachne wall generator for multicolor printing. Use Classic wall generator instead. With Arachne enabled, the slicer may try to print these thin construction lines. With Classic wall generator, they should remain non-printable construction geometry and disappear from the final toolpath. So, when using multicolor mode: inner ring = one part outer rotating ring = one part text grip = one connected part This makes it much easier to assign colors in Bambu Studio without selecting every single letter manually. Final practical note: For single-color printing, print the complete assembly normally. For quick multicolor printing, split the complete assembly into parts and assign colors. Produced in extremely limited numbers during the final years of the R34 generation, the Nismo variants and conversion packages were developed using knowledge gained directly from endurance racing and the GT500 Super GT program. At its core sits the legendary RB26DETT 2.6-liter twin-turbocharged inline-six , officially rated at 276 horsepower due to Japan’s gentleman’s agreement, though real output was significantly higher and often exceeded 330 horsepower in factory form, paired with a 6-speed Getrag manual transmission and Nissan’s advanced ATTESA E-TS Pro all-wheel-drive system , capable of dynamically distributing torque between the front and rear wheels for incredible grip and stability under all conditions. Combined with the Super-HICAS four-wheel steering system , the R34 Nismo delivered exceptional agility and cornering precision despite its relatively compact dimensions. The Nismo treatment focused heavily on improving chassis rigidity, aerodynamics, and responsiveness. The car featured upgraded suspension tuning, reinforced bushings, stiffer sway bars, improved cooling systems, and enhanced braking performance, all designed to sharpen the car’s behavior both on the road and the racetrack. Visually, the GT-R R34 Nismo became instantly recognizable thanks to its aggressive aerodynamic upgrades, including a redesigned front bumper with larger cooling ducts, side skirts, rear spats, a carbon fiber rear diffuser, and the iconic adjustable GT-style rear wing, all inspired by Nissan’s motorsport programs and engineered to improve high-speed stability and airflow efficiency. One of the most famous versions was the Nismo Z-Tune , built using hand-selected low-mileage R34 chassis and re-engineered almost entirely by Nismo, featuring a stroked 2.8-liter Z2 RB engine producing around 500 horsepower , extensive use of carbon fiber body panels, race-derived suspension geometry, and bespoke aerodynamic development, becoming widely regarded as the ultimate Skyline GT-R ever produced. Only 19 Z-Tunes were ever built, making them some of the rarest and most valuable Japanese cars in existence. The Nissan Skyline GT-R R34 Nismo became legendary not only because of its performance, but because it perfectly captured the golden era of Japanese engineering, combining advanced technology, tuning potential, motorsport heritage, and unmistakable styling into a machine that dominated video games, movies, street culture, and motorsport alike, ultimately cementing its place as one of the greatest and most iconic performance cars ever built. The model also uses an adjustable flat wing. The front propeller is a 3D printed 3 blade propeller driven by a rubber band. The materials and assembly approach are pretty similar, but this version was printed using Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament. This model is intended as a toy and a simple educational aircraft. Materials Required 3D printer duh Rubber band (40 to 50 mm) Super glue Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament or any other suitable filament. Optional: sandpaper or small file for cleaning tight printed joints Assembly Instructions Step 1: Print all parts Print all the model parts. For best results, keep the parts lightweight. A heavy fuselage or propeller will reduce flight performance. After printing, remove any stringing, rough edges or small blobs from the parts. Step 2: Adjust the adjustable wing The wing should sit straight and level when viewed from the front. Small changes to the wing position or angle can be used later to trim the flight path. Step 3: Insert the rod hook and attach the small nub Insert the rod, as shown in the pictures, and then add the nub on the outside of the nose of the plane. Do not glue anything as off yet. Step 4: Install the propeller Then insert the propeller after the nub and glue only the front of the propeller to the rod, make sure to not glue the nub to the nose or rod. Allow the glue to dry fully before installing the rubber band or testing the propeller. Check that the propeller can rotate freely, which then inturn should also now turn the hook and thus wind the rubber band. The nub should be abe to rotate independently to the propeller and hook. If the propeller is stiff, lightly clean or sand the contact area until it spins smoothly. Step 5: Attach the rubber band Attach one end of the rubber band to the rear hook on the fuselage. Attach the other end to the propeller hook. The rubber band should sit along the fuselage centreline. It should be tight enough to drive the propeller, but not so tight that it bends the fuselage or pulls the propeller out of alignment. Step 6: Check alignment Before winding the rubber band, check the full model alignment. The fuselage should be straight, the wing should be level or adjusted, and the propeller should spin freely. The rubber band should not rub heavily against the printed body. If the model turns too much during testing, adjust the wing position slightly and test again. Step 7: First test wind Wind the propeller gently by hand for the first test. Do not fully wind the rubber band immediately. Start with a low number of turns to check that the propeller works and that the rubber band stays attached. Release the propeller carefully and check that it spins smoothly. Step 8: Flight trimming Test the plane in a clear open area. If the nose drops or rises quickly, increase throw speed or try a different wing angle. (CoG sits below the wings so the issue can be fixed with just how you throw it). If the plane rolls or turns sharply, check that the wing is symmetrically bent or is flat and that the propeller is aligned with the fuselage centreline. Notes This model is designed for simple educational testing and is a toy, not long-distance powered flight (a motorised version would be cool). Lightweight printing improves performance. The propeller must spin freely for the rubber band mechanism to work properly. The adjustable wing is useful for experimenting with stability and trim. Test indoors only if there is enough space, or outdoors in calm conditions. Do not aim the plane at people, animals, windows or fragile objects. One of the weak points of this model is the hook for the rubber band at the back of the plane. Do reinforce it with either superglue (worked best for me) or epoxy. Print Material Used Printed using Bambu Lab PLA Matte Ivory White filament.

description: This is my take on a motorized shade solution for automating existing roller-style shades. This works with traditional cordless roller shades (the spring loaded type that you pull down). Its based around a relatively cheap aliexpress geared brushless motor with an encoder driven by an esp32 for use with ESPHome and HomeAssistant. The finished product is capable of accurate positional control and uses a reed switch at the full open position to re-home the system each time the shade is fully opened. They are relatively quiet, very reliable and operate on 12v DC power. You will have to attach a small magnet to the shade (with tape or something). Here is the Bill of Materials: Item Qty Links Socket head cap M3x6 5 Socket head cap M2x4 7 Small Neodymium Magnet 1 CHR-GM25-BL2418 DC12V i34 (130rpm variant) 1 Link Alibaba (cheaper for bulk) MKA17101 Reed Switch NO 1 Link 5v Buck Converter 1 Link 3x7cm Protoboards 1 Link ESP32 1 Link 608 2RS Ball Bearing 1 Link The more of these you build the cheaper they are per unit because you end up buying the smaller components in bulk anyways. If you make 5 of them they end up being around $25 each. Use Alibaba for the motors if ordering more than one or two. In theory you probably don't need a protoboard if you really want to cut costs. There are two versions of the printed files, one with holes sized for heat-set inserts and one with holes meant to be directly threaded into. Here is a diagram of the wiring: Push the reed switch as much towards the esp32 (into the page) as possible to get it closest to the magnet that you will attach to the shade. When attaching the magnet to the shade, it works best if it is mounted sideways rather than flat. Here is a picture of how I did it, and so far it has never failed to home properly after a month of use. Wherever you place it will determine the stopping point of the shade. The bottom endpoint is configurable inside home assistant. The only issue I have run into is drift over many cycles if the shade isn't homed for a while (eg. 50% →0% → 50%) over and over without fully opening. After around 20 ish cycles it will drift downwards about an inch. As long as they are opened fully periodically, this will never be a problem. Assembly should be pretty straightforward if you follow the exploded view diagram. The gear shroud needs to be snapped on and might require some force, Its not meant to come off again without breaking. I've also included a version of the wall plate with different mounting points for shallower window frames and the hangar I used for the other end of the shade. You may also need to make a different size shade insert to fit in your particular tube. If you leave a comment with the inner diameter of your tube i can add more variants. That's it! Happy printing!

I really like the design of BeamCase and I wanted a smaller version of it. So what I have created is basically that. I have based some of the design on the BeamCase (designed from scratch) - mainly the truss on the mobo tray. The case is not modular, there is only one 5.5L version - and I won't be making any other versions of it. Specs: 5.5L volume (not accounting for panels) Max 47mm cooler height Max 2 slot 200mm GPU Flex ATX PSU 90mm fans at the top - brackets are made for Noctua NF-A9x14 which are 14.5mm thick Filament: Frame - I've used Bambu Labs PETG-HF, but according to the internet It would be best if you used ABS or ASA for the internal parts, although you will need to take the shrinkage into the account Panels - Does not really matter, PLA is fine. I used Polymer Panchroma PLA Matte Lime Green Note on seams: If you want to use raw STLs, make sure the seams for the brackets that go into the T-Slots are NOT anywhere near the T-Slots. I have manually painted seams in the included profile to avoid that. Note on panels: Panels are in a separate print profile and have an internal infill-based pattern - which means you can control it in the slicer. I am partial to triangles but you can set it up however you want :) You will get better results using thicker nozzles, I've used 0.6mm - 0.4mm works ok too but the panels are a bit less rigid. Parts needed: 200mm double reverse PCI-E riser - Specifically this one (4.0) from Aliexpress Bracket is made to fit only this riser but I've included step file so you can modify it to fit yours 16mm push button for power button - you can buy it pre-made, I soldered my own, cable length should be ~20cm Hardware needed: 1010 T-Slot Makerbeam 200mm extrusion profiles T-Slot M3 Nuts from Makerbeam Countersunk M3 screws, just buy a whole bag of each, you can use them in different projects :) 6mm 8mm 12mm 16mm PSU - #6-32 x 3/8" UNC screws - I bought these M3 nuts Note: I take no responsibility for you breaking your potentially expensive PC parts. You are building this case at your own risk, so double-check clearances, whether you are using the correct length of screws, support heavy components, and proceed carefully. I only tested it with my own components and I cannot guarantee it will fit your exact configuration. Components I have used for my build: Mobo - Asrock B550M-ITX/ac Cooler - Thermalright AXP90-X47 Full Copper CPU Fan - NF-A12x15 with this bracket that I've slightly modified PSU - Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT GPU - Powercolor Radeon 9060XT Reaper Assembly Instructions: Here are all the 3D printed parts that you will need: (apart from the gpu bracket locker which I realised I forgot to print, it's present in subsequent pics) Tools that you will need: M3 driver - hex key is fine too but you will need more elbow grease Electric screwdriver with M3 bit (H2) - technically not necessary, but it will make it much easier Prepping the parts Insert hex nuts in correct places and press them in. 2 on the front of the mobo tray 4 on the back of the mobo tray 2 in the back of the case (power button) 2 in the gpu bracket locker 2 in the back of the pcie riser You should prepare the beams (inserting Makerbeam T-Slot nuts on the sides) before you start putting the case together. It will be really annoying to do afterwards - so my suggestion is to triple check everything and try to imagine how it will go together (feel free to scroll down to use the pics to help your imagination). The holes for panels are lined up exactly with the T-Slot nuts - on end positions. Note: The parts (brackets) that you insert into the beams have the T-Slot shaped in a way where you will be essentially “shaving” off a sliver of plastic when inserting them. That's by design, I found it gives the best fit. So if they do not “go in” all the way, take it out, flip them out, clear out the plastic shavings and try again. Top beams Insert fan brackets and push them towards the center Insert end brackets, holes should be facing outwards Insert T-Slot nuts in places where you will be mounting the panels - so, 2 on the top, 2 on each sides Push the fans into the brackets Bottom beams Insert end bracket - I am using a custom one made for Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT PSU (included in the files), so if you will be using the generic one, it will look slightly different. Frame Screw the back of the case to the mobo tray using 16mm screws Note: You will be screwing into the plastic and essentially threading it, so electric screwdriver with M3 bit is recommended. Don't screw them in fully with the electric screwdriver though or you'll risk stripping the threads. Use a normal M3 driver for that. Stop when you encounter too much resistance. Motherboard I would suggest prepping the motherboard first (cpu, cooler, ram, storage). I've also inserted the pcie riser and power cables cause I found it annoying to do it after the case is put together. Note: The case itself is held together by 4 screws at this point, so I would suggest laying it on the corner of a desk/table so that you do not put unnecessary stress on the plastic parts at this point. Insert the IO shield for the motherboard Put the motherboard on the motherboard posts Put 4 x 16mm screws through the spacers that you have printed Screw the motherboard into the tray PCI-E Riser Bracket Install the PCIE riser bracket with 12mm screws to the back of the mobo tray PSU You can put your PSU in and secure it to the back of the case with #6-32 x 3/8" screws This will allow to put the case vertically and the weight of the mobo tray will rest on the PSU for now Make sure your pcie riser was inserted and routed by this point and it goes above the PSU Bottom Beams You can now slide the bottom beams with brace installed and screw them in from the back of the case with 16mm screws If you are using Enhance ENP-7660L-OVT PSU then you can screw it to the custom brace using #6-32 x 3/8" screws Power button Unscrew the nut from your 16mm power button, put it through the power button plate, screw the nut in Put the cable through the back of the case and screw the plate into the back of the case with 6mm screws GPU Connect the GPU to the riser Put the GPU into the case Line up the holes from the pcie riser to the ones on the pcie riser bracket Screw the pcie riser into the pcie riser bracket using 8mm screws - leave it a bit loose for now, as in don't screw it in fully - this will make it easier to line up everything properly Insert the gpu bracket that "plugs" the hole on the back of the case - you might need to push the gpu upwards a little bit Screw in 12mm screws from the top to secure the gpu - you might need to push the gpu towards the mobo tray to wiggle them in - hold your finger underneath the nuts, they might pop out Front Line it up to the mobo tray Install the front of the frame to the mobo tray using 16mm screws It might help if you temporarily screw in the front to the bottom beams to line it up better. Put the top beams on and route fan cables accordingly Secure all the braces with 12mm (not 16mm!!) screws from the outside. Done, you've built the frame :) Panels Now the only thing remaining is to put on the panels. Mount side, top and bottom panels with 6mm screws Mount the front panel with 16mm screws

description: The Foldable Ramp Recently, I designed and uploaded the Action Monster Truck . And of course, every monster truck needs a ramp for some awesome jumps! The seal process for the 6374 brushless motor is divided into two main parts: the stator and the rotor. For the rotor: I used a small brush to apply a very thin, even layer of epoxy resin. Keeping this layer thin is crucial to prevent throwing off the rotor's dynamic balance. For the stator : I made a custom mold to fit around the entire coil and magnet assembly. First, I sealed the wire connections using 706 RTV silicone glue for flexible strain relief, and then I potted the entire component with epoxy. Just a couple of quick tips: make sure to seal or mask off the bearing area beforehand to prevent any epoxy from seeping in and ruining the bearings. Also, remember to thread screws into the screw holes when sealing the stator; this keeps the epoxy from leaking out through them As for the ESC (Electronic Speed Controller) : Using an ESC with a higher current rating is absolutely fine and actually gives you a nice safety margin. However, keep in mind that a larger ESC might not fit inside the motor housing compartment. If you run into space issues, you can check out my other setup: keep only the motor in the pod , and mount the ESC up on the board/boat inside a dedicated, sealed waterproof box. This not only solves the tight fit but also makes heat dissipation and maintenance a lot easier. model_name: Pull-Up System - for door frames and traveling
tags: pull up|door frame|pull up handles|home gym
description: Why? I'm a huge fan of calisthenics. Over 5 years ago I decided I needed a regimen that could travel with me anywhere, with minimal equipment. Then I would never have an excuse to miss. Pull-ups while traveling can be a challenge. Sometimes there's a playground nearby, sometimes the hotel actually has a pull-up bar. And sometimes there's nothing (work takes me to remote areas). This design uses gravity and your door frame to hold you securely while you do pull-ups. It's meant to replace this travel system: https://a.co/d/0bsIKWrO . I've had issues getting the metal set through TSA (was fine but kept getting flagged), they're heavy, and the price ranges from $35 - $150. My set was around $70. Bambu estimates costs for my printed system to be $16.31 (small boy 70 mm frame) to $22.44 (big boy 90 mm frame). SIZES Frame: Designed for door frames where the wall + casing = 150 mm or around 6 inches thick. For casing of different heights I have two sizes: 70 mm and 90 mm (mine is 70 mm). The 70 mm version can fit everything on a single 256x256 plate, 90 mm will have to be done in pieces. If you're using this for hotel door frames, you never know what size they may have … choose wisely (or print both). Arm: “Small boy” arm is 32 mm deep and 40 mm wide. "Big boy” arm is 32 mm deep and 60 mm wide. Handle: 28 mm diameter (easier to grip but can be more painful). 32 mm diameter (harder to grip but can be less painful). Both are common options with gymnastics rings. SAFETY You are responsible for ensuring your printer, materials, slicer settings, door frame, paracord and use of the provided files and instructions are sufficient to ensure your safety. Testing I weigh 215 lbs. and am wearing a 40 lbs. weighted vest in the torture test you see. Note that I used an earlier and weaker prototype of the “small boy” version . The weakest link is the handle, be sure to properly thread your paracord. I'm confident that if you use the correct filament and settings, and don't put 300+ lbs. on one side, you should be okay. For those who are skeptical or are bigger, use the “big boy” version. Materials and Settings The profile has these by default: Filament: PETG or stronger filament Walls: 7, and 7 shell layers, top and bottom Home Gym I use other 3D printed stuff for some of my home gym equipment and haven't had a problem with safety: https://makerworld.com/collections/29592071 The last photo shows my setup for doing dips at the hotel, using 3D printed rings. ASSEMBLY & USE Arrange the arms so that the “hands” face each other, like a claw. Slide the pin through the large center hole. Thread 1100 lb paracord through one small arm hole, one handle hole, travel under the base of the handle, through the other handle hole, and the other arm hole, then tie with a knot (I used and recommend a square knot). You can thread it so that the handle is perpendicular to the door frame or at a 45 degree angle (see examples in the photos). Open the arms and carefully place over the door frame (if you're concerned about the wall or casing finish, put some electrical tape on the edges that make contact). Grab the handles and slowly lower yourself, shifting your weight to the system (note: the paracord and knot will work out some slack, and you'll shift downward a little).

Airform Lamp v2 This project is a complete rework of my original Airform Lamp . The Airform Lamp was one of my first FDM 3D printing projects . At the time, limited experience led to some design flaws, particularly in the lamp’s shape and printability. This new version was developed to eliminate those issues . Airform Lamp V2 improves upon the original by featuring a reworked internal and outer structure , using only easily printable angles for more consistent and reliable results. The new version also uses the Lamp Kit 001 instead of the previous E14 bulb setup . The new Lamp uses way less Supports and is much more clean and consistent with newly made print profiles (see below for more info) If you prefer the proportions and build of the original Airform Lamp , the project is still available and can be found here, althoug i do not recommend printing the old settings : Airform Lamp Print Settings To achieve the best possible surface quality when printing the lampshade, I added a sacrificial (dummy) object to the build plate. This object helps even out the layer printing time , which significantly reduces visible layer lines on certain areas of the lampshade. Without it, uneven cooling can cause noticeable artifacts. For the smoothest results , the following settings were enabled: Ironing on the top layers Variable layer height Arachne wall mode Reduced wall speed for improved surface quality These adjustments help achieve a clean, consistent finish on the lampshade. If you have any ideas for improvements, let me know in the comments :) Instructions (find the corresponding pictures for the instructions on the right) Step 1: Feed the cable of the LED module through the center hole of the lamp base. Step 2: Place the LED module (with the light facing upward) and the module holder onto the lamp base. Step 3: Rotate the module holder to ensure the LED module is securely fixed in position . Step 4: Insert the bottom cap into the underside of the lamp base. The cap should hold in place by tension . Step 5: Attach the lamp shade to the threaded part of the lamp base. description: Modular Pole Organizer Sistema modulare regolabile progettato per organizzare in modo pratico lo spazio attorno a ombrelloni, pali, aste verticali, supporti da campeggio, strutture da balcone e componenti della barca. La base si apre lateralmente e può quindi essere montata senza dover sfilare il palo dall’alto. Una vite completamente stampata permette di adattare il serraggio a diametri differenti, mentre gli attacchi esterni a coda di rondine consentono di aggiungere, rimuovere e sostituire rapidamente gli accessori. Il progetto comprende due misure di morsetto, entrambe compatibili con gli stessi accessori. Per chiudere e bloccare correttamente la base è necessario stampare almeno un accessorio, da inserire nella coda di rondine posta sul lato apribile del morsetto. Accessori inclusi e accessori compatibili In questa pubblicazione sono inclusi: Gancio piccolo singolo Gancio piccolo triplo Gancio grande singolo Gancio grande triplo Gli altri accessori compatibili con il sistema sono disponibili come pubblicazioni separate, così da permettermi una migliore gestione dei profili di stampa e di eventuali aggiornamenti o modifiche. Tutti gli accessori utilizzano lo stesso attacco a coda di rondine e possono essere montati su entrambe le misure della base. Accessori disponibili in pubblicazioni separate Supporto per Telecamere, Ø50 e Ø70, orizzontale e verticale Porta cellulare con rotazione e inclinazione regolabili Set porta bicchieri singolo, doppio e triplo Portasacchetto spazzatura modulare – Porta Sacchetti con manici Contenitore con coperchio/posacenere e contenitore interno Tavolini/piani d'appoggio rettangolari disponibili in 4 misure e tavolino a forma delfino Tavolini/Piani d'appoggio a tema carte da gioco (cuori, quadri, fiori e picche) Per utilizzare gli accessori pubblicati separatamente è necessario stampare anche una delle due basi del Modular Umbrella & Pole Organizer . Altri accessori sono in fase di sviluppo e verranno pubblicati successivamente mantenendo lo stesso sistema di aggancio. È possibile richiedere la progettazione di accessori specifici: valuterò di volta in volta la fattibilità della richiesta. Caratteristiche principali Base apribile e smontabile Montaggio laterale senza sfilare il palo Serraggio regolabile tramite vite stampata Nessuna vite o componente metallico necessario Due misure disponibili Attacchi modulari a coda di rondine Accessori intercambiabili tra entrambe le basi Possibilità di installare più accessori contemporaneamente Adatto a ombrelloni, pali, aste, ringhiere e supporti verticali Progettato per essere ampliato con nuovi accessori Misure delle basi Base Small Misura Dimensioni Diametro minimo compatibile Ø20 mm Diametro massimo compatibile Ø32 mm Base Large Misura Dimensioni Diametro minimo compatibile Ø30 mm Diametro massimo compatibile Ø50 mm Le due basi utilizzano lo stesso attacco a coda di rondine. Tutti gli accessori possono quindi essere montati indifferentemente sulla versione Small o Large. Sistema modulare Ogni base dispone di più guide a coda di rondine distribuite lungo il corpo. Questo permette di: montare più accessori sulla stessa base; cambiare rapidamente configurazione; orientare gli accessori sui diversi lati del palo; utilizzare la stessa collezione di accessori con entrambe le misure di morsetto. Gli accessori vengono inseriti facendoli scorrere nelle apposite guide. Possibili utilizzi Il sistema è particolarmente adatto per: ombrelloni da spiaggia; ombrelloni da giardino; pali e aste verticali; strutture da campeggio; ringhiere e supporti da balcone; bitte, tientibene e supporti verticali in barca; officine, garage e postazioni di lavoro. L’ombrellone rappresenta l’utilizzo principale, ma il sistema può essere montato su qualsiasi supporto verticale compatibile con il diametro delle basi. Materiale consigliato Per l’utilizzo esterno è consigliato stampare il modello in: PETG; ASA; ABS. Il PLA può essere utilizzato per prove o impieghi interni, ma non è consigliato lasciarlo a lungo sotto il sole o in ambienti molto caldi. Impostazioni di stampa consigliate Altezza layer: 0,20 mm Pareti: almeno 4 Riempimento: 30–40% Supporti: da valutare in base all’orientamento dei singoli componenti Materiale consigliato: PETG Preparazione e montaggio Dopo la stampa, togliere i supporti e aprire delicatamente le due metà del morsetto utilizzando entrambe le mani, fino a sganciare la cerniera apribile. Prima del montaggio definitivo, provare a inserire la punta della vite nell’apposita sede presente sulla parte mobile del morsetto. Una volta inserita, ruotare la vite per alcuni giri, in modo da verificare che l’accoppiamento sia libero e corretto, quindi sfilarla nuovamente. Con il morsetto aperto, avvitare la vite nel corpo principale fino a portarla completamente in avanti. Inserire la parte mobile del morsetto nell’incavo presente sulla punta della vite, verificando che sia correttamente centrata rispetto al corpo principale. Svitare lentamente la vite per richiamare indietro la parte mobile, controllando che questa si inserisca correttamente nelle guide centrali e possa scorrere senza impuntamenti. Posizionare la base attorno al palo o al supporto verticale. Richiudere il morsetto. Inserire almeno un accessorio nella coda di rondine situata sul lato apribile, in modo da bloccare correttamente la base. Stringere la vite stampata fino a ottenere un fissaggio stabile. Inserire gli altri accessori desiderati nelle restanti guide a coda di rondine. Non è necessario serrare eccessivamente la vite. È sufficiente eliminare il gioco e verificare che la base non possa ruotare sul palo. Avvertenze Verificare sempre la stabilità del morsetto prima di appoggiare telefoni, bicchieri o altri oggetti. Non utilizzare il sistema per sostenere carichi pesanti. La compatibilità effettiva può variare in base alla forma e alla superficie del palo. Durante il primo montaggio, muovere delicatamente la parte mobile e verificare che sia correttamente inserita nelle guide prima di stringere la vite. Compatibilità Gli accessori inclusi utilizzano tutti lo stesso profilo a coda di rondine e sono compatibili con entrambe le basi: Small: Ø20–32 mm Large: Ø30–50 mm

description: Ce modèle 3D permet de fabriquer un support de bouteilles pour ventilateur , conçu pour créer un rafraîchisseur d'air artisanal (ou climatiseur d'appoint) très simple et économique. Comment ça marche ? Le principe : Vous remplissez deux bouteilles de soda (de 500 ml) avec de l'air ou de l'eau additionnée de sel (pour que la glace tienne plus longtemps), puis vous les mettez au congélateur. L'installation : Une fois imprimés, les supports s'emboîtent et s'accrochent directement sur la grille de votre ventilateur. Il suffit d'y glisser les bouteilles congelées : l'air propulsé par les pales se refroidit instantanément au contact de la glace. Détails et astuces de conception Impression facile : Le design est pensé pour s'imprimer sans aucun support. Les pièces se clipsent simplement entre elles. Fixation modulable : Le créateur a intégré des fentes sur le modèle. Si l'accroche d'origine ne suffit pas ou si vous voulez bloquer le système, vous pouvez utiliser des serre-câbles ( zip ties ) pour le fixer solidement à la grille. Astuce pratique : N'oubliez pas de placer une petite serviette ou un récipient sous le ventilateur pour récupérer l'eau de condensation qui va perler le long des bouteilles.

description: # ⚙️ Ultimate Parametric Gear Generator (Involute & Double/Step Gears) This is a highly precise, fully parametric **Spur Gear and Double/Step Gear Generator** designed specifically for 3D printing and mechanical engineering. Using the **MakerWorld Customizer**, you can create custom gears directly in your browser without any CAD knowledge! It uses true mathematical **involute tooth geometry**, ensuring smooth rotation, low friction, and maximum durability for your custom gearboxes, robotics, or RC projects. --- ### 🚀 Key Features * **True Involute Teeth:** Mathematically correct tooth profiles that roll smoothly without jamming. * **Double / Step Gear Option:** Easily stack two custom gears on a single shaft. Perfect for compound gear trains and high-reduction gearboxes! * **D-Cut / D-Shaft Support:** Toggle a flat side (D-cut) inside the bore to perfectly fit NEMA stepper motors or RC motors. * **Fully Parametric:** Adjust Module (size), Tooth Count, Gear Thickness, and Shaft Diameter with simple sliders. * **No External Libraries:** 100% standalone OpenSCAD script, perfectly compatible with the MakerWorld cloud compiler. --- ### 🔧 How to Customize Your Gear 1. Click on the **Open in Customizer** button on MakerWorld. 2. **Gear 1 (Base):** Set your desired tooth count, thickness, and Module (defines tooth size, standard is 2.0). 3. **Gear 2 (Step Gear):** Check `z2_aktiv` to add a secondary gear on top, or uncheck it for a standard single gear. 4. **Bore & Axis:** Set your shaft diameter. If you use a D-shaft motor, check `d_cut_aktiv` and define the flat width. 5. Click **Generate** and download your 3D-printable `.STL` file! --- ### 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings * **Material:** PETG, ABS, ASA, or Nylon for functional parts. PLA is fine for prototyping or low-load toys. * **Wall Loops:** 4 to 6 walls (perimeters) for maximum tooth strength. * **Infill:** 40% - 100% (Gyroid recommended). * **Top/Bottom Layers:** 5 layers. * **Cooling:** Keep it balanced to ensure great layer adhesion on the teeth.

SkyOrb — Live Flight Radar & Clock (ESP32) Watch real aircraft fly overhead in real time, right on your desk. SkyOrb is a desk gadget built around an ESP32 and two round 1.28" displays. One screen is a live flight radar with an animated sweep that makes nearby aircraft glow as it passes over them; the second screen is a clean digital clock with the day and date. This model is the 3D-printed enclosure that holds it all together — and the firmware is free and flashes straight from your web browser, no coding required. ✨ What it does Live flight tracking — shows real aircraft around your location using free ADS-B data (no account, no API key, no subscription). Animated radar sweep — planes light up as the sweep passes, just like a real radar scope. Callsigns and altitudes show right on the display. Airport markers — nearby airports appear on the radar; the portal can auto-find commercial airports near you. Digital clock — the second round display shows the time, day, and date. It auto-detects your time zone (with daylight saving) once you set your location, and supports both 12-hour and 24-hour formats. Set up from your phone — a built-in web page lets you set your location, search radius, airports, clock format, and even the portal's accent color. No computer needed after flashing. Tap to track — tap any flight in the web portal to open it on FlightRadar24. 🛠️ What you need (electronics) These are inexpensive, widely available parts: ESP32 dev board (30-pin ESP-WROOM-32) Two GC9A01 round 1.28" displays (240×240 SPI, 7-pin) — one for the radar, one for the clock 30-pin ESP32 GPIO breakout board with screw terminals — lets you wire everything up with no soldering A USB cable for power (Exact links to the parts I used are in the firmware project — see the link at the bottom.) 🖨️ About this print This model is the SkyOrb enclosure. It's designed to hold the ESP32, the breakout board, and both round displays in a clean desk-friendly housing. Print settings (suggested): Material: PLA Layer height: 0.2 mm Infill: 15–20% Supports: No Supports Needed No brim needed Print orientation and any part-specific notes are shown in the preview images. The display bezels are sized for standard GC9A01 round modules. ⚡ Flashing the firmware (no coding!) The firmware installs straight from your web browser using ESP Web Tools — there's nothing to download or compile. Wire up the two displays to the ESP32 using the breakout board (wiring diagram is included on the install page). Open the SkyOrb installer page in Chrome or Edge on a computer, plug in your ESP32, and click Install . After flashing, connect your phone to the SKYORB-Setup WiFi hotspot, pick your home network, and enter your password. Switch your phone back to your home WiFi, then open skyorb.local in a browser to set your location. Done — planes appear within seconds. The radar display even shows the setup address on screen at startup, so you never need a serial monitor or any developer tools. 💡 Why I built it I wanted something that made the invisible traffic in the sky above me feel real and tangible — a little window into what's flying overhead at any moment. SkyOrb turns live flight data into a calm, glanceable desk object, and pairing it with a clock made it something I actually keep next to my monitor all day. The whole thing is open and free so anyone can build their own. 📦 What's included 3D-printable enclosure files (this model) Link to the free firmware + browser-based installer Full wiring guide and step-by-step setup instructions 🔗 Firmware & full build guide The firmware, browser installer, wiring tables, and parts list are all free and open source here: https://gulfcoastmaker.github.io/SkyOrb/ Licensed under the MIT License — free to build, modify, and share. Flight data by airplanes.live · Airport & address lookup by OpenStreetMap · Browser flashing by ESP Web Tools. Built it? I'd love to see your SkyOrb — post a Make and share a photo!

description: Da ich für mein Dachfenster keine passende Lösung gefunden habe, habe ich diesen Adapter selbst konstruiert. Der Adapter ermöglicht es, den Abluftschlauch einer mobilen Klimaanlage durch ein Dachfenster zu führen, während das Fenster nahezu vollständig geschlossen bleiben kann. Dadurch wird der Luftaustausch mit der warmen Außenluft reduziert und die Kühlleistung verbessert. Eigenschaften Passend für 125 mm, 130 mm und 150 mm Abluftschläuche Integrierte Aussparung für den Fenstergriff Große Auslassfläche für einen möglichst geringen Strömungswiderstand Mehrteilige Bauweise für eine einfache Herstellung auf handelsüblichen 3D-Druckern Für verschiedene Schlauchdurchmesser stehen passende Anschlussstücke zur Verfügung Version 2 Ich habe bereits eine V2 des Modells erstellt. Hier wurden zusätzlich 6 Verstärkungsrippen ergänzt, die nach dem Druck eingeklebt werden. Hintergrund ist, dass der Adapter während eines längeren Betriebs der Klimaanlage durch die warme Abluft leicht erwärmt wird. Je nach Material kann sich der Auslassbereich mit der Zeit minimal verformen. Die Verstärkungsrippen erhöhen die Stabilität deutlich und halten den Auslass dauerhaft in Form. Zusammenbau Der Adapter besteht aus: 2 Auslassteilen 1 Schlauchadapter 6 Verstärkungsrippen (V2) Alle Teile habe ich mit einem hochwertigen Sekundenkleber verklebt. Durch die mehrteilige Bauweise lassen sich sämtliche Komponenten auch auf Druckern mit normaler Baugröße problemlos herstellen. Druckempfehlung Bei mir wurde das Modell erfolgreich mit Bambu PETG HF und dem Standard-Bambu-Profil gedruckt. Ein Druck mit normalem PETG hat ebenfalls gut funktioniert. Da es sich jedoch um einen langen Druck handelt und PETG zu leichter Tropfenbildung neigt, verwende ich zusätzlich einen selbst eingebauten Nozzle-Cleaning-G-Code , der die Düse regelmäßig reinigt. Dadurch konnte ich die Druckqualität nochmals verbessern. Natürlich kann der Adapter auch aus anderen temperaturbeständigen Materialien gedruckt werden. Hinweise Da Dachfenster und mobile Klimaanlagen sehr unterschiedlich sind, kann ich keine universelle Passgenauigkeit garantieren. Bitte prüft vor dem Druck die angegebenen Maße und wählt den passenden Schlauchdurchmesser (125 mm, 130 mm oder 150 mm). Dieses Modell wurde ursprünglich für meinen eigenen Anwendungsfall entwickelt und anschließend so aufbereitet, dass möglichst viele Nutzer davon profitieren können. Feedback Ich freue mich über jedes Feedback! Solltet ihr Verbesserungsvorschläge, Ideen oder Anpassungswünsche haben, schreibt diese gerne in die Kommentare. Ich bin jederzeit offen für konstruktive Kritik und werde sinnvolle Verbesserungen gerne in zukünftige Versionen einfließen lassen. Viel Spaß beim Drucken – und ich hoffe, der Adapter hilft euch dabei, auch an heißen Sommertagen einen kühlen Kopf zu bewahren! 😊

description: Description This is my replica of the famous Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm , designed and modeled directly from a precise 3D scan of an original 4-gram Rapala Jointed lure. Known for its broken-back design and unmistakable, hyper-active swimming action, the Jointed Floating is a legendary choice when fish are finicky or biting short. This 3D-printed version brings that exact lively, snake-like presentation directly to your tackle box, making it perfect for targeting perch, trout, pike, and zander. A massive amount of engineering and testing went into recreating the physics of a two-part jointed balsa lure in 3D-printed plastic. Because the action depends entirely on the freedom of movement between the two sections, the internal balance has been meticulously tuned to achieve the exact same characteristic swimming motion as the original classic. Design Notes 3D Scanned Precision: Modeled directly from a physical 3D scan of a real Rapala Jointed Floating 7 cm to ensure perfect proportions and flawless hydrodynamics. True-to-Original Weight: Engineered to match the compact 4-gram profile of the original, providing excellent buoyancy and a highly responsive action on light tackle gear. Finetuned Slicer Modifiers: The lively and chaotic swimming action of this lure relies heavily on custom internal weight distribution. I have integrated multiple precise slicer modifiers inside the model to perfect the center of mass for both sections. It is crucial that you do not change these settings , as they have been heavily tested and tuned across numerous prototypes. Crucial Support-Free Lip Design: The diving lip is oriented to print completely flat on its own separate plate. To handle the steep overhangs successfully without supports, it is highly recommended to print the lip at a 0.08 mm layer height . Printing it at a standard 0.2 mm layer height will cause print flaws on the curved edges. Strength & Testing 6.8 kg+ Load Capacity: Despite the jointed design, this lure uses the exact same robust internal hardware connection system as my other models. It has been thoroughly tested to lift at least 6.8 kg with absolutely no issues. The internal structure is rock-solid and fully prepared to handle heavy, hard-fighting predators. Strength & Finishing (Crucial Step) Applying a clear coat is highly recommended to ensure the model is 100% waterproof and to add structural strength. ⚠️ IMPORTANT FINISHING NOTE: Unlike my other models, do not dip this lure in your clear coat! Instead, I highly recommend applying your UV resin or epoxy clear coat with a brush . It is extremely important that you keep the central joint connection completely clean. If resin or epoxy gets inside the "link" where the two screw eyes connect, it will lock up the joint and ruin the lure's unique swimming action. Assembly The lure consists of three printed parts: the front body, the rear tail section, and the separate diving lip. Prep the Parts: Clean up any print lines or imperfections. Secure the diving lip into the front body slot using a strong 5-minute epoxy or superglue. Assemble the Joint (The Link): To create the jointed action, take two stainless steel screw eyes. Gently bend one of the eyelets slightly open with a pair of pliers, loop the second screw eye into it, and bend it completely shut again. Install the Joint: Screw the ends of this connected pair into the pre-modeled holes linking the front body and tail section together. Make sure the joint moves freely and smoothly. Install Remaining Hardware: Install the remaining 3 screw eyes (nose, front belly, and tail) into their pilot holes. (Tip: Use my 1mm Handdrill Handle tool from my profile to pre-drill the holes, or gently heat the screw eyes with a lighter before screwing them in for maximum strength). Rig the Hooks: Attach your split rings and size #8 treble hooks to the designated belly and tail screw eyes. Hardware Requirements To fully assemble the lure, you will need the following hardware: 5x Screw Eyes: Stainless steel. 1.3 mm thread thickness, 12 mm full length, 5 mm outer eye diameter, 8 mm shaft length. (Can be bought very cheaply on sites like Temu or AliExpress). 2x Split Rings: Size 5 mm. 2x Treble Hooks: Size #8. Important Print Profile Notice To make printing as easy as possible, the included print profile is split onto two plates : Plate 1: Contains the main body parts set to a standard 0.2 mm layer height . Plate 2: Contains the diving lip set to the required 0.08 mm layer height to handle the steep overhangs perfectly. (Note: If your printplate is big enough, you can easily combine these onto a single plate and utilize "Print by Object" to print both parts in a single run). Tight lines!!

Here's my take on a guitar → hurdy gurdy style conversion kit. This is a v1.0 release, so I would love to hear your feedback on improvements. You will need to source o-rings and dark rosin to use this as intended. I highly suggest checking out assembly instructions to make things clear on how to properly mount it without damaging anything on your guitar. How it works: It' fastened to the bottom and top string of your guitar and plays on the four middle strings using two o-rings coated with rosin. This creates friction which then vibrate the strings when cranking the wheel. Tips: Using rosin on the o-rings is required, it won't work well without it. Check out part list for more details. It's easier to tune the strings after you've installed the o-rings and before you assemble the Gurdy Wheel. DADA tuning works great, as well as GDAE. Extras: If your guitar has a pick guard, you can print out the + 2mm height foot to offset the height difference. If you need more tension on the o-rings you can use two +2 mm feet instead of the default ones. To apply rosin to the o-rings, use sandpaper or a knife to break up the rosin and slide the o-rings gently across the surface to coat them. Print out TPU feet if you are having issues with movement of the whole assembly when cranking. Also protects your guitar body. O-rings can possibly be printed and are provided with the print profile, but would need to be as soft as possible, as industry o-rings tend to be around 60-70A on the shore hardness scale. I've tried with 95A and that did not work. You can print the bearings and screw if you don't have the hardware available, but I highly recommend steel bearings and bolt for less play between the parts. Larger handle is provided in the print profile if you feel the small one does not suit you. Disclaimer: May or may not work on your exact guitar model. I've tested it on three different guitars and they all worked, but with different neck widths it's hard to say how it will perform on your particular model. I'm in no way responsible for any damage that may occur to your guitar during installation.

About the model This is a model of the P-51 Mustang, a World War II era escort fighter. I specifically modelled this after the “D” variant which featured a bubble canopy and was the most produced variant of the war. I included liveries of the iconic Red Tail Mustangs, and the D-Day invasion stripes, however these can be easily customized to your liking. Please ensure your printer is sufficiently maintained and proper material is used to ensure the best print possible. Glue is optional, both models from the cover photo were assembled without it. However, a small hobby knife or similar should be used during assembly. Additionally, please ensure that all support material is removed from the aircraft during assembly as excess material could decrease the effectiveness of joints. If you have any inquiries, feel free to leave a comment or DM me on makerworld. Happy Printing! Refer to the below image for assistance with assembly. NOTE: The left wing is omitted from the image for sake of simplicity, the assembly process is the same as the process for the right wing. NOTE 2: When testing, i found the holes on the horizontal stabilizers for the connecting rod can sometimes shrink and make it difficult to insert the connector without breaking it. If you run into this issue, take your hobby knife, put the point into the hole and carefully rotate it to expand the hole without breaking the sides of it. This should help significantly.

description: This is a lightweight (48 g), durable, and modular Front Fork Cargo Cage designed for bikepacking, commuting, and touring. Supports: Minimal supports required depending on your printer's bridging capability (mostly for the AirTag cap threads or recessed bolt holes). Hardware Required (BOM) Fork Mounting: 2x or 3x M5 Bolts (standard water bottle cage bolts, ~64 mm distance). Straps: Standard bikepacking straps (e.g., Voile straps) or heavy-duty hook-and-loop velcro straps. I tested it with PETG CF, all accessories mount holds well by friction. Doppel TinyWhoop Case Übersicht Da es häufiger Anfragen gab, ob ich ein Case entwickeln kann, welches zwei TinyWhoops gleichzeitig unterbringen kann, habe ich dieses Doppel TinyWhoop Case entworfen. Das Case ist die Weiterentwicklung meines bekannten BetaFPV-Cases für einen Copter und bietet nun Platz für bis zu zwei TinyWhoops, zahlreiche Akkus, ein 1S-Ladegerät sowie Ersatzteile und Werkzeug. Features Platz für 2 TinyWhoops In der Standardausführung können folgende Modelle direkt verwendet werden: 2 × BetaFPV Meteor 75 Pro Kompatible Copter Mit optionalen Einsätzen BetaFPV Air65 (mit Air65-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air65 II (mit Air65 II-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air75 (mit Air75-Einsatz) BetaFPV Air75 II (mit Air75 II-Einsatz) BetaFPV Meteor 65 Pro (mit Meteor 65 Pro-Einsatz) Mobula 6 (mit Air65-Einsatz) Ohne zusätzlichen Einsatz HDZero M8 Freestyle Für weitere Modelle können zukünftig zusätzliche Einsätze veröffentlicht werden. Ladegerät-Kompatibilität Im Case ist Platz für das beliebte WhoopStor 3 1S Ladegerät . Zusätzlich ist ein optionaler Einsatz erhältlich, mit dem auch das BetaFPV Hexa 1S Ladegerät sicher im Case untergebracht werden kann. Akku-Aufbewahrung Im Deckel des Cases können bis zu 29 Stück 1S LiPos sicher verstaut werden. Wichtiger Hinweis: Die Halteklammern für die Akkus müssen gegebenenfalls mit etwas Sekundenkleber fixiert werden, damit sie dauerhaft sicher sitzen und sich nicht verschieben. Parts- & Tool-Fach Das Case verfügt über eine integrierte Ablage für: Ersatzteile Werkzeug Propeller Schrauben weiteres Zubehör Die Ablage wird durch ein verschiebbares Rollo verschlossen und schützt den Inhalt während des Transports. Verbesserte Verschlüsse Da das Doppel-Case größer als das ursprüngliche Einzel-Case ist, wurde es mit zwei Verschlüssen ausgestattet. Dadurch wird gewährleistet, dass das Case auch bei voller Beladung sicher verschlossen bleibt. Wichtiger Hinweis zur finalen Version Die auf den Bildern gezeigte Version ist gespiegelt. Nach dem ersten Testdruck ist mir aufgefallen, dass das Ladegerät in der ursprünglichen Anordnung auf dem Kopf stehen würde. Deshalb wurden die Positionen des Ladegeräts und der Tool-Ablage in der finalen Version miteinander getauscht. Die veröffentlichten Dateien enthalten bereits diese überarbeitete Version. Benötigte Hardware Für den Zusammenbau werden zusätzlich folgende Schrauben benötigt: Scharniere 3 × M3x20 mm Schrauben Verschlüsse 4 × M3x30 mm Schrauben Für jeden Verschluss werden zwei Schrauben benötigt. Montage der Scharniere Deckel und Unterteil so ausrichten, dass die Scharnierhälften ineinandergreifen. Die Scharnierhälften zusammenschieben. Anschließend jeweils eine M3x20 mm Schraube durch das Scharnier führen. Die Schraube dient dabei als Achse und ermöglicht die Drehbewegung des Deckels. Montage der Verschlüsse Die beiden Verschlussklemmen mit insgesamt vier M3x30 mm Schrauben montieren. Anschließend prüfen, ob die Verschlüsse leichtgängig arbeiten und das Case sicher schließen. Montage der Tool-Ablage Schritt 1 Zunächst die linke und rechte Seitenwand mit dem Boden zusammenstecken. Gegebenenfalls muss der Boden leicht nachbearbeitet werden, damit er mit etwas Druck in die beiden Seitenwände passt. Schritt 2 Die vormontierte Baugruppe in die dafür vorgesehene Aussparung im Case einschieben. Dabei zunächst etwa 1 cm vor der endgültigen Position stoppen. Schritt 3 Nun das Rollo von der Frontseite aus in die Führungsschienen einschieben. Tipp: Ein kleiner Tropfen Öl in den Führungen erleichtert das Einschieben und verbessert die Leichtgängigkeit des Rollos. Schritt 4 Sobald das Rollo vollständig eingeschoben wurde, kann die komplette Baugruppe bis zur Endposition in das Case geschoben werden. Schritt 5 Falls der Rahmen etwas locker sitzt, kann dieser mit einem kleinen Tropfen Sekundenkleber fixiert werden. Viel Spaß mit dem Doppel TinyWhoop Case! Dieses Case wurde speziell für TinyWhoop-Piloten entwickelt, die mehrere Copter, Akkus, Ladegerät, Ersatzteile und Werkzeug kompakt und sicher transportieren möchten.

description: Powered Pottery Handle and Coil Extruder 2.0 New Design is all 3D printed to use with Powered Caulk Gun This is a powered pottery extruder. It has a 47mm (1.85 in) inside diameter. Can support extruding shapes of about 1.5". There are three separate Print Profiles for all the pieces. The extruder main body is printed from Transparent PETG, the Accessories for the plunger and adapter to the caulk gun, and a wide variety of handle and coil dies printed in PLA. IMPORTANT - The Extruder Body should be printed so it has solid walls, the profile is setup to print very slow to allow better transparency and better layer adhesion. If you change print settings be careful, the powered caulk gun can put enough force to separate the layer lines on the printed body. The setting for transparent PETG were tested with Sunlu Clear PETG and held up to the forces. Other plastics and settings may need to be experimented with. With a 0.4mm nozzle the body takes a bit of time to print. Using a 0.6mm nozzle can speed this up. SEE NOTE BELOW ON USING VARIABLE LAYER HEIGHT FOR THREADS. THE DEFAULT LAYER HEIGHT IS 0.24mm AND THE THREADS ARE AT 0.08MM. IF YOU CHANGE NOZZLES THIS WILL NEED TO BE RESET. Assembly Instructions Assembly is pretty easy, print the extruder body and cap in the first profile and the p;unger and adapter in the second profile. Print one or more of the extruder dies in the third profile 1) The plunger adaptor replaces the black plastic part on the caulk gun and the plunger screws into the adapter. 2) Then add one of the extruder dies onto the extruder body and screw on the top fitting. 3) Load clay, it takes about 700g of clay. Don't overfill need to leave about 1.5" of free space to allow room to screw the extruder to the caulk gun. A plunger handle is included to help pack down the clay. 4) Then attach the extruder body to the caulk gun. Use caution when running, the extruder body should be strong enough but best to stop the plunger before it goes all the way to the end. Addition Parts Needed Extruder Gun - Ryobi Caulk Gun - https://www.ryobitools.com/products/33287195169 Notes: Can usually find it around $50 on sale without battery, if you already have Ryobi one tools. Full kit is usually $130.00-$200.00 Other options may work, the harbor freight version looks like its the same interface for the caulk tube ($39 without battery). I have not tested to see if this works: https://www.harborfreight.com/20v-caulk-and-adhesive-gun-tool-only-59793.html European versions use a different tube style so not sure they work. Tested by user @wbarringer42 with the Dewalt DCE560 as well as the Ryobi. There are now over 16 coil and handle dies! NOTE: IF YOU CHANGE NOZZLE (or possibly other changes), THE ADJUSTABLE LAYER HEIGHT FOR THE THREADS WILL NOT BE SET. ITS ONLY SET FOR THE 0.4MM NOZZLE. For the threads make sure the layer height is at 0.08mm not the default 0.24mm or the threads will not be as good. The threads on the original 3mf file have 0.08 layer height using the Variable Layer Height option for both the top and bottom threads. Same for the matting cap. Also with the PETG print slow to get good layer adhesion. At 0.24 layer height the threads are not great and maybe hard to get started. Also print the PETG slow both for the translucent to be more clear (its never clear without alot of post processing) and for strength. description: Motivation If you're curious about the motivation behind 3D-printed FPV drone frames, check out the [BETA] ManaFly 3" Generative FPV Drone Frame project: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2000546-beta-manafly-3-generative-fpv-drone-frame?from=search#profileId-2154440 That page goes into much more detail on the motivation, use cases, crash resistance, frame-swapping, and the overall advantages of a 3D-printed frame over a traditional carbon fiber one. This project follows the same idea and versatility, scaled up to fit most common components used on 7-inch drones. Compatibility Flight Controller - 20 x 20 mm FPV stack - 30.5 x 30.5 mm FPV stack VTX - 20x20 mm (M2) — small VTX mounts, fits most modern analog and compact digital systems - 25.5x25.5 mm (M2) — standard mount for DJI digital VTX units (Air Unit / O3 / O4) - 30x30 mm (M3) — larger mounts for older or high-power VTX units with better heat handling Camera - Analog Mini / Micro / Nano - A custom mount can be made for any camera smaller than 21 mm Prop Size - 7-inch props (standard) Filament I used ABS for its stiffness, but the frame can also be printed in PETG or PA6-CF. A detailed breakdown of each filament option, along with a comparison against a carbon fiber frame, is available on the [BETA] ManaFly 3" Generative FPV Drone Frame project page linked above. IMPORTANT — Print Settings, Please Read Filament: ABS, PETG Infill: 50% Gyroid (50-70% range recommended) Wall loops: 8 Filament use: ~170 g Print orientation: Flat / horizontal, for maximum strength Support type: Automatic tree supports Infill — 50% Gyroid: Going higher 70%+ has only a low effect on strength. Wall loops — 8: this setting has a major effect on final mass while greatly increasing rigidity. For reference, with the same 50% gyroid infill, 2 wall loops give a mass of ~121 g, while 8 wall loops give ~157 g. Bed adhesion matters. Apply a bed adhesive before printing, and set the bed temperature to 110°C (the recommended setting for ABS) — otherwise the frame risks delaminating from the bed mid-print. Printer configuration — required for this frame's size: Because of this frame's large footprint (251 x 251 mm), some default printer settings need to be changed before slicing, or the print head can physically collide with the part and damage the printer: 1. Remove the bed exclusion zone from your printer configuration, so the part fits within the build area. 2. On a Bambu Lab P1S, increase the printable height from 250 mm to 256 mm. 3. Bend the Filament Cutter Lever Actuator out of the way . Once the exclusion zone is removed, the print head can collide with this component during printing. After the Modular Bricks Remote, I’ve been wanting to design other CyberBrick hardware into modular bricks. I believed a complete vehicle project would make this concept far more engaging, so lots of development work was required beyond designing basic modular bricks. The project is now finished — the Modular Bricks Kart, available in the Mecanum Wheel Version. Mecanum wheel vehicles are incredibly fun. They can drive like ordinary cars and also perform omnidirectional lateral sliding. Modular Bricks feature easy assembly and disassembly, allowing quick swapping between different toy models. Even children can assemble them with little difficulty. Once you have the full set of basic modular bricks, assembling any subsequent model becomes quick and hassle-free. This kart adopts exactly this design. Except for the wheels, the entire chassis and body require no screws or adhesive — assembly is just like stacking building blocks. It’s compatible with the official standard remote. If you are interested, I recommend trying my previously released Modular Bricks Remote, which lets you own a full set of modular brick toys. Some future models will rely on the unique advantages of the modular brick system to deliver functions unavailable with standard remote controllers. The remote links are in the Assembly Guild. Controlling a Mecanum wheel vehicle normally requires four motors, yet the CyberBrick receiver only supports two. Fortunately, it comes with four servo ports, so I opted to use four servos for power. This setup allows full vehicle functionality with a single receiver unit, while servos also deliver superior torque output. · Download the assembly guide for detailed build instructions, covering three manuals: Basic Modular Bricks, Chassis and Body, Mecanum Wheels. · The printing profiles are split into three sets matching the assembly guides; all three must be printed. description: Filtro Roller Automatico de 20cm para Sump – Agua Cristalina y Saludable (Diseño DIY) Mantener un agua biológicamente sana y visualmente cristalina es uno de los mayores desafíos en el acuarismo marino. Este diseño modular impreso en 3D consiste en un Filtro Roller de 20 cm de ancho de rodillo , desarrollado específicamente para optimizar la filtración mecánica de tu sistema sin comprometer espacio ni presupuesto. A diferencia de los calcetines de filtración tradicionales que se saturan rápidamente y requieren un lavado constante, este sistema permite renovar el tejido filtrante de manera eficiente antes de que la materia orgánica comience a descomponerse en el agua. El proyecto está pensado con un enfoque puramente DIY (Hazlo Tú Mismo) : la descarga incluye el núcleo del rodillo de 20cm y los soportes principales optimizados mecánicamente para que cada usuario pueda diseñar, adaptar o fabricar su propia bandeja de alojamiento personalizada dentro del sump, ajustándose milimétricamente a las divisiones y flujos específicos de su acuario. 🛠️ Piezas Requeridas Para llevar a cabo el montaje completo de este sistema de filtración, necesitarás preparar tanto los componentes impresos como algunos elementos de ferretería comunes: Componentes Impresos en 3D: Rodillo Principal (20cm): Estructura central optimizada (disponible en una o varias piezas según el tamaño de tu impresora). Soportes Laterales y Ejes: Piezas de sujeción para fijar el conjunto sobre tu bandeja o sump. Controlador de Avance : Diseño ergonómico para el enrollado automatico del fieltro. Tornillería plástica (M6 x10mm): Se recomienda encarecidamente utilizar tornillos de nylon para evitar cualquier tipo de corrosión o contaminación con el agua salada. Tubo de PVC / Varilla acrílica (Opcional): Puede ser utilizado como eje central de soporte si deseas darle una rigidez extrema al conjunto. 💡 Parámetros de Impresión Recomendados: Material: PETG (Evitar por completo el PLA debido a la degradación por humedad constante y exposición al agua salada). Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 4-part mould (3 sides and a small insert for the base) to cast round tumblers/mugs with an angular design. You need to cast plaster in the larger mould three times for the sides, for every one cast of the small insert. This gives a complete plaster mould. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, with most casting slips this should give a final tumbler size of 6.5cm diameter and 7cm height, or a capacity of around 150ml. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 350ml of plaster for the side pieces and around 75ml for the base insert, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. This uses the updated 3 part mould design, which is compatible with other updated 3 part moulds but not the original ornament moulds. This new design has slots added to the back to allow the mould to bend slightly when releasing the plaster, making the process much easier.

Oscillating Desktop Fan – 3D Printable Design This project is a compact oscillating desktop fan designed for 3D printing. It uses two 12V fans, adjustable fan speed control, and an automatic left-to-right oscillation mechanism. The vertical angle of the fan can be adjusted manually. The airflow speed can be controlled using the knob located on the side of the body. The oscillation mechanism is powered by a small N20 geared motor, providing a slow and smooth left-to-right movement. Features Automatic left-to-right oscillation Adjustable fan speed Manually adjustable vertical angle Compact desktop design Two 12V fans 3D printable body and mechanical parts Easy access to the controls and electronic components Suitable for desks, workshops, and hobby rooms Electronic Components 2 × 12V fans N20 6V 30 RPM geared motor DC-DC step-down converter PWM fan speed controller 12V power supply On/off switches Wires, screws, and basic electronic components I used an N20 6V 30 RPM geared motor for the oscillation mechanism. The motor is powered at approximately 3V through a DC-DC step-down converter. In my setup, 3V provides a suitable and balanced oscillation speed. The motor can also be operated at 3V, 3.5V, or 4V depending on the desired movement speed. Increasing the voltage will increase the oscillation speed. You can also use an N20 10 RPM or 15 RPM geared motor if one is available. Since lower-RPM motors may behave differently depending on the applied voltage, I recommend testing the motor speed before completing the final assembly. Electrical Wiring I recommend connecting the 12V power input to the switches first, and then distributing power from the outputs of the switches to the relevant components. With this wiring method, no power will be supplied to the fans, speed controller, step-down converter, or other electronic components when the switches are turned off. In my video, I distributed the power before the switches. However, for anyone building the project, placing the switches between the 12V input and the electronic components is the better wiring method. The general connection order should be: 12V power input → Switches → Related circuits and components This prevents unnecessary power consumption and ensures that the connected circuits are not continuously powered when the switches are off. Printing Notes I divided the project into a total of six build plates. The plates are named according to the type of print surface that should be used. In the project files: Plates named Smooth Plate should be printed on a smooth print surface. Plates named Textured Plate should be printed on a textured print surface. It is especially important to print certain sliding, rotating, or contact parts on a Smooth Plate. These parts require smooth contact surfaces for the oscillation mechanism to operate correctly. If the contact surfaces are too rough, the additional friction may cause: Excessive load on the N20 motor Irregular oscillation movement The mechanism to jam The motor to become unable to move the mechanism For this reason, please check the build plate names carefully before printing and use the specified print surface. Most parts can be printed using PLA or PETG. PETG is recommended for parts located close to the motor or electronic components, especially if the fan will be operated for extended periods. I recommend keeping the prepared print orientations and plate layouts where possible. However, always check support requirements and inspect the slicer preview before starting the print. Assembly and Mechanism Notes Depending on your printer calibration and dimensional tolerances, some parts may require light sanding or minor adjustment. All moving, rotating, and contacting areas of the oscillation mechanism should be lightly lubricated using a plastic-compatible lubricant. Pay particular attention to: Rotating connection points Shaft and bearing areas Plastic surfaces that slide against each other Moving joints in the oscillation mechanism Only apply enough lubricant to create a thin layer on the contact surfaces. Excessive lubrication is not necessary. Make sure that the lubricant is safe for plastic parts. After completing the assembly, check the following: The oscillation mechanism should move freely when operated by hand Moving parts should not rub against the housing Fan wires should not restrict the oscillation movement Wires should not enter or become trapped inside moving parts The motor should be mounted securely Screws in moving joints should not be overtightened Electrical connections should be properly insulated The mechanism should not jam at the left or right movement limits Before powering the motor, move the mechanism slowly by hand and check for excessive friction, resistance, or jamming. If the mechanism does not move freely by hand, do not operate it with the motor. First locate the source of the friction or obstruction. Lightly sand the contact surfaces if necessary and apply lubricant again. Important This project requires basic knowledge of electronics, soldering, and mechanical assembly. Before connecting the power supply, always check the voltage, polarity, and all electrical connections. During the first test, operate the oscillation motor at a low voltage and make sure that the mechanism moves freely. Do not leave the device unattended during the initial tests. Feel free to share your prints, improvements, and modifications on MakerWorld. I would be happy to see your version of the fan.
