Supporto telefono per bicicletta e moto - versione 2.0 Questa è una nuova versione del supporto telefono che ho progettato qualche mese fa ( https://makerworld.com/it/models/2877387-phone-holder-for-bicycle-motorcycle-scooter#profileId-3213255 ). Ho migliorato un po' l'estetica e ho reso più pratico l'aggancio e lo sgancio quando si cambia l'orientamento del telefono. Rispetto al modello precedente che era fatto di soli tre pezzi, per quello attuale ho scelto di separare le graffe che avvolgono il telefono, stampandole in modo che la trazione a cui sono sottoposte agisca nel senso della lunghezza del filamento, invece che dei layer sovrapposti. Ho introdotto una nuova molla elicoidale, che migliora l'apertura delle due parti laterali, e aumentato l'infill al 90% per gli snodi e le leve di serraggio. Per unire le diverse parti ho utilizzato sia i ganci a scatto già presenti nel precedente modello, sia un nuovo sistema di inserimento con profilo a coda di rondine e bloccaggio a fine corsa. Descrizione del modello Il supporto telefono è composto da 7 particolari: morsetto di fissaggio al manubrio base fissa del supporto base mobile leva di serraggio molla elicoidale graffe laterali “A” (2 pezzi) graffe inferiori “B” (2 pezzi) Il morsetto snodato si applica al manubrio della bicicletta o della moto. L’apertura è regolabile e si adatta a barre con diametro compreso tra circa 18 e 22 mm. Per migliorare l’aderenza sulla superficie liscia del manubrio, è previsto l’utilizzo di un comune elastico di gomma, come mostrato nelle istruzioni di montaggio. Il serraggio iniziale avviene tramite la vite integrata nel morsetto; una volta raggiunta la presa corretta, il bloccaggio finale viene fatto con la leva a scatto. L'estremità del morsetto va inserita in una delle due basi del supporto per mezzo di due profili a coda di rondine, permettendo di scegliere l’orientamento del telefono in verticale o in orizzontale. La due basi scorrono tra di loro per mezzo di una guida e una barra filettata che consente la regolazione della distanza fra le graffe laterali, in base alle dimensioni dello smartphone. La barra è dotata di una leva con eccentrico e molla di contrasto per il blocco e sblocco rapido, così da poter inserire e rimuovere il telefono in modo pratico. Caratteristiche principali Supporto telefono per bici, scooter e moto leggere Morsetto regolabile per manubri da circa 18 a 22 mm Orientamento del telefono verticale o orizzontale Larghezza regolabile in base allo smartphone Leva di blocco e sblocco rapido Nessun attrezzo necessario per il montaggio Solo parti in stampa 3D, nessun altro componente in metallo Design ottimizzato per aumentare resistenza a trazione Materiali e attrezzi necessari Per completare l’assemblaggio è sufficiente aggiungere un comune elastico di gomma con diametro indicativo di circa 30-40 mm. Non sono necessari attrezzi. Consigli di stampa Il supporto è stato progettato per poter sfruttare al massimo le caratteristiche di resistenza nel senso della lunghezza del filamento, anche con materiali poco performanti. Io l'ho stampato con un comune PLA e l'ho testato sulla mia bici. Per renderlo ancora più robusto, ad esempio per l'utilizzo su moto, si può stampare in PETG, o, per chi ha stampanti più performanti della mia A1, anche in PET, ABS o PC. Istruzioni di montaggio 1. Assemblaggio dei particolari Dopo aver stampato tutti i particolari, rimuovere i supporti delle parti a sbalzo ed eliminare le piccole imperfezioni, aiutandosi se necessario con una limetta per unghie. Avvitare e svitare completamente un paio di volte le barre filettate, per eliminare gli impuntamenti. Inserire le graffe laterali “A” negli inserti a coda di rondine delle basi, spingere a fondo fino a che si avverte il “clic” del bloccaggio. Inserire i ganci delle graffe inferiori “B” nei fori delle basi, applicando una pressione uniforme (si, ci vuole parecchia forza, è normale) Accoppiare fra loro le due basi, inserendo la guida, la barra filettata e la molla. Basta avvitare la barra solo per pochi millimetri, la regolazione finale sarà fatta in seguito in base alle dimensioni del telefono. 2. Montaggio del morsetto sul manubrio Aprire lo snodo del morsetto e agganciare l’elastico di gomma tra il filetto della vite e l’estremità opposta del morsetto, facendogli fare mezza torsione in modo che rimanga in posizione. Inserire il morsetto aperto sotto il manubrio e, mentre lo si richiude, sfilare l’elastico dall’estremità opposta e agganciarlo al filetto della vite, vicino all’altro capo. Avvicinare tra loro le due estremità del morsetto e iniziare a serrare la vite girando la leva di bloccaggio. Non serrare subito a fondo: quando il morsetto inizia a fare presa sul manubrio, utilizzare la leva a scatto per il bloccaggio definitivo. Verificare che a morsetto montato, la scritta “UP” sia in alto. 2. Aggancio e sgancio del supporto A seconda che si voglia orientare il telefono in orizzontale o verticale, inserire dall'alto il supporto sul morsetto, utilizzando gli scassi a coda di rondine presenti su una o sull'altra base. Far scorrere verso il basso il supporto, fino a che si avverte il “clic” del bloccaggio. Se si desidera cambiare l'orientamento del telefono, basta tirare verso l'alto il supporto, tenendo fermo il morsetto, sfilarlo e inserirlo nello scasso dell'altra base. 3. Regolazione apertura e blocco del telefono Iniziare a serrare la barra filettata per avvicinare le graffe laterali. Inserire il telefono e continuare la regolazione fino a lasciare lo spazio sufficiente per poterlo estrarre facilmente. Verificare infine che il telefono venga bloccato correttamente agendo sulla leva. Note di sicurezza Prima di usare il supporto su strada, verificare sempre che tutte le parti siano ben agganciate, che il morsetto sia stabile sul manubrio e che il telefono sia trattenuto correttamente. Trattandosi di un oggetto stampato in 3D, la resistenza finale dipende dal materiale utilizzato, dalle impostazioni di stampa e dalla qualità della stampa stessa. Per maggiore sicurezza, soprattutto su moto, scooter o strade sconnesse, consiglio di usare anche un laccetto o un sistema di sicurezza aggiuntivo per evitare la caduta accidentale dello smartphone.

description: 80mm to 120mm Low-Profile Fan Adapter: Short Description: This is a precision-engineered duct adapter that mounts an 80mm pc fan to a 120mm case opening. This can also be used to attach a 120mm fan to an 80mm case opening. Why this design? A flat blanking plate creates a sharp orifice that kills static pressure. A full-length funnel solves that but wastes filament and print time. This adapter splits the difference: a conical bore tapering gives you a smooth, low-turbulence airflow in a compact form factor of just 28mm that is fully self-supporting in PETG with zero internal supports. Quick specs: 120mm mount (105mm hole spacing) ↔ 80mm intake (71.5mm hole spacing) · 28mm tall · ~55g PETG · ~2 hrs print time CAD drawing: This is my first time doing a cad drawing, please forgive me for any mistakes (NOT TO SCALE) Print profiles included: PLA (0.4mm nozzle) — included for convenience, but not recommended due to risk of warping and melting PETG (0.4mm nozzle) — the recommended profile. Best balance of strength, print speed, and detail. PETG (0.6mm nozzle) — for maximum strength. Thicker extrusion lines add rigidity to the bore walls and bosses if you want extra durability or are running the adapter under mechanical stress. Test fit first — some 80mm fans and 120mm openings vary by 1-2mm from spec. Verify your hardware before printing a full batch, you can look at the cad drawings provided. Questions or fit issues? Drop a comment — happy to help troubleshoot. Thanks for taking your time to read this, and happy printing!

Standard sand filtration is great for coarse debris, but it fails to trap particles smaller than 20–40 microns. This leads to cloudy water and oily surfaces. This Pre-Filter is designed to sit directly inside your inflatable pool to catch ultra-fine contaminants before they can reach your filtration sand. By filling the chamber with a regular filter sponge or aquarium filter floss, you create a powerful micro-barrier that elevates your pool's water clarity. Inside the housing, an integrated internal grid prevents the filter media from collapsing or being sucked into the hose under vacuum pressure. 💡 Why Do You Need This? Standard sand filters cannot effectively capture: Sunscreen & Body Oils: They bypass the sand and form an oily film on the water. If they reach the sand filter, they coat the sand grains, causing them to clump together and create channels where unfiltered water flows right back into the pool. Filter floss/sponge naturally binds these greases. Pollen & Fine Dust: Micro-particles pass right through sand, keeping the water cloudy. This pre-filter traps them at the source. Algae Spores & Fine Silt: Captures early-stage organic material, preventing the sand from becoming slimy and losing its efficiency.

description: Inspired by the zeromouse and finalmouse, this is a more accessible and affordable ultralight wireless mouse that uses the Bambu Wireless Mouse Components Kit. This is a size reduction of my other ultralight mouse . Check out that one if this is too small for you. The mouse buttons use a locking dovetail design, which means you can design your own buttons and hot swap them as you like. To install the ones in the print profile, clear the support material from the dovetail, then slide the button onto the mouse body from the front. The protrusion under the button face that actually engages with the PCB button needs to be toward the outside of the mouse on both sides. They should fit nice and easy if they are on the correct sides. If they are on the wrong sides, you will have to force them and will likely break the mouse body. I have included a profile for taller and even shorter buttons, but the ones in the main profile are my suggestion. There bambu kit needs to be modified slightly in order to make these parts fit correctly. The solder tab on the battery terminals needs to be folded in so that it bends slightly toward the spring/nub. This is a delicate operation that should be done carefully with pliers so the solder connection and wire are not broken from the tabs. This allows the contacts to be installed with the wires facing down, so the wires do not interfere with the hand grips. The small flared pieces of metal on either side of the nub/spring also need to be crushed down with pliers so they do not snag when being installed upside down. These wires need to be installed first, then the lens, followed by the board (with wheel preinstalled), before finally adding the finger buttons. This was designed to be used with dot skates like this . The skates from the normal bambu kit need to be cut in half to fit, and the cut corners need to be rounded. One goes under each button and one goes in each rear corner. IMPORTANT: The mouse will not function without the skid pads. It will slide perfectly fine on a mousepad, but the skid pads keep the laser the correct distance from the surface. Without them, the laser will not track correctly. I use these rechargeable lithium batteries so I dont go through AAAs too often. These batteries are lighter than a standard AAA and have USB-C ports in them to recharge them. If you are willing to do a bit of soldering, the Bambu PCB will accept standard 3 pin micro switches. The plastic finger button heights work for the stock Bambu buttons but should also work with standard 3 pin micro switches. I have tested with Huano blue shell pink dots and Kailh GM 8.0s as well and both work with the included finger buttons.

model_name: Fan Vertical Antenna V2 - Ground Mount, 10-40m
description: I like building antennas. This is an ongoing project and there have been major changes from V1 to V2. There may be more to come based on how it works. If you want a “sure-thing” and support - I'd recommend a DX Commander. Version 1 of this model had issues with the base deforming during high heat. I had updated the V1 model with an improved base but have since reinforced it more based on AI analysis. There were a couple issues: PETG is apparently subject to “creep” if under tension the black PETG I used absorbed more heat allowing easier deformation the mechanical structure wasn't robust enough ASA is the recommended filament for this build. I'm still using PETG for two reasons: 1) I want to see how the improved mechanical design works, and 2) I haven't finished my external exhaust hookup so I can print ASA. I've also split it into two models - one for ground mount (this one) and added a pole mount option (a new style). I've also added a number of support pieces that I'll reference later. Changes for V2: Even stronger base using design and printing modifications based on AI analysis of the CAD files Added a bird defender , holes on each layer to add filament that sticks up. It doesn't stop the birds from landing on the antenna and pooping on it, but it does seem to reduce it The base is designed to use ¼" by 1" stainless steel bolts. You'll also need washers, lock washers and nuts (11) ¼" x 1" stainless bolts (11) ¼" stainless lock washers (22) ¼" stainless washers (11) ¼" stainless wing nuts This uses a 12m Heavy Duty Spider Pole with the top two sections removed. For permanent mounting, you will need the “stay up” kit. You will also need stainless/marine grade ¼" ring terminals for wiring the driven elements, base driven element connectors, base ground element connectors and radials. A panel mount SO-239 is used. Note : when wiring it, have the wire make a complete loop (feed the driven elements in both directions). It will work otherwise but if you rewire wrong it de-tunes the antenna. When installing the plates, they can be above or below the “stay-up” clamps. When I got my second Spider Pole, I found differences in how tightly the plates fit. Push them as low as they will go on the appropriate section. If they are still a little loose and can rotate, put electrical tape on the side diameter to snug it up. For tuning, start with 40 meters. Disconnect the driven elements for all other bands while leaving them installed. Once 40m is tune, go higher in frequency band by band. NOTE: On the first version I couldn't get 10m to tune. I was able to tune it. The issue is that with harmonics its hard to tell which low is for the 10m element and which is just a harmonic. Before connecting the 10m element, use your NanoVNA to do a sweep from 1 MHz to 30 MHz using NanoVNASaver. Save that sweep as a reference. Connect the 10m element and do another sweep. It should identify a new low that is the one you would use for calculating the calibration for 10m. On V1 I had planned on it being used for field activations. I assumed I'd need to retune it every time I put it up so I left the holes in the plates larger to allow zip ties to go through. This was not the case. While I used zip ties while tuning, once tuned I used adhesive heat shrink tubing to to hold the foldback. This allowed smaller holes and removed little parts. For the guy ropes, Kevlar line is recommended. Paracord needs adjusting due to stretching but I haven't had an issue with this in the temporary mount, only the permanent mount. I will update with my wire lengths the next time I take it down to tune. I used smaller lengths than the recommended lengths for the DX Commander Signature 9. Related models are: Wire Labels for the driven elements https://makerworld.com/en/models/1486447-pota-performer-18-gauge-wire-band-labels#profileId-1553134 “Sockets” to allow screw guy anchors to be below ground level allowing you to remove the guy rope and mow over the anchor https://makerworld.com/en/models/2986316-antenna-guy-anchor-recess#profileId-3351047 Base Plate to keep base from sliding (requires and H2D, if you don't have one, you can use stakes around the base) https://makerworld.com/en/models/2586413-vertical-fan-antenna-stake-base#profileId-2853279 I failed to take pictures of all the parts when I printed them. I'll be adding more pictures as I have a chance to get them.

description: This is my interpretation of the Panzer DC tank made by @Kugelblatz Since this is a fake tank, I thought I would make a backstory for it! After 1945, the German industrial complex was still able to churn out more machines of war; the Panzer IX was but one of them. In 1946, a replacement for the Maus was requested. Most allied tanks struggled against the armor geometry of the Maus, so it was used as the basis for the Panzer 9. The Turret of the Maus was scaled up to fit the new 200mm Kwk cannon and a 100mm coaxial cannon. The main turret was raised in order to fit the engine bay underneath it. A modified King Tiger turret was placed in the front section to deal with more lightly armored enemies. The Panther tanks were deemed a success, and an enlarged turret design was requested to be used with the 88mm gun and to be mounted on the midsection of the tank. A larger design in general was developed to make it more difficult for the newly unleashed T95 TD, and T29/T34 Heavy tanks to penetrate the side armor. The Panzer IX is roughly the size of two Maus tanks, so it was seen as a more feasible production option compared to the P.1000 Ratte. A squadron of Anti-air vehicles would be at the Panzer IX's side at all times to deter bombing attacks from the Allies. (Note the second Panzer IX was destroyed by an American F-80 about two weeks into deployment.) This is a fake tank, but I hope you like the lore I thought of! Enjoy!

This project converts the Behringer Model D into a compact desktop unit inspired by the Elektron form factor (Octatrack MK1, Digitakt, Digitone, etc.). The enclosure has a similar footprint and overall proportions to Elektron devices, although dimensions are not identical. The design has been printed, assembled and tested. Features Similar footprint to Elektron desktop instruments Two-piece enclosure with integrated tenon joints for easy alignment and increased rigidity Rear cable routing slots for the original ribbon cables Dedicated mounting plates for the original I/O and power board Internal support for the connector PCB Reuses the original Model D electronics and front panel Assembly Perform a dry fit before gluing. If required, lightly sand the tenons for a perfect fit (normally not necessary). Insert the eight M3 nuts into the internal slots before closing the enclosure. Apply a small amount of CA glue inside the tenon slots of one side panel. Avoid using too much glue. Insert the tenons into the glued slots. Apply a thin bead of CA glue only along the center of the mating surfaces. Avoid excess glue to prevent squeeze-out. Apply a small amount of CA glue to the exposed top surfaces of the tenons and assemble the enclosure. Keep it square while the glue cures. Moderate pressure is sufficient. An optional CA glue activator can be used to speed up curing. Allow the enclosure to fully cure before installing the electronics. Remove the electronics from the original Behringer Model D. Keep all original hardware, as some parts will be reused. Install the I/O board on the dedicated rear plate and route the ribbon cables through the side slots. Install the supplied PCB support underneath the connector board using the existing holes. It is optional but recommended, as it helps support the PCB while connecting the cables. Install the front panel, connect all cables and test the unit before fitting the rear covers. Secure the rear covers using 14 × 8–10 mm self-tapping screws. Tighten the screws only until snug. Excessive torque is unnecessary and may damage the printed parts. Printing Notes The logo cover can be printed either with the raised logo or as a plain single-color version. PLA and PETG both work well. PETG is recommended if higher impact and heat resistance are desired. Printing Tips Due to its size, the enclosure may be prone to slight warping. Minor warping usually does not affect assembly, but the following tips can help achieve the best results: If your printer has an Aux Fan (such as the Bambu Lab H2 series), disable it. Direct airflow on large flat parts can increase warping. Thoroughly clean the build plate with warm water and dish soap before printing to maximize bed adhesion. Allow the print to cool completely on the build plate before removing it. Removing the part while it is still warm may cause additional warping. Disclaimer This project includes only the printed enclosure and related printed parts. The Behringer Model D, electronics, knobs, screws and PCB assemblies are not included. This is an unofficial community project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Behringer.

description: I like building antennas. This is an ongoing project and there have been major changes from V1 to V2. There may be more to come based on how it works. If you want a “sure-thing” and support - I'd recommend a DX Commander. Version 1 of this model had issues with the base deforming during high heat. I had updated that model with an improved base but have since reinforced it more based on AI analysis. There were a couple issues: PETG is apparently subject to “creep” if under tension the black PETG I used absorbed more heat allowing easier deformation the mechanical structure wasn't robust enough ASA is the recommended filament for this build. I'm still using PETG for two reasons: 1) I want to see how the improved mechanical design works, and 2) I haven't finished my external exhaust hookup so I can print ASA. I've also split it into two models - one for ground mount (as in V1) and added a pole mount option (this one). I've also added a number of support pieces that I'll reference later. Changes for V2: Even stronger base using design and printing modifications based on AI analysis of the CAD files Now supports permanent mounting on a pole in the ground (There will be a separate ground mount version) Wire hole diameter decreased - removed the need for small spacers New layer for guy ropes - SpiderBeam recommends a higher level guy rope. Since V1 was ground mounted I chose to move the guy ropes lower. This version adds a new layer consistent with SpiderBeam's recommendation Added a bird defender , holes on each layer to add filament that sticks up. It doesn't stop the birds from landing on the antenna and pooping on it, but it does seem to reduce it The base is designed to use ¼" by 1" stainless steel bolts. You'll also need washers, lock washers and nuts (11) ¼" x 1" stainless bolts (11) ¼" stainless lock washers (22) ¼" stainless washers (11) ¼" stainless wing nuts This uses a 12m Heavy Duty Spider Pole with the top two sections removed. For permanent mounting, you will need the “stay up” kit. You will also need stainless/marine grade ¼" ring terminals for wiring the driven elements, base driven elements, base ground elements and radials. A panel mount SO-239 is used. Note: when wiring it, have the wire make a complete loop (feed the driven elements in both directions). It will work otherwise but if you rewire wrong it de-tunes the antenna. When installing the plates, they can be above or below the “stay-up” clamps. When I got my second Spider Pole, I found differences in how tightly the plates fit. Push them as low as they will go on the appropriate section. If they are still a little loose and can rotate, put electrical tape on the side diameter to snug it up. For tuning, start with 40 meters. Disconnect the driven elements for all other bands while leaving them installed. Once 40m is tune, go higher in frequency band by band. NOTE: On the first version I couldn't get 10m to tune. I was able to tune it. The issue is that with harmonics its hard to tell which low is for the 10m element and which is just a harmonic. Before connecting the 10m element, use your NanoVNA to do a sweep from 1 MHz to 30 MHz using NanoVNASaver. Save that sweep as a reference. Connect the 10m element and do another sweep. It should identify a new low that is the one you would use for calculating the calibration for 10m. On V1 I had planned on it being used for field activations. I assumed I'd need to retune so I left the holes in the plates larger to allow zip ties to go through. Since this is intended for a permanent mount, I used smaller wire holes since you don't need zip ties. (I used zip ties while tuning, but once tuned I used adhesive heat shrink tubing to to hold the foldback). For the guy ropes, Kevlar line is recommended. I've used paracord but it needs regular adjusting due to stretching. I will update with my wire lengths the next time I take it down to tune. I used smaller lengths than the recommended lengths for the DX Commander Signature 9. Related models are: Wire Labels for the driven elements https://makerworld.com/en/models/1486447-pota-performer-18-gauge-wire-band-labels#profileId-1553134 “Sockets” to allow screw guy anchors to be below ground level allowing you to remove the guy rope and mow over the anchor https://makerworld.com/en/models/2986316-antenna-guy-anchor-recess#profileId-3351047 PVC pipe mount spacer (not uploaded yet) Grass deflector to keep grass from growing around the antenna base (not uploaded yet) Covers and plugs for 2" conduit https://makerworld.com/en/models/2986399-antenna-coax-conduit-2-schedule-40-pvc-cap#profileId-3351151 Coax labels for in the shack https://makerworld.com/en/models/2843997-coax-labels#profileId-3170941 I failed to take pictures of all the parts when I printed them. I'll be adding more pictures as I have a chance to get them.

description: TPU Wristband for Google Fitbit Air Flexible TPU Band · Snap-In Fit · Printable Pins A complete 3D printed TPU wristband for the Google Fitbit Air . This design lets you wear the Fitbit Air like a regular wristband, without needing an additional commercial strap. The Fitbit Air “bean” simply clicks into the printed band and is held in place by the flexible TPU structure. I printed my version in TPU 95A , which works very well, but softer or slightly harder TPU materials should also work depending on your printer, settings, and personal comfort preference. ✨ Key Features Complete Printable Wristband This is a full wristband design for the Google Fitbit Air, not just a holder or adapter. Flexible TPU Design Designed to be printed in TPU, making the band flexible, wearable, and comfortable on the wrist. Secure Snap-In Fit The Google Fitbit Air clicks directly into the band and sits securely inside the integrated holder. Printable Closure Pins To close the band, use one or multiple printed band pins. The pins are pushed through the holes of the band to lock it in place. Custom Color Options The band pins can be printed in the same color or in a different color to create a nice accent. You can also mix materials for the pins, for example TPU for a flexible look or PLA/PETG for a stiffer pin. Uni-Size Design The current version is a uni-size model and should fit a wide range of wrist sizes, from relatively small to larger wrist circumferences. Lightweight & Minimal The design uses only a small amount of material and keeps the overall look clean and simple. ⚠️ Compatibility Warning This model is designed specifically for the Google Fitbit Air . Please do not print this wristband for other Fitbit or Google devices unless you have checked the dimensions yourself. The fit is intentionally designed around the Google Fitbit Air, so other devices will most likely not fit correctly. ⚠️ Disclaimer Use this model at your own risk. I am not responsible for any damage to your Google Fitbit Air, the printed wristband, the printed pins, or anything else. Please always make sure the Fitbit Air is clicked in securely and the band is properly closed before wearing it, especially during sports or movement. 🖨️ Printing Instructions Recommended Material I printed my version in TPU 95A . Softer TPU should also work and may feel more comfortable. Slightly harder TPU may also work, but the band will become less flexible. Band Pins The pins can be printed in: TPU PLA PETG or basically any other material you prefer For a more flexible and soft closure, use TPU. For a stiffer and more defined pin, PLA or PETG can work well. Print Profile Please use my uploaded print profile for the best result, especially if you are unsure about TPU settings. Supports Supports are not strictly required , but they can improve the visual result. If you are able to print clean TPU supports, or if you can support TPU with PLA using a dual extruder / multi-material setup, you can get a cleaner finish around the Fitbit Air “bean” opening. Without supports, the top side of the bean opening may look a bit rougher or less clean, but the part should still function normally. Material & Support Tip If your printer handles TPU well, printing the entire model in TPU is the simplest option. If you have a dual extruder or multi-material setup, using PLA as support material for TPU can help improve the surface quality in supported areas. Filament Usage The model is small and needs only a moderate amount of TPU. 🛠️ Assembly & Usage Print the TPU wristband. Print one or more band pins. Click the Google Fitbit Air into the integrated holder. Wrap the band around your wrist. Choose the holes that fit your wrist size best. Push the printed pin through the band holes to close the wristband. Check that the Fitbit Air is secure and the closure pin is fully seated before wearing. 🎨 Customization Ideas Print the band in classic black for a clean look. Use white TPU for a bright, sporty style. Print the pins in a contrasting color for a small design accent. Try different TPU hardness levels to adjust comfort and flexibility. Use multiple pins if you want a stronger or more secure closure. 💬 Final Note This is currently a uni-size design , made to cover a fairly wide range of wrist sizes. Feedback and makes are very welcome. If you like this design, please leave a like and share a picture of your make. Happy printing!

IP67 LED Strip Clip (Tape / Glue-On Version) If you have ever tried mounting a rugged, waterproof IP67 LED strip, you know that standard mounting clips are a total nightmare. They are always too narrow, which ends up crushing the thick silicone sleeve, ruining the look, or worse, damaging the LEDs inside. I designed this heavy-duty clip specifically to fit the extra width and height of IP67 waterproof silicone sleeves perfectly. No Screws, No Drilling! This version is engineered with a completely flat, solid base meant for mounting with double-sided tape (like 3M VHB tape) or glue (silicone, construction adhesive, or hot glue). It is ideal for renting situations, aluminum profiles, glass, tile, or anywhere you simply cannot, or do not want to, drill holes. Why this design works great: - Perfect Silicone Fit: Tailored dimensions ensure the thick IP67 casing slides or snaps in easily without being squeezed. - Maximized Surface Area: The bottom is perfectly flat and widened to provide maximum grip for tape or adhesive, so your LED strips won't sag over time. - Low-Profile and Clean: Minimalistic look that stays practically invisible once installed under cabinets, behind desks, or along accent walls. - Print-Optimized Strength: Designed to be printed flat on its side. This layer orientation ensures the clip arms are incredibly strong and won't snap when you press the LED strip into place. No supports required! Recommended Print Settings: For the best durability and flexibility, I highly recommend using the uploaded Bambu Studio Print Profile (.3mf) or following these settings: - Orientation: Print the clip flat on its side (already pre-configured in the profile) for maximum mechanical strength! - Material PETG / ASA: Highly recommended if your LED strips run hot at full brightness or if you are mounting them outdoors (for UV and weather resistance). - Material PLA: Works perfectly fine for normal indoor setups. - Layer Height: 0.20mm is the sweet spot for speed and strength. - Infill: 20% to 100% (Since it is a tiny part, using a higher infill or adding more wall loops gives the arms great springiness and durability). - Supports: None needed! 100% support-free geometry. Installation Tip: Make sure to clean the mounting surface with some rubbing alcohol before applying your double-sided tape or adhesive. Let the glue or tape cure for a bit before snapping the IP67 LED strip into the clips for the strongest bond! description: Upgrade Your View: High-Mount Roof Rack Adapter for AUTO-VOX Solar1 Pro / Solar3a Backup Cameras Tired of the low, license-plate mounting position for your wireless backup camera? They are not angry — they are concentrating! Their tightly closed eyes, clenched teeth, and serious expressions show how hard they are trying to squeeze their legs together and hold the bag closed. It is clearly a very demanding farm job. The cow is pressing with all its strength. The pig is giving one mighty little squeeze. The sheep is putting all that woolly determination to work. The chicken is clucking with concentration and squeezing with all its feathery might. Prefer a happier expression? When they are off duty, the Farm Animal Bag Clip Squad can also become a tiny farm playset. Create wild adventures, arrange an important animal meeting, or let them compete to see who can make the funniest squeezing face. Their chunky shapes and exaggerated expressions make them fun characters for playful souls of all ages. Their home on the fridge Each animal has a hole on its back designed for a 6 × 2 mm magnet. I have also added an optional second magnet hole using a negative part in Bambu Studio. Print the model as it is to create two magnet holes for a stronger hold on the refrigerator. These clips are made for anyone who enjoys practical prints with a silly personality — especially grown-ups who are still children at heart. The Tomato System – Storm Edition The original Tomato System exceeded all expectations and quickly became one of my most popular gardening designs. It proved that a modular, stackable support system could be easy to print, easy to expand, and adaptable to a wide range of plants. As more growers began using it, one piece of feedback appeared consistently: “Can it be made even stronger?” The Tomato System – Storm Edition is the result. Rather than simply reinforcing the original design, I went back to the drawing board and rethought how the entire structure is assembled. The goal was simple: create a version that is noticeably more rigid, more stable, and better suited for demanding outdoor conditions while maintaining the flexibility that made the original system so popular. A Stronger Approach The biggest change is found in the way the system is assembled. Unlike the original Tomato System, which used push-fit vertical posts and external locking clips, the Storm Edition uses threaded vertical posts that screw directly into each support level. This creates a much stronger mechanical connection between sections and significantly increases the overall rigidity of the structure. The threaded design also introduces a unique advantage. New levels can be added without loosening or affecting the sections below. As your plant grows throughout the season, the support structure can grow with it—one level at a time. Cleaner Assembly, Fewer Parts Because each level is securely connected using threaded posts, the side locking clips used by the original design are no longer necessary. The result is a cleaner appearance, fewer loose components, and a more streamlined assembly process. Simply connect the sections using the supplied posts and continue building upward as needed. Designed Around Plant Growth Every plant grows differently, which is why the Storm Edition includes two lengths of vertical posts. Long posts allow for larger spacing between support levels, while short posts can be used when additional support is needed around fruit-heavy branches or dense growth. By mixing the two lengths, you can fine-tune the structure to suit the shape and growth pattern of your individual plant. Built for the Outdoors For gardeners growing directly in soil, the Storm Edition includes optional Soil Anchors. These pointed attachments screw onto the bottom of the vertical posts and help the structure penetrate the ground more easily. They also provide a more secure footing in loose soil, improving stability and helping the system remain firmly planted even in challenging weather conditions. The “Storm Edition” name wasn’t chosen by accident. Not Just for Garden Beds One of the most requested additions was support for existing potted plants. To solve this, the Storm Edition includes an optional Flat Base accessory that allows the system to be used on patios, balconies, greenhouses, windowsills, and other flat surfaces. Simply place the pot inside the base and build the support structure around it. This makes the system just as useful for container gardening as it is for traditional garden beds. The Next Evolution The original Tomato System remains available and continues to be a fantastic option for many growers. https://makerworld.com/en/models/938466-the-tomato-system#profileId-903723 However, if you’re looking for the strongest, most versatile, and most refined version of the concept, the Storm Edition represents the next step in its evolution: Stronger connections. Greater stability. More flexibility. Better support for growing plants. And just like the original, it’s designed to be easy to print, easy to expand, and built to grow alongside your harvest. 🍅 Happy growing!

model_name: Cantilever case for 48 Pencils with Eject Buttons
description: Organize your workspace with this compact, cascading 4-tier pencil and crayon box! Designed with both aesthetics and ergonomics in mind, this cantilever-style box holds up to 48 pencils (12 per tray) and expands smoothly to give you a perfect overview of your color palette. ✨ Key Features: Smart "Eject" Buttons: No more struggling to pick up a pencil. Each slot features a clever built-in button – simply press it, and the pencil pops up for effortless grabbing. Ergonomic Tilt: The bottom tray is equipped with retractable legs. When deployed, the entire organizer tilts toward you. This not only makes reaching for colors easier but also naturally aligns the pencils with the eject buttons using gravity. 100% 3D Printable / No Hardware Required: The entire folding mechanism can be assembled using a custom 3D-printed strap/pin insert that holds everything together perfectly. (Note: Standard M3 screws can be used as an optional alternative). Customizable Magnetic Closure: The trays feature hidden slots for 4x2mm round magnets. Each corner has room for up to 3 magnets. You can use just 1 magnet per corner (as I did in my build) or add more to adjust and fine-tune the exact magnetic pull and snapping force you want when closing the box. ⚙ Printing & Materials: Orientation: All parts are already oriented correctly in the files – just slice and print! Filament: I printed the entire box in PETG, which I highly recommend. You can use PLA for the main trays and body, but the custom strap/pin inserts must be printed in PETG (or ABS/ASA). PLA is too brittle for the mechanical stress of the hinges and may snap. Magnets: 4x2mm round (up to 12 per tray depending on desired strength). 🧩 Printed Parts List & STL Filenames To build the complete 48-pencil organizer (4 tiers), you will need to print the following parts: Part Name Qty STL Filename Notes & Material Inner Tray 4 Inner_Tray_x4.stl Main insert, holds 12 pencils. Outer Tray 4 Outer_Tray_x4.stl Outer shell for each tier. Eject Buttons 48 Eject_Button_x48.stl The lifting mechanism. Frame 4 Frame_x4.stl Aesthetic top trim. Short Link 4 Short_Link_x4.stl Cantilever expansion arms. Long Link 4 Long_Link_x4.stl Cantilever expansion arms. Rear Tilt Legs 1 Rear_Tilt_Legs_x1.stl Deploys for ergonomic tilt. Hinge Strap 8 Hinge_Strap_PETG_x8.stl Print in PETG! 3D printed alternative to M3 screws. you can replace each strap with three M3 screws. 🛠 Additional Hardware Required (Non-Printed) Button Pivot Axis: 4 pieces of standard 1.75mm filament . Cut these to the length of the tray. They serve as a simple, cheap, and effective hinge axis for the eject buttons. Magnets (Optional): 4x2mm round neodymium magnets. The trays feature top and bottom magnet slots in each corner. You can use 1 to 3 magnets per corner depending on how strong you want the snapping force to be. Middle Trays (x2): 8 to 24 magnets per tray (requires both top and bottom slots). Bottom Tray: 4 to 12 magnets (requires top slots only). Top Tray: 4 to 12 magnets (requires bottom slots only). 💡 Pro Tip: I recommend installing top magnets in the top tray as well! A dedicated top cover/lid for easy transport is on my TODO list and will be released in a future update. Linkage Assembly (Choose Option A or B): Option A (100% 3D Printed): Use the 8x printed hinge straps (Hinge_Strap_PETG_x8.stl). Option B (Hardware): Use 24x short M3 screws (6 per tier). 🛠 Assembly Instructions Step 1: Assembling the Inner Trays 1. Gather parts: You need 1 Inner Tray, 12 Eject Buttons, and ~20cm of 1.75mm filament. 2. Position buttons: Place the tray flat and put the 12 buttons into their slots. 3. Thread filament: Push the filament through the side hole, passing through all button hinges. Tip: Cut the filament tip at an angle for easier routing. Twist it if it gets stuck. 4. Trim excess: Cut the filament flush with the outside of the tray. Repeat this entire process 4 times. Step 2: Assembling the Bottom Outer Tray (Tier 1) 1. Attach Links: Counting the side pins from the front: Leave the 1st pinempty, attach a Short Link to the 2nd pin, and a Long Link to the 3rd pin. 2. Attach Legs: Snap the 2 Rear Tilt Legs into the connection points at the back of the tray. 3. Insert Magnets: Place magnets into the top pockets. (Optional: Use a tiny drop of glue to secure them). 4. Attach Frame & Hardware: Snap the Frame onto the top. Secure the links and legs with 6x M3 screws or 2x printed Hinge Straps. Step 3: Stacking and Connecting (Tiers 2, 3, & 4) 1. Add Magnets: Insert magnets into both top and bottom pockets of the new tray. ⚠ CRITICAL: Double-check magnet polarity so the trays attract each other! 2. Shift Linkage: Attach the tray to the tier below. The links shift forward by one slot: The link from the 2nd slot below goes to the 1st slot here. The link from the 3rd slot below goes to the 2nd slot here. 3. Add New Links: • Tier 2: Add a Long Link in the 3rd slot. • Tier 3: Add a Short Link in the 3rd slot. • Tier 4 (Top): Leave the 3rd slot empty. Note: Do not install rear legs on these tiers. 4. Secure: Lock each tier with a Frame and your chosen hardware (screws or printed straps). Step 4: Final Assembly 1. Insert Inner Trays: Press your completed Inner Trays down into the assembled Outer Trays. They are designed for a snug friction fit. 2. Check Direction: Make sure the Eject Buttons are facing the front of the box! 3. Done! Load up your 48 pencils or crayons, extend the rear legs, and enjoy your new cascading organizer. 🚀 To-Do / Future Ideas (V2.0) While I am incredibly happy with how this design turned out and believe it is fully ready to organize your desk right now, a maker's work is never truly done! Here are a few ideas I am exploring for future updates: Dedicated Top Lid: Designing a snap-on cover (utilizing those top magnets) to protect the pencils from dust and make the entire box completely portable. Design Simplification: Exploring ways to merge the inner and outer trays into a single printable piece to reduce both print time and assembly steps. Enhanced Stability: Fine-tuning the cantilever linkage geometry to slightly reduce the backward offset of the expanded tiers, making the fully opened box even more balanced and stable. If you have any feedback or ideas after printing, let me know in the comments!

description: 🍷 FrosNest – Keep your wine cool, enjoy the moment. 🍷☀️ FrosNest is a wine-serving accessory designed to keep your bottles at their ideal serving temperature for as long as possible during meals, aperitifs, barbecues, and summer gatherings. Compatible with the vast majority of 750 ml wine bottles , FrosNest accommodates a standard ice pack, ice cubes, or a combination of both. Its insulated cooling compartment helps reduce heat exchange while its design promotes the circulation of cool air around the bottle. The sections surrounding the bottle that do not contain a cooling source feature a double-wall construction , creating an insulating air gap that slows heat transfer and improves temperature retention. Designed as a complete wine-serving station, FrosNest also includes a dedicated corkscrew holder and an ergonomic carrying handle, making it easy to transport everything with one hand. 🔄 Update – FrosNest V4 Both V2 and V3 remain fully functional and continue to do exactly what they were designed for: helping keep your bottle at its ideal serving temperature for longer. V4 is not a fix , but rather a natural evolution of the concept, making it even more practical and versatile. What's New in V4 🗑️ The mini trash bin is now fully integrated into the FrosNest. There's no longer a separate accessory to print or store. It's always within reach for the cork, foil capsule, Champagne wire cage, or any small waste, helping keep your table clean and organized. 🧊 The cooling compartment has been enlarged to 104 × 40 mm , making it compatible with a wider variety of commercially available ice packs. 🍾 The corkscrew holder has been redesigned to better accommodate a larger range of waiter's corkscrews while making insertion and removal easier. 🥂 A new optional removable wine glass holder is now available for both V3 and V4. It is compatible with many stemmed wine glasses featuring a stem diameter of less than approximately 9 mm . Up to two holders can be mounted on each side , allowing you to carry up to four wine glasses together with the FrosNest. I hope this new evolution makes FrosNest even more enjoyable to use while preserving everything that made the previous versions so successful. 🍷❄️ 🔄 Update – FrosNest V3 Thanks to your amazing feedback, FrosNest has already evolved! 😊 First of all, the original version remains fully functional and already does exactly what it was designed to do: help keep your bottle at its ideal serving temperature for longer. However, after reading your suggestions and feedback, I wanted to push the concept even further. FrosNest V3 builds upon the original design by improving the circulation of cooled air around the bottle while keeping the same simple, practical, and efficient philosophy. V3 introduces several improvements: ❄️ The cooling compartment has been moved above the bottle. Since cooled air is denser than warm air, this new position promotes a more natural circulation of cool air around the bottle, helping to maintain its serving temperature even more effectively. 🍾 The bottle opening has been increased to 90 mm , making FrosNest compatible with most standard Champagne bottles in addition to regular 750 ml wine bottles. 🎨 The FrosNest logo has been reduced in size , minimizing filament color changes on multi-material printers and reducing filament waste during color swaps. 🗑️ A new optional accessory has been added: a removable mini trash bin , perfect for holding the cork, foil capsule, wire hood, or any small waste that would otherwise end up on the table. A version is available for both FrosNest V2 and FrosNest V3 . A huge thank you to everyone who took the time to share ideas and suggestions. Your feedback has helped make FrosNest V3 an even more refined and versatile design while preserving the spirit of the original concept. 🍷❄️ Features ❄️ Compatible with 160 × 95 × 30 mm ice packs 🧊 Can be used with ice cubes, cold water, or a combination of both 🍷 Compatible with most 750 ml wine bottles 🔒 Insulated lid to reduce cold loss 🌡️ Double-wall insulation around the non-cooled sections 🍾 Integrated corkscrew holder ✋ Ergonomic carrying handle 🖨️ Designed for 3D printing 🌞 Perfect for patios, barbecues, picnics, and outdoor dining Printing Recommendations For the best printing results, do not enable the "Supports on Build Plate Only" option . Print the FrosNest standing upright on its base , exactly as provided in the model files. This orientation has been carefully designed to: ✅ Minimize filament consumption ✅ Generate supports only where they are truly needed ✅ Optimize the watertightness of the cooling compartment ✅ Ensure a reliable print Usage Tips To maximize temperature retention: Use an ice pack, ice cubes, or a combination of both. Adding a small amount of cold water to the cooling compartment increases the contact surface with the ice pack, improving cooling efficiency. On particularly hot days, simply place a lightly damp towel or cloth over both the bottle and the FrosNest to further reduce heat exchange with the surrounding air. Optional Accessory An optional condensation drip tray can also be printed. Placed underneath the FrosNest, it collects condensation and meltwater from the cooling compartment, helping to keep your table clean and dry during outdoor meals and gatherings. Why "FrosNest"? Because every great bottle deserves a comfortable place to rest. FrosNest combines Frost and Nest —a protective home that helps your wine stay at its ideal serving temperature for longer, so every glass can be enjoyed exactly as intended. And thanks to its playful mascot—a cheerful wine bottle enjoying the cool—FrosNest reminds us that even fine wine deserves to relax a little. 😉🍷❄️

description: PawDrop – Paw-Operated Feeder Meet PawDrop , an interactive pet training feeder created for the MakerWorld Pet Feeder Design Contest and designed around Bambu Lab’s new PLA Pure . Unlike a traditional automatic feeder, PawDrop is operated by the pet itself: The pet presses the front lever with its paw The internal opening releases small treats A printed PETG spring automatically resets the mechanism PawDrop is immediately ready for the next round This turns treat time into a simple and rewarding enrichment activity. Why PawDrop? Paw-operated mechanical design No electronics or batteries No screws, glue or purchased hardware Fully 3D printable Printed PETG reset spring Optional ballast compartment for extra stability Designed and tested on the Bambu Lab A1 Mini Simple five-step assembly Suitable for small dry treats or kibble The wide stance provides excellent stability. For especially enthusiastic pets, the hollow space underneath the inlay can also be filled with clean stones or another suitable weight before the inlay is installed. Materials The main components can be printed in PLA Pure : Body Legs Lever Inlay Lid PLA Pure was chosen because its clean formulation and very low printing emissions make it especially interesting for objects used around pets and inside the home. Important: Print the spring in PETG The red spring must be printed in PETG . During testing, PETG provided the best combination of flexibility, spring force and durability. A PLA spring may work initially but can fatigue or break after only a few activations. The spring is intentionally printed in a contrasting color so that the mechanical reset system remains slightly visible. Assembly Attach the legs to the body Insert the PETG spring Insert the front lever Place the inlay inside the body Attach the lid No tools are required. How to use PawDrop Fill the container with small, dry treats. Start by demonstrating the mechanism and pressing the lever yourself. Once your pet understands where the reward comes from, encourage it to touch and press the lever with its paw. Keep the first training sessions short and positive. Printing notes PawDrop was designed to fit within the 180 × 180 mm build volume of the A1 Mini . The A1 Mini print profile is therefore divided across multiple plates. The color combination is completely optional. Only the spring material is functionally important. Safety and hygiene Use PawDrop only with appropriately sized dry treats and supervise your pet during use. Although PLA Pure uses ingredients certified for food-contact applications, the safety and cleanability of a finished FDM print also depend on the printer, nozzle, printing environment and maintenance. Clean the accessible parts regularly, inspect them for damage and replace worn components when necessary. Do not use PawDrop with wet or sticky food. Designed, printed and tested with the help of Waldi , PawDrop’s official Chief Tester. 🐾 UPDATE: A second print profile with a lighter spring is now included for users who prefer an easierer paw press.

model_name: [V2] Dual Hose Adapter Mod 150mm for portable AC
description: 🚨 UPDATE 2026-06-27 (V2): Complete Redesign! 🚨- focus on printing the slim version. It is all you need, 50% less time and 50% less filament with the same functionality. Only 1 Build plate - no splitting anymore. Big version only left for legacy/looks/A1Mini. More info at the bottom. Pair this with my 150mm Hose through-pass Connector (link) ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Compatibility I designed this adapter for a budget-friendly portable AC bought at "Action" here in Germany. The unit is sold under the house brand KINZO (9000 BTU), but a friend tested it on a Comfee device (7000BTU) and it fits perfectly as well. After doing some research, it turns out this is a very common OEM device base shared by many different brands on the market. While I found some mods for models with corner air intakes, there was nothing clean available for this flat style, so I designed my own. As long as your unit shares the same outer dimensions for the air vent cover (which most of these OEM models do), this adapter will be compatible. It supports portable ACs from various manufacturers, including but not limited to: comfee TRONIC KINZO HOME DELUXE EUHOMY argo MEDION HANTECH (I will expand this list as I receive more feedback from the community. So far, it has been physically verified on Comfee, Argo, Tronic, Hantech and Kinzo devices). 👉 The most important step: Measure your existing intake air vent cover to ensure a match. It should be approximately 219 x 290 mm: 🌬️ Why use a 2-Hose Mod? Standard single-hose ACs push hot air out, creating a vacuum that constantly sucks warm air back into your room through cracks, doors, and walls—meaning you waste energy exhausting air you just cooled. This dual-hose mod fixes that. In my case, it cut both cooling time and energy consumption in half to reach the same room temperature. It's a massive boost to overall efficiency and performance! If you want more detail about this process I can recommend the Video form Technology Connection, explainigng all of it in detail: 🛠️ Materials Needed (BOM, just to connect the adapter to a 150mm hose) 1x 150mm Hose Clamp (Amazon) (you will need multiple) 1x 150mm flexible Hose (Amazon) 1x Outside air intake solution (e.g., my 3D-printed trough-pass connector for 150mm hose) My Setup & Material Tips I used this adapter with a 20mm XPS panel (you can get it easy at a local hardware store, online prices are crazy). which I lined with reflective radiator insulation foil (Amazon). and Aliminium Tape (Amazon). The whole setup cost me less than 10€ at my local hardware store . Also I used my 3D-printed trough-pass connector for the 150mm hose (for 0-60mm panels) You can easily cut XPS with a standard utility knife and simply glue 2 panels together if you have a bigger window. It is lightweight, stable, thermal isolating, completely opaque (light-tight), and seals beautifully, if you take some time to cut it to match your window. If you don't want to use XPS, this design easily adapts to plywood, acrylic, or any other window insert material you prefer. I highly recommend you isolate at least the exhaust site, to not have it act like a heater for the room. Here is a link for isolation (Amazon) , but just a old blanket will also do the trick, if you are on a budget. You find the step by step installation guide in the print profile off the pass-trough if you need more insight. 🖨️ Print & Material Options I highly recommend PETG for durability and easy of use. PLA works (since it should not get too hot) but isn't ideal. ABS/ASA is overkill, but totally okay. If possible, print it in one piece on a large build plate. For smaller printers (like the A1 mini), I have included split profiles. If you print the split version, just use superglue, tape, or plastic welding to fuse the parts together so the adapter stays completely airtight. you only need very small supports for the handle. The rest of the adapter prints without supports and I did not even need a brim. If you have problems with bed adhesion consider a bigger brim. For installation: Clean the brim off if you printed it with one. Then insert the 2 clips into the designated slots (mirrored to the printed guides). They should fit tighly and not come out easy, use some superglue if they are too loose. Swap your AC's stock vent cover with this adapter, connect your 150mm hose, and you are done! Mesh / Filer: If you don't plan to vacuum your radiator regularly I highly encourage the use of a filter. With the big version you can just continue using the original filter, but with some handy fingers you are able to shove the original filter also behind the slim version. For convenience and looks I also added a printable filter that fits perfectly inside the slim version. If you decide to print it, it is very important that your build plate is very clean and you do not use a cold plate, so it releases easy once cooled down. It relies on very fine lines on the first Layer, use the print profiles, the modifiers in the slicer are very important! Changelog: 2026-07-01: I added a printable mesh / filter for the slim version 2026-06-27: V2 - complete redesign 🚀- I realized there was some unused space under the old cover that wasn’t actually occupied air intake. It bugged me from the beginning that the first design was just a tad too big to fit on a single build plate for the X/P/A series printers. After running some prototypes, I managed to squeeze the footprint down just enough to fit mid-size build plates perfectly. This tighter design also allowed me to shrink the overall model, resulting in 50% faster print times and 50% less material - without sacrificing any functionality. A true success! Note: I will leave the old, larger V1 version online for anyone who prefers full coverage (for looks), or in case some AC models have a slightly different air intake design (though I believe most are identical). Also the A1 mini version is too flimsy if I split the Slim version the same way so A1 mini will keep the big version.

Description This model let's you make your own custom bookfinity books inside Bambu Studio. Just select a book size, change the text, and upload an image to make your custom book to store your stuff. This version is with the Latch to lock the book. If you want it without the latch and use just magnets, use this version here . What is Bookfinity? Bookfinity is a storage system that let's you store gridfinity stuff inside custom book shelf toolboxes. These look fantastic on a bookshelf and let's you grab your tools and components with ease. It's the most organised storage solution for any hobby. It consists of two parts: a bottom part which holds the part, and a top cover that includes the hinge. These two parts are aligned with the tabs and need superglue to attach together (Assembly Instructions below). How to use this Easy Edit Model? Step 1 - Select your book thickness Find the book size you want to edit. The 3MF files are organized by the bin height, eg 3U Books take 3U bins. Each profile has the following sizes: 2x2, 2x3, 3x3, 3x4, 3x5, 4x4, 4x5. Step 2 - Select your book Select your book size, and rotate the screen so you're looking underneath like this: Step 3 - Change to Objects On the left hand side, change the Process from Global to Objects. Step 4 - Click on your book Click on the book on the build bed, you'll see the text options on the left hand side. Step 5 - Select Edit Text Right click the main text and press “Edit Text”. A popup will appear Step 6 - Change the text Change the input text and you can change the size and move it around. (You can change the font too, but certain fonts don't print too well). Step 7a - Create an SVG (optional) There are many free SVGs online, and I've uploaded all of the SVGs I've used on Bookfinity on this model. If you need a custom one, you can use ChatGPT with the following prompt: “Create an image of an svg-style stencil with thick black lines of: ” and insert the name of the tool. Step 7b - Convert the PNG to SVG (optional) If you create a PNG, you'll need to convert it to an SVG. You can do it with a free site like FreeConvert. Step 8 - Insert the SVG Right click your book, press “Add Modifier” > “SVG”. TIP: if you insert your SVG, and it's just a rectangle this is because the SVG has an outline / border. This is wrong and won't work. If you generated the SVG using FreeConvert or similar, try change one of the options. on FreeConvert, I found if you go to Advanced Settings and change the "Color Mode" to “Black & White” and redownload it, it fixes this issue. Step 9 - Move, Scale and Rotate your SVG Using the Move, Scale and Rotate buttons, get your SVG where you need it. Step 10 - Set the depth of the SVG Firstly find your SVG on the menu on the left (remember to press “Objects” if you've gone off it). Right click it and press “Edit SVG”. A popup will appear. On the popup, set the Depth to 0.60mm and ensure the “From Surface” distance is 0.00mm. You can use “Use Surface” but it makes it invisible on the prepare tab so harder to use. Step 11 - Set the colour of your SVG On the left hand side, right click the SVG, press “Change Filament” and select the colour you wish to use, eg Black. Step 12: Enable Prime Tower Change Process back to "Global", then under the “Others” tab, find “Prime Tower” and select “Enable”. Move the prime tower so it doesn't clash with your model. This will make the books print much cleaner. Step 13 - Boost the model How to assemble a book Add superglue to the glue area shown below 2. Install the Bolts Install the latch using an M3 x 30mm Bolt, and an M3 Nyloc to the top cover. The nut should be at the top of the book. Install an M3 x 30mm bolt with an M3 Nyloc nut to the bottom cover. 3. Print a Gridfinity holder for your tool / stuff. If you're just looking for storage bins, these Simple Bins are guaranteed to fit. 4. Add Magnets (optional) Insert 4x D4 x 2mm magnets into the cover and base to make the books stay closed. These are available on the Bambu Shop, linked below. Notice a mistake? Got advice / requests? Please leave comments, or DM me (: Remember to also post photos of your books! Posting Remixes Yes! Upload your custom books as remixes for other people to help them out, get inspo and earn yourself some points! Use of AI Some of the SVGs used on the book covers were made using AI. The 3D model was made by human. The cover photo was made on PowerPoint, but an AI background remover tool was used. All other photos are real. Adjust your text, size, and thickness to create a perfect display piece for your desk, gaming setup, office, bedroom, events, or as a custom gift. ⭐ Key Features ⚙️ Fully Parametric Design The model automatically adapts to your custom text while maintaining balanced proportions and a strong structure. ✏️ Personalized Text Create your own: Names Gamer tags Room signs Event displays Custom messages Gifts 📏 Adjustable Size & Thickness Scale the sign to fit your space while keeping the design stable and visually balanced. 🖨️ 3MF Ready – Optimized for 3D Printing Prepared for easy printing with clean geometry and maker-friendly setup. 🎨 Color Customization Choose your own filament colors: Two-color swaps Contrasting text and base Premium silk PLA finishes 🚫 Support-Free Printing Designed for clean FDM printing without supports. 🧠 Design Details This is not just a simple text model. The parametric system rebuilds the sign based on your input: Text spacing is adjusted automatically Base length adapts to the text Structure stays balanced Geometry remains clean for printing Each personalized sign becomes a unique version of the design. 📏Here is a quick breakdown of all the parameters in the script, organized by their categories: 1. Global Settings Scale_factor : Multiplies the overall size of the entire model (e.g., 2 makes it twice as big). Center_Z_axis : If true, floats the model in mid-air (useful for viewing). Keep false for 3D printing so it sits flat on the bed. 2. Font Selection Selected_Font : Chooses the font style for your text. 3. Bold Settings Bold_Text : Turns on/off a thickening effect for the text. Bold_thickness : Controls how much extra thickness is added when Bold is turned on. 4. Main Text Settings Your_name : The actual word, name, or phrase you want to display. Font_size : The 2D visual size of the main text. Text_height : The 3D physical thickness (height) of the main text letters. 5. Backplate Settings Back_height : The 3D thickness of the solid base that holds the sign together. Border_size : Adds an extra solid outline/padding around the main text on the backplate. 6. Underline Options Show_underline : Toggles a decorative line underneath the main text. Underline_thickness : How thick the underline bar is. Underline_Gap : The empty vertical space between the bottom of the letters and the underline. Underline_extension : How far the underline sticks out past the left and right edges of the text. 7. Background Text Options Show_background_text : Toggles a large background letter or word (like a watermark behind the main text). Bg_text : The specific letter or word for the background (e.g., the first letter of a name). Bg_size : The visual size of the background text (usually much larger than the main text). Big_letter_height : The 3D thickness of the background text. Set to 0 to make it flat against the backplate. Bg_xy_space : Adds a thick outline/padding around the background text to make it chunkier. Bg_x_offset / Bg_y_offset : Moves the background text left/right and up/down to position it perfectly behind the main text. 8. Color Options Back_color : Sets the color for the base/backplate, the border, and the large background letter. Text_color : Sets the color for the main text and the underline. 🖨️ Print Settings Recommended: Layer height: 0.20 mm / 0.16 mm quality Walls: 2–3 Infill: 10–20% Supports: Not required Great results with color swaps to highlight the raised lettering. ❤️ Share Your Makes I love seeing what people create! This project is a parametric decorative Bubble Tray. Fully programmed in OpenSCAD, it features an elegant border made entirely of perfect spheres. The design utilizes a flawless vertical transition between the base and the spheres, eliminating any empty gaps or flat triangles at the absolute bottom (Z=0), ensuring an impeccable fusion finish. --- UNLIMITED CUSTOMIZATION --- The mathematical model automatically scales and calculates the entire distribution of spheres along the perimeter, ensuring accurate tangency and spacing regardless of the chosen length, width, or sphere radius. With support for 1 to 6 layers of stacked spheres, the combinations are virtually endless. --- PARAMETER GUIDE --- 1. Main Dimensions - Tray Length and Width: Defines the overall size of the round shape. - Base Thickness: Controls the height of the solid internal bottom plate. 2. Sphere Geometry (Advanced Settings) - Sphere Radius: Defines the diameter of the spheres and, consequently, the thickness of the outer wall. Change this to achieve anything from delicate small spheres to massive giant spheres. The model recalculates the required quantity automatically. - Height Ratio: Adjusts the height of the containment border relative to the sphere radius. - Overlap Factor (Penetration): Controls how much the spheres intersect each other laterally. The default (0.20) provides the optimal visual balance and structural strength. 3. Sphere Layers (Towering) - Number of Layers: Create anything from a simple flat tray (1 layer) to a deep basket-style tower with up to 10 perfectly stacked layers. - Vertical Overlap Factor: Controls the mathematical fusion between upper and lower layers (recommended: 0.40). 4. Customization and Details - Bottom Logo: A dedicated space to deboss your brand/logo on the smooth bottom face. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Clean Print Bed: Unlike other beaded models, this project's base is mathematically flat with no angular cuts on the spheres touching the build plate. - Support-Free Design: The sphere geometries are calculated to guarantee a progressive overhang angle easily handled by modern printers. No internal or external supports are required! - Premium Finish Tip: For a truly professional, textured clay or ceramic look, enable the "Fuzzy Skin" feature on the Outside walls only in your slicer! --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal for the vertical curves of the spheres) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Recommended for filling small fusions) - Infill: 10% Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Supports: No supports needed! - Fuzzy Skin (Optional for premium finish): Contour, Thickness: 0.3mm, Point distance: 0.8mm 💡 Pro Tip: Enable Variable/Adaptive Layer Height in your slicer.

📝 Project Description Overview Tired of fighting your dog every time you try to brush their teeth? This Dog Dental Care Mouth Prop is designed to safely and gently keep your dog's jaw propped open, allowing you to easily access and clean the hard-to-reach rear molars. Inspired by professional veterinary tools, it features a stable bite shelf and an ergonomic outer ring for a secure grip. 📏 Sizing & Customization Guide This model is fully customizable in all dimensions to fit any dog breed, from small terriers to extra-large retrievers. However, to get the perfect fit, you must measure your dog before printing: Muzzle Width: Measure the horizontal width of your dog's snout/jaw. Your print's inner opening needs to be slightly wider than this to clear their lips comfortably without pinching. Bite Height (Opening Gap): Check how wide your dog can comfortably open their mouth without overextending or straining their jaw joint. ⚠️ CRITICAL PRINT SETTINGS (For Safety & Strength) Dogs have immense jaw pressure. To ensure this tool does not crack, splinter, or break during use, do not use standard PLA and follow these specific slicer settings strictly: Material: PETG (Highly recommended for its flexibility and impact resistance. Unlike PLA, PETG deforms under high stress instead of shattering into sharp plastic shards). Wall Loops: 5 - 6 Top Shell Layers: 6 Bottom Shell Layers: 6 Infill Density: 60% Infill Pattern: Gyroid 🚨 Important Safety & Hygiene Disclaimer Bacteria Trap: FDM 3D prints have microscopic layer lines and can get scratched by sharp dog teeth. These tiny crevices can trap canine saliva and bacteria, making the raw print difficult to sanitize completely over time. Microplastics Risk: Sharp dog teeth scraping against raw, uncoated 3D-printed plastic can cause mechanical abrasion. This friction can shave off tiny microplastic particles that your pet might accidentally ingest during the brushing process. Post-Processing Recommendation: For long-term use and peace of mind, it is highly recommended to sand the printed part and coat it with a certified food-safe, high-strength epoxy resin. This seals the layer lines, blocks microplastic shedding, and creates a perfectly smooth, glassy, and washable surface. Alternative: If left raw, treat this as a short-term or limited-use item, check it constantly for signs of wear or shedding, and clean it thoroughly with pet-safe disinfectant after every single use. Never leave your dog unattended with this device.

description: Hallo guten Tag. Hiermit präsentiere ich euch die Pool Wasserfall/Düse Kombi, Komplett als 3D Druck. Wir wollten gerne einen Wasserfall im Pool haben, hatten aber keine Lust immer umzustecken, bzw. Wasserfall vom Rücklauf abmontieren, und die Düse wieder drauf zu montieren. Somit machte ich mich ans Werk, Vollständig 3D Druckbar und leicht umschaltbar von Düse auf Wasserfall ganz ohne lästiges Umstecken oder Abmontieren. Der Zusammenbau ist leicht verständlich, das Rohr wird in den Grundkorpus von oben eingesteckt bis es klickt. Somit ist das Rohr 360° drehbar. Der Wasserfall Aufsatz wird mit Gewinde ins Rohr eingeschraubt. Die Stellwelle wird so eingeschoben, dass das ovale Loch nach unten zeigt. Die Düsenseite ist leicht konisch, sie startet bei 25mm Durchmesser, und geht zum Schaft hin auf 26mm. Ich habe das Düsenloch ein wenig angepasst, um einen stärkeren Strahl zu generieren. Ich nutze eine Sandfilterpumpe von Steinbach, die Drückt ordentlich und liefert durch die Wasserfall/Düse Kombi ein starkes Ergebnis. Wenn die Düsenfunktion aktiviert ist, läuft aus dem Wasserfall minimal Wasser raus, da alles ohne O-Ringe funktioniert. das Stört aber nicht, und ist wirklich minimal. description: Inventum AC701 Secondary Intake Hose Adapter / Dual Hose Conversion This is an air duct adapter for the Inventum AC701 portable air conditioner. It allows you to add a secondary intake hose to the rear intake side of the unit. Single-hose portable air conditioners exhaust hot air outside. Because that exhausted air has to be replaced somehow, the room can become slightly negatively pressurized and pull warm outside air back in through gaps, doors, vents, and window seals. This adapter is intended to reduce that effect by allowing the AC unit to draw condenser/intake air through a second hose instead of constantly pulling already-cooled room air. This is not an official Inventum part. Included versions There are three hose-size versions: - 125 mm version — for hoses with approximately 125 mm inner diameter - 145 mm version — for hoses with approximately 145 mm inner diameter - 150 mm version — for hoses with approximately 150 mm inner diameter The listed diameter is the outside diameter of the printed hose connection spigot, intended to match the inside diameter of the hose. Compatibility Designed for: - Inventum AC701 It may fit similar Inventum units, but I have only tested/designed it for the AC701. Recommended material Print this in ABS. The part sits close to a portable AC unit and may be exposed to warm air, sunlight near a window, and higher temperatures than normal indoor prints. For that reason I do **not** recommend PLA. ASA should also work if you prefer it, but ABS is the recommended material. Installation notes - Mount the adapter over the rear intake grille as shown in the photos. - Use a hose size matching the printed version. - Keep the hose as short and straight as practical. - Avoid sharp bends or restrictions. - Make sure the original exhaust hose is still properly routed outside. - Keep intake and exhaust hose openings separated outside so the AC does not pull its own hot exhaust air back in. - After first use, check that the AC still has good airflow and that the printed part does not become too hot. Safety / disclaimer Use at your own risk. This is a modification to the airflow path of the AC unit. Do not block the exhaust, do not restrict airflow, and monitor the unit during the first test run. Stop using the adapter if the AC behaves abnormally, overheats, gives errors, or airflow seems restricted.

It works entirely on hydrodynamics—using the static angles of the blades to spin the incoming water flow.
