description: Looking for a reliable self-watering semi-hydro system for Alocasias, Anthuriums, and small Philodendrons? This fully waterproof modular planter system is built around a universal 0.5L disposable plastic cup. Designed for fast, lightweight printing, it combines a wick-based inner pot with a decorative outer pot. A complete setup weighs only about 70 grams and prints in just 2–2.5 hours. The outer pot is available in 14 unique designs. All photos show real prints—no renders here UPDATE 04.07.2026. For US users, the outer pot is also compatible with a standard 16 oz disposable plastic cup. For comparison, height / internal diameter: * The outer pot has a minimum internal diameter of 100 mm; it can be slightly larger depending on the design. Since the 16 oz cup is slightly shorter, I have included two printable spacer inserts (10 mm and 20 mm tall). Simply place one in the outer pot to raise the reservoir cup to the desired height. The inserts are located in the inner pot print profile. If you would like a little more clearance between the top of the cup and the outer pot, you can scale the outer pot by 3% in the X and Y axes in your slicer. This increases the internal diameter while preserving the intended 2-wall construction. I will add a separate, shorter inner pot for the 16 oz cup, working on it… ### ### ### Many similar models rely on a fully 3D-printed water reservoir. While they can work well, achieving a waterproof print requires specialized print settings and a fully calibrated printer, a lot of filament (many walls), and significantly longer print times. Even then, a completely leak-free result cannot always be guaranteed. So why bother when universal 0.5L disposable plastic cups are widely available with almost no cost? Instead of relying on a printed reservoir, this design uses a standard 0.5L disposable plastic cup as the water reservoir. The result is a lightweight, low-cost, reliable, and fully leak-proof planter system that minimizes both print time and filament usage. The inner planter pot is compatible with all common semi-hydro growing media, including Pon, LECA, Fluval Stratum, perlite , and similar substrates. The setup consists of: Printed inner pot 0.5L disposable plastic cup as the water reservoir Printed decorative outer pot A. Inner Pot Volume: approximately 420 ml Reservoir capacity: approximately 120 ml of nutrient solution Two wick holes A tested single-wall design, https://makerworld.com/en/models/2153264-self-watering-alocasia-propagation-cup-with-wick Weight: 13 g, print time: 30 minutes (with printer calibration) Has two large ventilation openings for improved airflow and healthier root development. The ventilation openings can also be used to refill the reservoir without removing the inner pot (I use a large syringe for this purpose), and can be used for the convenient inner pot removal B. Reservoir For the reservoir, a standard European 0.5L disposable plastic cup is used. The size for the reference is: height 145 mm, bottom diameter 60 mm, top diameter 95 mm. C. Decorative Outer Pot The decorative outer pot conceals the plastic cup while maintaining a lightweight and efficient design. Unlike many decorative pots/planters, this design is optimized for low filament usage and fast printing without sacrificing strength or appearance. It features: Double-wall construction for fast printing and low filament usage Weight: 55–65 g, depending on the design Print time: 2–2.5 hours, depending on the design No supports required Cutouts for convenient reservoir removal Currently, there are 14 decorative pot designs available. All versions were designed to print without supports, have been fully tested, and are currently used with Alocasia plants. ( I have more designs ready to share, but first I’d love to see whether this project interests the community. ) Printing Notes Inner Pot PETG is strongly recommended for the inner pot due to its flexibility and superior layer adhesion compared to PLA. I also recommend printing the inner pot in transparent filament to monitor root development and health. Alternatively, transparent and opaque filaments can be combined to match the outer pot color while still allowing root observation (see photos). Outer Pot The outer pot can be printed at a 0.24 mm layer height for faster printing. If your printer struggles with the bottom overhangs, consider printing the first 5 mm at a 0.20 mm layer height. The outer pot can be printed with any filament. I used PLA. A non-transparent filament is recommended to block light and prevent algae growth in the reservoir. For planters placed in direct sunlight, avoid very dark colors to minimize water and substrate heating and potential PLA softening. Filament Usage A complete setup consisting of the plain decorative pot and inner pot requires only approximately 70-80 g of filament and prints in 2–2.5 hours. description: BONBON Capsule Cooling Surprise | Mini Ice Pack + Real Reward Concept A slim reusable refillable ice pack concept designed for cooler bags, lunch boxes, camping, travel, outdoor family use, and simple DIY summer cooling setups. BONBON contest concept This entry is designed as a capsule surprise idea with two versions: a mini capsule-size version that fits inside the BONBON capsule as the surprise item a larger real-size version that can be used as a practical reusable ice pack The mini version represents the small capsule surprise, while the larger version shows the real functional cooling product that the surprise can unlock, represent, or be redeemed for. Important Capsule Fit Note This model is designed for the BONBON 2.7-inch capsule contest. https://makerworld.com/uk/models/2566374-bonbon-2-7-inch-capsule-content-checker The capsule checker shown in the photos was taken from the contest host/creator’s MakerWorld profile and used to test the model size. The model was checked inside the contest-size checker to confirm the fit. How to use Fill it partly with water, leave enough empty space for ice expansion, freeze it, and use it as a flat cooling block. The slim rounded shape makes it easy to place inside a cooler bag, lunch bag, backpack pocket, or near small DIY cooling setups where a flatter ice pack is more convenient than a bulky block. This design uses a recessed filling area and a separate cap, helping keep the overall shape compact and easy to handle. The ice pack uses an internal honeycomb-style structure to help divide the water volume into smaller sections and support the flat walls during freezing. This helps reduce deformation and stress from ice expansion while keeping the model slim and lightweight. Important Do not fill completely. Water expands when frozen. Always leave empty space inside before freezing. The internal structure does not mean the model can be filled completely. It only helps support the shape and divide the water volume. This is a 3D printed container, so always test for leaks before using it near electronics, food, bags, or temperature-sensitive items. Leak / material preparation note Possible leaks are not automatically caused by the model design. This is a functional 3D printed container, so water-tightness depends heavily on the material, printer condition, slicer settings, and calibration. Before using the ice pack, make sure your filament is properly dried, especially PETG, and that your printer is calibrated for that exact material. Incorrect flow, too high or too low temperature, poor layer bonding, wet filament, under-extrusion, weak walls, dirty nozzle, or modified print settings can all cause leaks. For better sealing, print slowly, use enough walls and top/bottom layers, check extrusion and flow calibration, and make sure the cap and filling area are printed cleanly. Always perform a leak test before freezing or using the model in a bag, near electronics, near food, or near temperature-sensitive items. Recommended print settings PETG or PLA Tough Plus recommended 0.2 mm layer height 4–5 walls recommended for freezer use 25–40% infill 5–6 top/bottom layers Print slowly for better layer bonding Dry filament before printing, especially PETG Calibrate flow/extrusion for your material Use a clean build plate Make sure the cap and filling area are printed cleanly before use Leak test before freezing or daily use Use ideas Cooler bags Lunch bags Camping Travel Outdoor summer use Picnics Road trips DIY fan cooling setups Small cooling box setups Safety note This is a 3D printed functional prototype, not a certified food-contact or medical cooling product. Create high-quality custom trays for gifts, organization, or home decor. This project was developed to offer maximum flexibility: simply adjust the dimensions, and the script seamlessly recalculates the heart border distribution, maintaining a flawless geometry designed for support-free 3D printing. Perfect for both personal use and the production of unique, exclusive pieces. --- CUSTOMIZATION --- The model is designed so that any user can configure it quickly, with the number of hearts being automatically calculated to fill the entire perimeter! 1. Basic Settings - Tray Length & Width: Maximum exterior dimensions of the tray (mm). - Base Thickness: Thickness of the base along the Z-axis. - Cut Inner Hearts: Enables boolean subtraction to remove the inner portion of the hearts, yielding a smooth interior wall. - Alternating Layers: Enables horizontal offset (half-step) on even layers, aligning geometry in a brick pattern. - Number of Layers: Quantity of heart rings stacked along the Z-axis. - Heart Base Size: Size of the heart (mm). The script recalculates the perimeter and automatically adjusts the instance count. 2. Engraving & Text Settings - Enable Top Text: Adds embossed (raised) text to the center of the base's top face. - Enable Bottom Logo: Adds debossed (engraved) text to the base's bottom face. 3. Advanced Settings For users who want fine-grained control over mesh and placement: - Heart Width / Thickness / Height Ratio: Individual scale of the heart on its local X, Y, and Z axes. - Heart Size Multiplier: Global scale (XYZ) applied to the heart. - Heart Facing Rotation: Angular rotation (local Z-axis) of each heart at its origin. - Heart Z Offset: Z-axis displacement of the heart layers. Negative values intersect with Z=0 (cut plane), generating a flat bed adhesion area. - Heart Radial Offset: Radial displacement of the anchor line. Negative values increase volumetric intersection with the base. - Lateral and Vertical Overlap Factor: Interpenetration rate between adjacent instances. --- TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & PRINTING --- - Clean Printing Base: The parametric bottom is cut perfectly flat on the Z-axis, ensuring maximum bed adhesion without the fragility of the heart tips. - Support-Free: The design ensures progressive overhangs without the need for any supports in FDM printing. - Premium Finish Tip: For a wonderful textured ceramic look, enable the "Fuzzy Skin" option on the outer contour in your slicer! RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal for the vertical curves of the spheres) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Recommended for filling small fusions) - Infill: 10% Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Supports: No supports needed! - Fuzzy Skin (Optional for premium finish): Contour, Thickness: 0.3mm, Point distance: 0.8mm 💡 Pro Tip: Enable Variable/Adaptive Layer Height in your slicer.

description: # 🌿 Begonie Maculata aka Polka Dot Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Without a limit stopper on the end of the blind cord, the cord will swing wildly when windows are opened for ventilation. It easily tangles with curtain tracks and window frames, and even poses entanglement risks for kids. This model targets this pain point, firmly locking the cord end and fundamentally restricting large-range swinging of the pull cord. Upgrade Highlight: Threaded Lock Mounting Mechanism The original version adopted an integrated snap-fit structure, which was hard to install & remove and prone to loosening after long-term pulling. This new upgraded split threaded locking system consists of a textured anti-slip knob and pulley bracket. For installation: Thread the cord through the pulley then tighten the knob. The threaded structure delivers even, stable clamping force. To detach, simply twist the knob counterclockwise without forcing or damaging the part—easy enough for elderly users to operate independently. Granular anti-slip texture is added to the thread contact surface to prevent slipping even with damp hands, and the threads resist stripping after repeated long-term use. Hollow Triangular Lightweight Bracket: Large hollow cutouts drastically reduce filament consumption and shorten print time, while the triangular mechanical frame maintains structural rigidity to avoid cracking under daily tension. 2. Integrated Smooth Pulley Groove: Rounded inner slot protects the pull cord from sharp edges, reducing abrasion and extending the service life of nylon blind cords. 3. Support-Free Printing Geometry: No complex overhangs across the whole model. It can be printed directly on consumer FDM 3D printers without extra support structures, lowering print failure rates. Standard PLA filament provides sufficient strength for indoor long-term use, with good heat and aging resistance. Compatibility Fits most standard woven nylon pull cords for household roller blinds. Tolerance is reserved in the design, so cords with minor thickness differences can be securely clamped. Please note that the structural grip in this V1 isn't perfect, precisely because the thin walls required for illumination make it tricky to design robust joints at this scale. 🛠️ Assembly Instructions Before starting: If you feel you need glue, use it! If you don't plan on taking the rocket apart, gluing is the best option. 🧴 Joystick: Assemble the joystick background together with its buttons. 🕹️ Wiring: Remove the power cable from the levitation kit's motherboard, but leave the mini-board (touch button) connected. ⚡ Power plug: Insert the power plug into the back cover (as shown in the photo) and route it upwards through the internal hole. If you swipe your finger on the outside of that area, the button will activate when the UFO is levitating on the base! 👆💡 Base: Assemble the walls to the base of the rocket (glue is recommended). 🏗️ Floor: Next, cover the magnetic base with the floor piece you decided to print ( DO NOT GLUE THIS PART! ). 🚫🧴 Claw: If the tolerance is too loose, you can glue the claw to the top of the rocket; otherwise, just snap it into place. Leave the light on top and cover it with the cap so it doesn't move. 💡 Drop the top shell onto the bottom one, adjust it slightly, and you're done! I’ll try to create an improved V2 later. 🔄 FOR NON-AMS ONLY: You will need a tiny drop of glue for both the floor and the windows. Be careful, I know it can be a bit tricky! 🤏 🎯 Final Setup Once everything is assembled, carefully lower the UFO right in the center, as close to the claw as possible. You'll hear a characteristic sound when it locks into the levitation point. Then, just place your favorite mini-figure on top!!! 🤠👾 I have created quite a few of them » HERE « , take a look and print whichever ones you like! 🖨️ ✨I hope you all like it! 🦖 Best regards. 🟢Don't forget you can follow me on Instagram as @Jotas3D ^^ 📸 ⚠️ » HERE « for Toy Story Logo ⚠️

description: 🔠 Customizable Text / Name Sign Generator — Precision‑Built Typographic Display System The Text / Name Sign Generator transforms any letter and name combination into a clean, sculptural display piece. Name Size — Size of the engraved name. Name Height — Raised height for multicolor printing. Engraving Depth — Depth of the carved name. 📐 Position & Rotation Name X Offset — Horizontal placement of the name. Name Y Offset — Vertical placement of the name. Name Rotation — Rotates the engraved name. Letter Rotation — Rotates the main letter independently. 🖼️ Name Border Enable Name Border — Turns the border on or off. description: Schluss mit Schmutz am Poolboden! Wer einen Bestway Lay-Z-Spa besitzt, kennt das Problem: Sand, kleine Blätter und Schmutz sammeln sich unweigerlich am Boden, und die integrierte Pumpe schafft es nicht, diesen gezielt zu entfernen. Dieses funktionale Modul löst das Problem elegant und einfach. Es verwandelt die Standard-Ansaugdüse deines Pools in einen effektiven Bodensauger. Das Modul auf die Ansaugdüse stecken (der Unterdruck fixiert es sofort). Den Poolboden mit dem Schlauch absaugen. Die Story hinter dem Design – Vom "Fail" zum Feature! Eigentlich war der Plan ein ganz anderer: Ich wollte den Adapter ursprünglich mit einem passenden Gewinde versehen, um ihn fest auf die Düse aufzuschrauben. Da es aber verdammt schwer war, die exakten Spezifikationen des Pool-Gewindes zu finden (und ich beim Abmessen wohl auch ein wenig zu doof war...), passte das gedruckte Gewinde hinten und vorne nicht. Kurz geärgert, kurz nachgedacht – und festgestellt: It’s not a bug, it’s a feature! Das mühsame Auf- und Abschrauben im Wasser bei jedem Reinigungszyklus wäre viel zu umständlich gewesen. Die neue, gewindelose Version wird jetzt einfach nur noch über den Einlass geschoben. Durch den Unterdruck der Pumpe saugt sich das Modul bombenfest an und lässt sich nach der Reinigung sekundenschnell wieder abnehmen. Schneller und einfacher geht es nicht! Geniales Plug & Play: Das Modul wird bei laufender Pumpe einfach auf die Ansaugdüse im Pool gesteckt. Der Unterdruck der Pumpe saugt das Teil fest an und hält es sicher in Position – ganz ohne Schrauben oder Klemmen. Integrierter Schmutzfang: Im Inneren des Adapters ist exakt Platz für ein handelsübliches Filterbällchen (z. B. von Steinbach). Dieses fängt den aufgesaugten Schmutz direkt auf, bevor er überhaupt in die Pumpe oder den Hauptfilter gelangen kann. Das Filterbällchen kann danach einfach ausgewaschen werden. Universeller Anschluss: Das Modul verfügt über einen 1-Zoll-Anschluss. Hier kann ein Standard-Gartenschlauch (z. B. mit Gardena-Kupplung) aufgesteckt werden. Mit dem freien Ende des Schlauchs kannst du nun bequem den gesamten Poolboden absaugen. description: Eliminator Updated to Version 1.1 - July 6th, 2026 Please note I have updated the trap version to V1.1. Occasionally I will be providing updates and improvements to the Earwig Eliminator and these will be uploaded in the form of versions (V1.1, V1.2 etc). These will include mostly minor feature additions and geometry changes to ensure maximum success rate based on my testing and public feedback. Changes for V1.1: Addition of grip indents for making lid opening easier, Geometry changes to add additional entrance paths, Geometry changes to lower the bait station and slightly raise entrance holes, Addition of “Water Reservoir” to provide the option of increasing humidity inside the trap. ______________________________________________________________________ The Earwig Eliminator is a reusable, poison free, bait-style trap designed to help control earwigs around patios, gardens, planters, sheds, foundations, and outdoor living areas. The trap uses 13 entrance tunnels and a bait station to lure earwigs inside, where they fall into the surrounding moat. This trap is a surface level take on the traditional oil/soya sauce trap with out the mess of an open tray or container. The secure screw-on lid helps protect the contents from rain, spills, pets, and accidental tampering while still allowing earwigs to enter through the outer tunnels. Its low-profile round design makes it easy to place discreetly in problem areas. Tips for Success: Experimenting with baits is key to using this trap effectively. I recommend Vegetable oil in the moat with Soya Sauce in the secondary bait cup as a starting point. The vegetable oil both acts as a bait and also ensures nothing can get out of the moat. Also being virtually clear, its easy to see if you’ve got any visitors. Oil from a can of Sardines is also extremely effective in my experience. I am currently testing the moat dry for effectiveness, but I don’t currently recommend using it this way. Baits can be interchange or experimented with as you see fit, these traps require some experiementation but once you find what works they are highly effective! ** After testing, I have had excellent luck with a dry moat and Sardine oil in the center bait station. I f using this method, be sure to open the trap over a bucket or Rubbermaid container with water and few drops of dish soap. You will want to immediately dump your catch in to the bucket. Without oil in the moat the earwigs will be alive, this trap is not escape proof without the oil in the moat so be prepared when opening! I also advise using gloves (latex or gardening). The GIF in the picture roll is a dry moat with sardine oil in the cup. With or without oil, these traps can still attract ants depending on your bait. If this happens, I suggest adding ant-specific bait traps near your earwig eliminator. While you will catch hundreds in the moat once they try to get to the bait in the cup, the ant baits kill the colony at the source which is needed to completely resolve the ant problem. Ant-Bait refills can also be easily found and placed in your bait cup, the first ants will drown in the moat and the survives will carry the poison bait back to the colony. If catch is slow, moving the traps around occasionally can be helpful. Be sure to try all sorts of areas if needed. The traps can be washed with soap and water, although earwigs are attracted to scents and pheromones from other earwig’s waste, the dirtier it gets the better it attracts more earwigs (does not factor as much if using oil filled moat). V1.1 Incorporates a “Water Reservoir” around the top rim. Earwigs like damp, high humidity places. If you feel your trap is going to be in a dry place, consider experimenting with a bit of water in this Reservoir before screwing on the lid. This will evaporate making the trap more attractive to earwigs. * PLA will warp in direct sunlight. It will also heat up and be very unattractive to earwigs if you leave it in a full sun location. Earwigs like cool, damp and dark spaces. Try to find areas which are not exposed to direct sunlight such as garden beds, under patio furniture, near deck walls etc. If some heat-sunlight is anticipated, consider printing in ASA or ASA-CF. This trap has significantly helped control our earwig population which for the last few years has been out of control. Would love to see what people are using as effective baits. Always welcome feedback and if you have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out. Simple, reusable, and made to target earwigs where they hide.

Quindi se lo ingrandite sugli assi x e y tenete attiva la funzione “Scala uniforme”, dopodiché per variare lo spessore, togliete il flag da “Scala uniforme” ed agite solo sul valore dell’asse z che imposterete ai millimetri desiderati (io ho messo 2 mm e va benissimo). Inoltre consiglio di fare le calibrazioni del flusso dinamico e del flaw rate previste in bambu studio. Personalmente prima delle stampe asciugo il PLA con AMS 2 PRO per circa 1 oretta. Sono questi piccoli accorgimenti, insieme a tanti altri, che determinano la riuscita di una bella stampa . Prima di mettere giudizi negativi, cortesemente regolate questi parametri. Se avete difficoltà o continuate a riscontrare problemi non esitate a contattarmi, cerchiamo insieme le soluzioni in un perfetto clima collaborativo. description: Does your cat loudly demand food the moment you leave for work? Or is it quite the opposite- eating everything at once and overeating when you leave a full bowl for the whole day? The solution is simpler than you think! 🐱 Meet CR Pet Feeder - a smart, automatic feeder that you can build yourself in just one afternoon. No soldering and no complicated coding required. With a dedicated Android application, you can dispense meals and control your pet's diet from anywhere on Earth. Download the manual, gather the simple parts, and set up a healthy feeding schedule for your cat today! 🐾 🐾 About the CR Pet Feeder Project You can find many automatic pet feeder projects online, but this project was created to address their biggest limitations. Here is what makes it unique: Dedicated Android App: I created a custom Android application. Unlike most DIY projects that only work on a local home network, this app allows you to fully control the feeder from anywhere in the world. Extremely Simple Assembly: The project is designed so that anyone can easily build it. You don't need any soldering skills. The only electronics required are an ESP32 board and a single MG996R servo motor. Effortless Programming: Forget about installing IDEs or writing code. Flashing the precompiled firmware to the ESP32 is done with a single click directly from your web browser (see instructions for details). 📱 App & Feeder Features: Feeding Schedule: Set automatic feeding times at specific hours. Manual Feeding: Instantly dispense a portion with a single tap in the app. Feeding History: View logs so you always know exactly if and when a meal was successfully dispensed. Supported Languages: The application is fully localized in Polish and English. ⚠️ Important Safety Instructions: I personally tested this device for some time and it worked flawlessly, but mechanical devices and Wi-Fi networks can be unpredictable. Food jams, power outages, or temporary internet connection losses can always happen. For this reason, the food hopper has been deliberately designed to be reasonably compact. This device is meant to conveniently feed your pet during the day (e.g., when you are at work), but I strongly advise against leaving your pet alone with it for more than 1 day, and absolutely not during a long vacation. Safety first! 3D Printing Tip: For printing components that come into direct contact with pet food, I highly recommend using food-safe filaments, such as Bambu Lab PLA Pure .

description: Check out my newly released models: Product Description Meet the Self-Locking Towel Holder — a minimalist, wall-mounted accessory that keeps your towel exactly where you want it, using nothing but gravity and a clever internal ball mechanism. No hooks to snag on, no clips to fiddle with, no adhesives on the fabric. Just push the towel in, and it holds itself. How It Works Inside the arched body sits a free-rolling ball housed in a tapered channel. The mechanism works in three intuitive steps: Insert — Push the edge of the towel upward into the slot from below. The ball lifts out of the way, letting the fabric pass through easily. Lock — As soon as you let go, the towel naturally pulls downward. The ball rolls down with it and wedges the fabric against the tapered wall of the channel, gripping it firmly. The harder the towel pulls, the tighter the hold. Release — To remove the towel, simply pull it sideways (horizontally) instead of down. This motion disengages the ball from the wedge zone, instantly releasing the fabric with zero effort. It's a purely mechanical, gravity-driven design — no springs, no magnets, no moving parts to wear out beyond a single ball. Key Features 🪝 One-handed operation — insert and release with a single motion 🎨 Warm brown finish — pairs beautifully with neutral, Japandi, or earth-tone bathroom interiors 🧺 Universal fit — works with hand towels, tea towels, dish cloths, and thin bath towels 🌊 Bathroom & kitchen ready — great next to the sink, shower, or by the stove 🔩 Minimal footprint — the compact arched profile takes up almost no wall space 🛠️ Easy install — double-sided tape Why You'll Love It No more towels sliding off hooks or bunching up on bars. This holder embraces the beauty of simple physics — the more your towel wants to fall, the more securely it stays. A tiny piece of engineering that quietly does its job, every single day.

First iteration of the Dubia Roach Vertical Habitat. Each complete set comes with 8 Roach Plates and 3 Roach Bridges to hold everything together into a 166x150x200mm (L*W*H) cuboid structure. The material I use is PLA basic/matte. The Challenge: Traditional Roach Housing Issues Conventional roach enclosures frequently become unsanitary and prone to fruit fly infestations. Because dubia roaches generate significant moisture through waste and regurgitation, standard cardboard egg crates quickly degrade. They soften, get consumed by the roaches, lose their structural integrity, and collapse into a messy heap at the bottom of the bin. This structural breakdown makes sorting the insects incredibly difficult and turns routine colony maintenance into a major hassle. The Solution: An Optimized, Reusable Habitat This innovative design prioritizes the safety and comfort of your roach colony while maximizing practical management. Smart Vertical Design: The vertical orientation allows waste (frass) to drop to the floor effortlessly, while the ribbed texture gives nymphs and adults of all sizes plenty of grip to navigate the structure. Elevated Base "Legs": Specially designed legs lift the structure above the accumulating debris at the bottom. This prevents the roaches from being crushed under the weight of a heavily populated habitat. Effortless Maintenance & Sorting: The flat plates make harvesting simple—just a quick tap easily dislodges the roaches into sorting buckets. Moisture & Pest Control: Enhanced spacing prevents the damp microclimates common in cardboard setups, drastically reducing fruit fly outbreaks. Built to Last: Made from durable, non-absorbent materials, the entire unit can be easily washed with warm, soapy water and reused indefinitely. Note: Each plate takes roughly 45.5g (0.0098 gallons, for the Americans) of material and over 1 hour 45 minutes to complete. The Bridges are about 4g (or 0.0034 quarts) each and takes about 13 minutes to complete. This means one complete structure requires 376g (or 0.678 pints) of filament and at least 14 hours to complete. Do NOT use any settings other than 2 walls or the joints will be too loose or too tight!

I've been growing herbs and strawberries in hydroponic towers at home for a long time. So I decided to develop my own design that eliminated these drawbacks. I combined NFT hydroponics and a traditional tower to create a spiral plant nutrition system. I also designed the tower for corner installation so it would take up a quarter of the space of a traditional circular tower. I also added many improvements, which I detailed in my YouTube video: For assembly, you will need: 1) a water tank. description: Based on the previous design, I made a larger version. The total blade height is now 360mm with a 70-degree twist. Printing blades: Clean your build plate before printing! Do not print if you have poor bed adhesion. You can print just one piece of the blade for a test. If your turbine isn't spinning well despite strong winds, please keep in mind how vertical axis wind turbines actually work: Location is everything: Mount it as high as possible in a wide-open space. Walls, roofs, and trees deflect the air and create turbulent "dead zones." Steady wind over strong wind: VAWTs need constant, laminar (smooth) airflow to build up momentum. Gusty, chaotic wind constantly disrupts the rotation. Hurricanes act as a brake: Surprisingly, extremely strong and turbulent wind can actually stop a VAWT! The chaotic air hits the blades from the wrong angles, destroying the aerodynamic lift and acting as a massive brake instead of pushing it forward ( I've noticed on my own that a lighter, steady wind works best ). Remember to mount it perfectly level. Hardware & Assembly: To assemble this project, you will need: 17x M3x6mm screws 2x 608ZZ ball bearings Note on tolerances: I designed the bearing housings with a very tight tolerance (essentially zero clearance). This works perfectly for my setup the bearings press-fit with an ideal amount of friction and hold very securely. I will try to include a slicer modifier so you can easily adjust the tolerance to fit your printer's calibration. Mounting: As is standard with my previous projects, the base includes a mounting hole, designed this time for a 25mm pipe or pole. Aerodynamics: The airfoil profile used for the blades is the symmetric NACA 0015. Assembly instructions are included in the attached PDF file.

Trotec PAC 2010 E Abluftadapter fürs Fenster – 142 mm / 150 mm Bajonett-System Dies ist ein Abluftadapter-System für die mobile Klimaanlage Trotec PAC 2010 E . Ich habe das Modell entwickelt, um die übliche Stoff-Fensterabdichtung durch eine stabilere und sauberere Lösung zu ersetzen. Als Fenstereinsatz verwende ich eine 6 mm Stegplatte / Hohlkammerplatte aus Polycarbonat . Das System besteht aus einer festen Basis an der Fensterplatte und wechselbaren Bajonett-Aufsätzen. Dadurch kann der Fenstereinsatz montiert bleiben, während man den Schlauchadapter oder den Verschlussdeckel später einfach wechseln kann. Kurze Bauteilübersicht Teil A – Innenflansch mit universellem Bajonettverschluss Teil A ist die feste Basis auf der Innenseite der Stegplatte. Es bleibt dauerhaft am Fenstereinsatz montiert und enthält die universelle Bajonettaufnahme. Die Teile B142, B150 und D passen alle in diesen Bajonettverschluss. Zusätzlich ist ein offenes Gitter integriert, damit Katzen nicht durch die Öffnung entkommen können, wenn kein Schlauch montiert ist. Teil B142 – Adapter für den originalen Trotec-Schlauch Teil B142 ist der Adapter für den originalen Abluftschlauch des Trotec PAC 2010 E. Der Schlauch hat bei mir ca. 142 mm Außendurchmesser über den Rillen . Diese Version habe ich selbst gedruckt und getestet. Der Schlauch wird in das gedruckte Innengewinde eingedreht. Teil B150 – Optionaler Adapter für 150-mm-Schlauch Teil B150 ist eine alternative Version für einen 150-mm-Abluftschlauch. Der Bajonettanschluss ist identisch zu B142 und passt daher ebenfalls in Teil A. Diese Version ist im Modell enthalten, wurde von mir aber noch nicht selbst gedruckt oder getestet . Bitte vor dem Druck unbedingt den echten Schlauchdurchmesser messen, da viele 150-mm-Schläuche die 150 mm als Nennmaß oder Innendurchmesser angeben. Teil C – Außen-Gegenring Teil C sitzt auf der Außenseite der Stegplatte. Teil A und Teil C werden durch die 6-mm-Steegplatte miteinander verschraubt und klemmen die Platte zwischen sich ein. Teil C hat ebenfalls ein offenes Gitter und Taschen für M3-Muttern. Teil D – Verschlussdeckel / Winterdeckel Teil D ist der abnehmbare Deckel für den Bajonettverschluss, wenn kein Abluftschlauch angeschlossen ist. Er nutzt denselben Bajonettanschluss wie die Schlauchadapter. Die Mitte ist geschlossen und der Deckel hat einen größeren Griff, damit man ihn besser drehen und entfernen kann. Getestete Version Ich habe persönlich die Version B142 für den originalen Trotec-Schlauch gedruckt und getestet. Gemessene Schlauchmaße des originalen Trotec-Schlauchs: Außendurchmesser über den Rillen: ca. 142 mm Innendurchmesser: ca. 128 mm Rillenabstand / Pitch: ca. 10 mm Die B150-Version ist zusätzlich enthalten, wurde von mir aber noch nicht getestet. Warum ein Gitter integriert ist In Teil A und Teil C ist ein offenes Gitter integriert. Das Gitter dient vor allem als einfache Sicherheit, falls der Schlauch nicht montiert ist. So können Katzen nicht einfach durch die Öffnung nach draußen gelangen. Das Gitter ist bewusst relativ offen gehalten, damit der Luftstrom der Klimaanlage möglichst wenig behindert wird. Verwendetes Material Ich habe die Teile mit folgendem Material gedruckt: Bambu Lab PETG HF Farbe: Weiß Ich empfehle PETG oder ein anderes temperaturbeständigeres Material. PLA würde ich nicht empfehlen, da der Abluftschlauch und der Bereich am Fenster warm werden können. Verwendete Schrauben und Muttern Zur Befestigung von Teil A und Teil C an der Stegplatte habe ich verwendet: M3-Schrauben M3-Muttern Die gedruckten Teile haben Taschen für M3-Muttern. Ich habe die Muttern mit 3D-Drucker-Kleber in die Taschen eingeklebt. Das hat bei mir sehr gut funktioniert. Fenstereinsatz / Stegplatte Als Fenstereinsatz habe ich eine Stegplatte von Bauhaus verwendet: Bauhaus Hohlkammerplatte ECO UV https://www.bauhaus.info/hohlkammerplatten/hohlkammerplatte-eco-uv/p/28541981 Die gekaufte Platte hatte folgende Maße: 2000 × 980 mm 6 mm Dicke Ich habe die Platte passend für mein Fenster zugeschnitten. Meine fertige Fensterplatte hatte ungefähr folgende Maße: 1460 mm Höhe 860 mm Breite 6 mm Dicke Montagehinweise Stegplatte passend für das Fenster zuschneiden. Die M3-Muttern bei Bedarf mit etwas 3D-Drucker-Kleber, Sekundenkleber oder einem geeigneten Kunststoffkleber in den Taschen fixieren. Ich habe die Muttern eingeklebt, damit sie bei der Montage nicht herausfallen. Das hat bei mir sehr gut funktioniert. Teil A auf der Innenseite der Platte einsetzen. description: Midea Portasplit Window Adapter – Guide Rail Mount for External Blinds This adapter is designed to be inserted directly into the guide rails of external blinds (Raffstore). A simple mechanism that automatically opens the trash bin lid when you open or pull out the cabinet. The string is attached to the moving cabinet front, door, or drawer. As the cabinet opens, the string becomes tensioned and pulls the hook mounted on the trash bin lid, lifting it automatically. When the cabinet closes, the lid returns to its normal position. This model was designed for an IKEA cabinet and a trash bin with a similar lid design, but it can also be adapted to other bins and cabinets with comparable construction. Attach the second hook to the fixed upper or side section of the cabinet using double-sided tape. Loop the cord over the hooks. !!!! When mounting the hooks, adjust the cord length so that there is a bit of slack when the cabinet is closed. Open the cabinet and check that the cord lifts the lid smoothly. Adjust the mounting position or cord length if necessary. Recommended Materials PLA for hooks TPU for cord You can use ordinary string if your basket requires a different length. Simply tie it to the printed hooks. Notes The exact position of the hook and the string attachment point may need small adjustments depending on the bin lid weight, cabinet travel, and available space. It is best to test the mechanism temporarily before permanent installation.

Description Parametric Oval & Rectangular Stacked Rings Tray (Modular Design) Create premium decorative and organizing trays with walls made of stacked horizontal rings. This project offers maximum parametric flexibility: choose between Oval/Round shapes and Rectangular/Square shapes (with adjustable corner radii). The script perfectly recalculates the base, wall flare angle, and layer overlaps. Designed for easy 3D printing without supports. --- PARAMETER MANUAL --- 1. Basic Settings - Base Shape: Overall shape of the base (Oval or Rectangular). - Tray Length: Total length of the tray (mm). - Tray Width: Total width of the tray (mm) - must be less than or equal to length. - Base Thickness: Vertical thickness of the base floor plate (mm). - Number of Layers: Quantity of rings stacked vertically to form the wall (Default: 5). - Ring Tube Radius: Radius of the tube forming each ring (mm). Controls the thickness and corrugated texture of the wall. - Wall Angle: Flare angle of the walls (degrees). 0° makes the wall straight vertical, while positive values open the tray in a tapered, conical shape. 2. Wall & Cut Settings - Cut Inner Wall: If enabled ("Yes"), the script performs a clean tapered internal subtraction, removing the inner corrugations to create a smooth interior wall. If disabled ("No"), the interior remains corrugated following the rings. - Inner Wall Thickness: Defines the final thickness of the smooth wall (mm) (used if Cut Inner Wall = Yes). - Floor Chamfer Size: Size of the internal transition chamfer/ramp (mm) at the joint where the floor meets the wall (used if Cut Inner Wall = Yes). 3. Engravings & Texts - Enable Bottom Logo: Enables debossed/engraved mirrored text to the bottom face (Z = 0) of the tray base for personalization. - Logo Text: Text for the bottom engraving (e.g. @yourhandle). - Logo Font Size: Font size of the bottom logo (mm). - Engraving Depth: Depth of the engraving (mm). - Enable Top Text: Adds high-relief custom text to the top center of the tray floor. - Top Text: Text for the top face. - Top Font Size: Font size of the top text (mm). - Top Text Height: Height/relief of the top text (mm). 4. Advanced Settings - Corner Radius: Radius of the rounded corners (mm) - used when Base Shape is Rectangular. - Vertical Overlap Factor: Interpenetration factor between adjacent rings (0.25 = 25% overlap, providing structural strength for printing). - Ring Z Offset: Global vertical offset of the rings (mm). Slightly negative values sink the first ring into the bed for a flat base and excellent print adhesion! - Ring Radial Offset: Global radial offset of the rings (mm). - Display Mode: CAD visualization mode (Full, Base Only, Border Only, Cross Section). - $fn: Resolution of the circular curves of the tray. - tube_fn: Resolution of the tube cross-section (ring). --- RECOMMENDED PRINT SETTINGS (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) --- - Layer Height: 0.16mm (Optimal for the vertical curves of the spheres) - Wall Generator: Arachne (Recommended for filling small fusions) - Infill: 10% Gyroid or Cross Hatch - Supports: No supports needed! - Fuzzy Skin (Optional for premium finish): Contour, Thickness: 0.3mm, Point distance: 0.8mm 💡 Pro Tip: Enable Variable/Adaptive Layer Height in your slicer.

description: Generate a circular, square, or rectangular vent grille with honeycomb, slot, or radial openings, screw-hole patterns, and an optional removable filter-retaining frame. This is a practical parametric grille generator for small vents, cabinet cutouts, fan openings, electronics enclosures, workshop panels, and generic indoor duct covers. Choose the duct shape, opening size, flange width, grille pattern, screw-hole layout, and optional filter-retaining frame. The default print includes a rectangular honeycomb grille plate plus a separate screw-aligned frame that can help retain a thin filter sheet, mesh, insect screen, or dust screen behind the grille. The OpenSCAD console prints an approximate open-area percentage and open area for the active settings. Treat this as a design guide for comparing settings, not a certified airflow rating. Features: - Circular, square, and rectangular duct/opening options. - Honeycomb, slot, and radial grille styles. - No-hole, corner/four-hole, side-center, round four-hole, and round six-hole screw patterns. - Optional raised filter pocket rim and removable screw-aligned retaining frame. - Support-free flat printing. - Bounded parameters for fast MakerWorld generation. Use PLA for indoor decorative or light utility covers. Use PETG if the grille may see warmth, sunlight, damp air, or tougher workshop handling. Do not use this as a certified HVAC, fire, appliance, high-temperature, pressure, or child-safety fan guard component. Customization Notes - `duct_shape` selects `circular` , `square` , or `rectangular` . - Use `duct_diameter` for circular openings, `square_size` for square openings, and `duct_width` / `duct_height` for rectangular openings. - `grille_style` selects `honeycomb` , `slots` , or `radial` . - `screw_pattern` selects the mounting-hole layout. - `filter_frame_enabled` includes a separate retaining frame in the print layout. - `display_mode` can export the whole print kit, the grille only, or the frame only. - `layout_direction` can switch the print-kit layout between vertical and horizontal spacing. - For large duct sizes, export `grille_only` and `frame_only` separately or split/rearrange the STL in your slicer to fit your bed. - Watch the echoed open-area estimate when changing grille size, bar width, or style.

Of course, the two slots work just as well for any other paperwork you want to separate — mail vs. bills, personal vs. work, "to file" vs. "filed" — whatever workflow makes sense for you. ## Features - **Two-slot design**: built-in workflow, not just storage - **Iconic silhouette**: the classic folder shape, reimagined as a functional desk object - **Minimalist & stylish**: fits modern desk setups and home offices - **Fuzzy skin finish**: a soft, textured surface that gives it a more premium, less "3D-printed" look - **Single print, no assembly**: prints as one piece, no supports required ## Dimensions - Width: 160mm - Height: 130mm - Depth: 40mm ## Print Settings - **Material**: PLA or PETG both work well - **Fuzzy skin**: adds noticeably more print time, but gives the surface a much more refined, matte, non-plasticky finish — worth it for a desk piece you'll see every day - **Layer height**: 0.16-0.2mm - **Infill**: 15-20% is enough (mostly flat panels, not heavily load-bearing) - **Supports**: not required ## Notes Started as a simple fix for our own paperwork chaos (health insurance vs. private insurance claims), but works for any two-pile system you need on your desk. If you come up with a clever use for the two slots, let us know in the comments!

description: 🩻Overview🩻 This high-precision 3D model is a faithful replica of the human knee joint, created through a rigorous anatomical and digital workflow. The skeletal structures were directly extracted and reconstructed from real CT scans to guarantee true-to-life bone morphology. The soft tissues—including ligaments, menisci, and articular cartilage—were then meticulously 3D modeled by hand, based on in-depth studies of MRI scans and anatomical literature. It serves as a premium medical-grade educational tool, perfect for students, orthopedic professionals, physical therapists, or 3D printing enthusiasts. Included Anatomical Structures The model features all critical bony and soft tissue structures necessary to understand the complex biomechanics of the knee: 🦴Skeletal Structure (CT Extracted): Femur, Tibia, Fibula, and Patella (kneecap), featuring accurate reproductions of condyles, epicondyles, and articular surfaces. 🔗Ligamentous Apparatus (MRI Modeled): Cruciate Ligaments (Anterior Cruciate Ligament - ACL & Posterior Cruciate Ligament - PCL). Collateral Ligaments (Medial Collateral Ligament - MCL & Lateral Collateral Ligament - LCL). Patellar System (including the patellar tendon/ligaments). 🦵Cartilage & Cushioning (MRI Modeled): Menisci (Medial and Lateral menisci). Articular Cartilage covering both the femoral and tibial contact surfaces. Intended Use Education & Didactics: An excellent tactile and visual aid for anatomy classrooms, medical schools, and healthcare training. Patient Communication: Ideal for orthopedic clinics and physiotherapy practices to visually explain injuries (e.g., ACL tears, meniscus damage, osteoarthritis) and surgical procedures to patients. Mechanical planetarium with accurate relative orbital periods. This hand-driven 17 gear train model of the solar system accurately shows the relative orbital periods of the 8 planets (Pluto can get lost). Herringbone gears and needle thrust bearings are used to reduce friction. UPDATE 23-June-2026: I have corrected the needle thrust parts list - I incorrectly had (65x90x3) for Uranus, and left out (50x70x3) for Saturn. Thanks to user_3243033349 for pointing out my mistake. Correct parts list is below. Orbital Periods and Errors Orbital periods are calculated relative to Mercury. Planet Actual Period (days) Model Period (days) Error (%) Neptune 60195 60068 0.21 Uranus 30688 30683 0.02 Saturn 10755 10767 -0.11 Jupiter 4331.74 4336.70 -0.11 Mars 686.98 686.73 0.04 Earth 365.24 364.80 0.12 Venus 224.7 224.69 0.00 Mercury 87.97 87.97 0.00 Parts List AXK Needle thrust bearings: these are used to reduce friction. Can be found cheaply on AliExpress (all of the bearings should be < €30 in total). The following are quantity x (inner x outer x depth) in mm: 9 x (8x21x2) - for the connecting and driving gears 4 x (35x52x2) - for base, Mercury, Venus and Earth 1 x (40x60x3) - for Mars 1 x (45x65x3) - for Jupiter 1 x (50x70x3) - for Saturn 1 x (60x85x3) - for Uranus Marbles for the Sun and planets. Diameters for the marbles are: Sun: 40 mm Mercury: 12 mm Venus: 16 mm Earth: 18 mm Mars: 16 mm Jupiter: 25 mm Saturn: 22 mm Uranus: 20 mm Neptune: 18 mm Printing Instructions Printed entirely with PLA, with P1S 0.4mm nozzle For the gears I used a really small layer height (0.08 mm) and slow first layer printing Notes on Assembly As the gears are herringbone, they cannot just be dropped in place from above. Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created a soccer version that is completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the soccer version here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2977052-soccer-football-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture#profileId-3339654 For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Versions with Themes I currently plan on making more variations of this model with specific themes. There are many possible versions that I could create. Let me know which ones you want to see, and let me know of any other ideas that you have. description: The Great Pyramid Cross-Section Explore the secrets of the Great Pyramid of Giza with this detailed cross-section display, revealing the intricate chambers that have fascinated humanity for millennia. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Are these voids hidden burial sites, or part of a larger, lost architectural plan? A New Discovery Beneath the Sands Recent, cutting-edge research using satellite imaging and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has suggested the existence of an extensive, deeper subterranean complex beneath the Giza Plateau. Summary This project is designed to germinate Chia seeds, although other small seeds can also be used. The seeds must first be activated by placing them in a container with water that barely covers them for several minutes. A gelatinous substance will be generated. Then they should be spread on the upper part of the grid, taking care that they are not very overlapping. The grid is placed in the container with water to the bottom of it and is kept covered for the first 2 days to generate a greenhouse effect. From the second day it is left uncovered, taking care to maintain the water level to the bottom of the grid. A spray can be used to moisten the sprouts a couple of times a day, but in my case it was not necessary. Although Chia sprouts can be consumed as food, we recommend that in this case the impression be made with filaments approved for this purpose. description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. A question for the more curious viewer: Why does the biceps tendon anchor to the scapula instead of attaching directly to the humerus? Let me know in the comments!

Based on the NSW Foundation font and designed for early writers, each letter features directional arrows and stroke numbers cut into the surface to guide proper handwriting formation - all 26 letters on a single, easy-to-use board. Thoughtfully Designed for Young Learners In stencil letters like a, b, d, e, g, o, p, q and others, small bridge points are needed to keep the inner parts of the letter connected to the plate. In many stencils these bridges are placed arbitrarily, interrupting the natural flow of the letter mid-stroke. In this design, the bridges are deliberately positioned at each letter's starting or ending point — so when a child begins tracing, they start at the bridge and follow the letter all the way around. The result is an uninterrupted tracing experience that teaches correct stroke formation, not just the shape of the letter. Print Options The arrows and stroke numbers are cut out of each letter — in a single colour they're still clearly visible and functional. For the best visual result, the colour change is already set in the slicer file at the correct layer height, so no manual configuration is needed. If you have an AMS , it will handle the filament swap automatically. No AMS? No problem — your printer will pause and prompt you to swap filament manually at the right moment. The result is a contrasting colour on the arrows and stroke numbers, making the letter outlines really pop. Print Tips Due to the fine details in this model, good bed adhesion is critical — poor adhesion can cause lifting or warping and ruin the small details. 🧼 Clean your plate thoroughly with hot water and dishwashing liquid before printing and allow to dry completely 🖼️ An outer brim is included in the slicer profile to prevent warping and lifting on this large, flat print. If you have adhesion issues on the insides of the letters, reslice with inner brims turned on. 🗼 Prime tower is disabled — this is intentional, so don't be alarmed when you don't see one in the preview Coming Soon A face-down version with coloured inserts is in development; the same great stencil with a premium finish. Follow my profile so you don't miss it! Also Check Out For individual letter pieces your child can pick up, arrange, and trace one at a time, head to my Stencil Puzzle Pieces — same font, same arrow system, same thoughtful bridge placement, but each letter is its own interlocking puzzle tile. Perfect for name recognition, word-building, and sorting games alongside this stencil. Browse my other models for more Foundation font tools designed for early learners.

description: Help students pause, breathe, and reset with this tactile Wave Breathing Pause Card from 3DprintEDU. This 3D printable SEL tool gives children a calming finger tracing path to follow while practising mindful breathing, focus, and emotional regulation. Students begin at the raised O , then slowly trace along the wave paths as they breathe in and out. The included 3MF file contains both versions , so you can choose the style that works best for your students, classroom, or sensory space: Raised Path Version An embossed tactile wave path that students can feel clearly as they trace. Indented Path Version An engraved tactile wave path that gives students a smooth recessed channel to follow with their finger. Both versions are no AMS , quick to print, and use less than 20 g of filament, making them easy to print for classrooms, calm corners, counselling spaces, occupational therapy rooms, and home regulation kits. How to Use Begin at the raised O , which is designed to be the consistent starting point across the SEL Pause Cards collection. Place your finger on the O and slowly follow the wave path. Students can breathe in as they trace up each wave, then breathe out as they trace down each wave. The repeated wave pattern gives students a gentle rhythm to follow as they slow their breathing and refocus. Repeat the path a few times, moving calmly from wave to wave. The tactile design gives students a simple, hands on way to pause, regulate, and reset. For younger students, an adult can guide the rhythm by saying: Trace up, breathe in. Trace down, breathe out. Keep going slowly. description: The project This life-size 3D model is a realistic human hand skeleton. It was created starting from a real CT scan to keep the true shape of the bones. After cleaning up the scan, custom joints were added directly into the design. The result is a highly accurate model that prints in one single piece and moves just like a real hand. ⚙️ Print-in-Place Kinematics & Anatomy Unlike standard static models or complex multi-part assemblies, this hand is designed to be printed as a single, continuous piece: Zero Assembly Required: The complex mechanical joints are built directly into the geometry. Once the print is finished, the fingers and thumb are immediately ready to flex, extend, and move. Bio-realistic Movement: The internal joint constraints were specifically calibrated to respect the natural limits and range of motion found in a real human hand. Medical-Grade Accuracy: Features true-to-life representations of the carpal bones, metacarpals, and phalanges, preserving the organic textures and shapes of the original scan. 🎓 Perfect For: Clinical & Academic Study: A fantastic, hands-on visual aid for medical students, physical therapists, and anatomy teachers. Biomechanical Demonstration: Easily explains how the skeletal framework behaves during grasping, finger articulation, and thumb opposition. 3D Printing Showcase: An incredibly impressive project to demonstrate your printer's dimensional accuracy, bridging capabilities, and print-in-place tolerances. Artistic Reference: A great physical tool for artists and animators studying lifelike hand poses. 💡 Print Guidelines Format: 100% Print-in-Place. Material: Optimized for standard PLA. Rigid materials work perfectly to demonstrate the skeletal kinematics—no TPU or flexible filament is needed. Scale: Pre-scaled to match the proportions of an average adult human hand (1:1 scale). Disclaimer: While highly accurate and derived from real medical data, this model is designed strictly for educational, demonstration, and hobbyist purposes. It is not intended for clinical diagnostics or to replace professional medical advice.

description: Overview This soccer kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to always be centered in the exact same position. It is a themed version of the model you can find here: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2961089-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture-floating-ball#profileId-3319236 All of the parts in this model are compatible with the parts in the original. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. Two versions of the ball are available. One that requires an AMS or dual nozzle and one that requires the pentagons to be pressed or glued into place. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates with both types of balls in the profile and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three or fourteen pieces: the base, the print-in-place linkages, and the ball that requires AMS or the ball that does not and the eleven pentagons. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All of these parts are completely compatible with the original model. https://makerworld.com/en/models/2961089-fixed-center-kinetic-sculpture-floating-ball#profileId-3319236 Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. If the no-AMS ball is printed, the pentagons need to be placed in place (they will likely require some glue). Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. description: Anatomy Pro: Interactive Bone Internal Structure Detailed Description Dive deep into human biology with this high-fidelity, multi-color educational model of a long bone (Femur/Humerus cross-section). This model is designed specifically for students, medical professionals, and science enthusiasts to visualize what lies beneath the "hard" surface of our skeletal system. The design features a strategic cutaway to reveal the complex layers of living tissue. It is an indispensable tool for classrooms or home-schooling environments where a 2D textbook image simply isn't enough to convey the 3D reality of biological architecture. Key Anatomical Features Included: Compact Bone: The dense, hard outer layer that provides strength. Spongy Bone (Cancellous): The intricate, porous lattice structure shown in the epiphysis. Bone Marrow: Represented by the central red core, the powerhouse of blood cell production. Epiphyseal Line: The visible "growth plate" remnant where the bone once lengthened. Blood Vessels: Detailed arterial and venous pathways (Red and Blue) showing how bone is a living, breathing organ. Print Settings & Material Recommendations To achieve the vibrant, anatomical accuracy seen in the photos, this model is optimized for multi-color printing (AMS/Unitree). Filament Recommendation: For the best results, I highly recommend using SUNLU Filament . Their tolerances are incredible for detailed anatomical prints like this. Bone Structure: SUNLU PLA Plus White – provides the perfect "bone" finish with superior strength. Marrow & Vessels: SUNLU PLA Meta Red and SUNLU PLA Meta Blue . The Meta series flows beautifully for those tiny vascular details. Pro Tip for Multi-Color: Since this is a color-intensive print, check out my tutorial: How to remesh and color prints effectively in Bambu Studio and/or Snapmaker U1 to minimize waste and maximize detail! History & Background This model was developed out of a need for affordable, tactile medical training aids. Traditional medical-grade bone models can cost hundreds of dollars. By 3D printing this design, educators can provide every student with a hands-on experience, allowing them to trace the path of blood vessels and feel the difference between the porous spongy bone and the solid compact bone. Remix Ideas & Expanded Use This model is a perfect base for several other projects: Pathology Remix: Modify the marrow or spongy bone area to show the effects of Osteoporosis or Leukemia for clinical demonstrations. LED Diorama: Scale up and hollow out the vascular channels to run fiber-optic "glowing" blood vessels. Desk Organizer: Remix the flat end of the bone to hold pens or medical tools for a doctor’s office. Spanish Version 2×1 = 2 2×2 = 4 2×3 = 6 ... This is the traditional format used in Spain and several other countries. International Version 1×2 = 2 2×2 = 4 3×2 = 6 ... This format is commonly found in educational materials from Germany, English-speaking countries, and other international resources. Both versions produce exactly the same results. description: Modular Articulated DNA Educational Model Let your students build, connect, and explore the DNA with this colourful modular model designed for hands-on learning. Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases, while the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone. This model is great for classrooms, STEM projects, biology demonstrations, or anyone who wants a fun physical way to understand nucleotide pairing and DNA structure. I also plan on extending this model with a couple of more pieces for better demonstration of topics like Transcription and Translation . Feel free to leave a like and follow if you'd like to stay updated. Parts You can print as many of the individual parts as you like and connect them with each other! Each nucleotide piece represents one of the DNA/RNA bases and the blue connector parts form the sugar-phosphate backbone: Cytosine Guanine Adenine Thymine Uracil Assembly & Colouring The backbone pieces can be clicked together with a little bit of force. It is recommended to use 5x2 (dxh) magnets for both the backbone pieces and nucleotides, to better hold them in place. Place the magnets into the slot (make sure you have them oriented all in the same way!) and use a paper clip, a scredriver, or something similar to push the magnet all the way into the slot. You can also remove the magnets if needed using a paper clip from the other side. Feel free to adjust the colouring of the pieces to your needs. My file uses the colours according to the Wikipedia nucleic acid image: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid#/media/File:Difference_DNA_RNA-EN.svg Versions There are two Versions of nucleotides: Standard Set (recommended!) nucleotides have no chamfer/fillet on the connection pin. This makes them harder to separate from their counterparts, but results in a more stable double strand. Rounded Nucleotide Set contains nucleotide pieces with a rounded down connection pin. This makes them easier to separate, e.g. when demonstrating something, but obviously also reduces the stability of the entire double strand in terms of base pairs disconnecting when you move the double strand around. After many months of developing, it’s finally here! This is an Inline 2 Vacuum Engine, a model of an inline 2 internal combustion engine, that runs off a vacuum. I have spent months working out every little detail and mainly trying to get every tolerance perfect. I also go through a lot of work on all of my models to ensure that they are easy to print, and with minimal supports. This model is completely press-fit, no glue, no tape, no magnets, just plain old PLA, modeled with the intent of being easy and fun to assemble and mess with, for experts to beginners to people who just enjoy messing around with cool contraptions. Additionally, those who have previous experience with vacuum engines can attempt to performance tune it, by changing the offset the camshaft has on the crankshaft. Simply print out all the parts (don't forget to boost with that free boost token ;), assemble with the easy assembly instructions, and enjoy! Note: You will need six 608 bearings, either 3D printed versions from Makerworld, or the metal versions which I have included in the Bill of Materials from Makersupply. Also note that the tolerances are very good for a Bambu Lab A1, but I cannot guarantee perfect fits with other printers, although they should be pretty close. Operation Instructions: Operation is easy, simply stick a vacuum up to the cone on the exhaust manifold, and watch it rip! You may need to give it a rotate or two to help it get started. Tips for success: Be sure that the camshaft if offset by a quarter turn from the crankshaft (explained in the instructions). Try lubing all of the areas where there is filament on filament contact, to reduce friction and increase speed and power. Clean out your vacuum's filter, or remove it entirely to improve your vacuum performance. Be sure there is little friction inside the crank case, as in make sure there are tiny gaps between all of the moving parts to ensure they move freely. Updates: I have many updates planned, from gaskets cutouts, to new exhaust manifolds for different vacuums. I will include links to them here as they are developed. I just finished a throttle body for this engine, and you can find it here Thank you for checking this model out, and if you enjoyed, please share with your friends and family! I love designing models like this, and yall's support keeps me going. It takes a lot of time and trial runs to design new models. This model was no exception! Instructions: This model can be a bit complicated, as there are many pieces, but personally I found it very fun to assemble, and very satisfying. Step One: Connect the piston heads to the connecting rods with the two pins. Next assemble the crankshaft. This can be a bit tricky, with all the pieces looking identical, but pay attention to the photo, and you'll do fine. Note, the the position of the two cranks should be opposite, but I accidently had them the same in the first photo. The parts include are the five crankshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two piston assemblies, the flywheel, and one of the two gears with a hexagon cutout. Step Two: Connect the two valves to the connecting rods with the two pins. Now assemble the camshaft, this can also be a bit tricky, since there are so many pieces that make up the camshaft. Again, just pay careful attention to the photos and you'll do great. Note: If you get the crankshaft and camshaft pieces mixed up just remember the camshaft has a shorter stroke than the crankshaft, meaning the pieces are smaller. The pieces used here are the five camshaft pieces, three 608 bearings, the two valve assemblies, and one of the two gears with a hexagonal cut out. Step Three: Attach the cylinder heads to the block. There are a different amount of each size of screw included in the file, and throughout the rest of these instructions I will refer to each screw by the amount of them that are included. The set of three screws go in the three holes in a line in the head, and the single screw goes in the single hole on the other side of the head. VERY IMPORTANT: The screws included with this file are FRAGILE and cannot take very much twisting force at all. To avoid breaking off screws inside of the engine block or oil pan, finger tighten or lightly tighten with a flat-head screwdriver until its not easy and then STOP SCREWING. Note that the screwheads are also 10mm, and you may be able to fit a socket on them, but you must still be very careful to not over tighten the screws. Step Four: Now it is time to lay the crankshaft, the camshaft, and the middle gear into the engine block. This step can be tricky, and must be done correctly or the engine will not function. The secret to vacuum engines is to have the camshaft a one quarter (0.25, 90 degrees) turn AHEAD of the crankshaft, in the direction you want it to rotate. In a simpler sense, this means that while the valve is completely open (Top Dead Center) the piston must be halfway up. When the piston reaches Top Dead Center, the valve with already be half closed. Additionally, since this engine has two cylinders, the pistons and valves must be in opposite positions to be most efficient. Finally, if you would like to mess around with tuning the engine for higher speeds, try changing the amount that the camshaft leads the crankshaft. Basically, try a lead of maybe a sixth of a turn or a third of a turn, instead of a quarter turn. Step Five: Once you've got those in place, you can carefully screw the oil pan to the engine block with the set of four screws included in the file. Be sure the quarter turn amount does not change while you set the engine block and the oil pan together. Step Six: Finally, attach the exhaust manifold to the heads with the set of two screws, and the nuts. This may take some finagling to get them on. Once again remember to not overtighten, I advise only finger tightening. Congrats! Your finished! Don't forget to share a comment with a photo about your experience, I love to hear about it, whether success or failure. Also don't forget to boost!
