🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Customizable vacuum hose adapter and nozzle generator for measured round hoses, flat crevice tips, oval tips, rectangle tips, barb ribs, brush collars, and an optional wall clip. This parametric generator starts from a round hose-side connection and lets you build a reducer, expander, nozzle, or transition into a round, oval, rounded-rectangle, or flat crevice outlet. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. 🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: Square Kumihimo disc for flat bracelets This is a square Kumihimo disc to make flat bracelets using the ancient Japanese artform of Kumihimo , which is done by weaving strings of silk, rope or yarn together using a disc to form a rope/bracelet with artistic patterns in the process. The disc has ten (10) horizontal and vertical notches to hold the strings in place and a rounded slot in the center for the weaving pattern to form. The top and bottom horizontal rows are labelled 1-10 and the left and right side vertical columns are labelled A-J to make it easier to stay oriented while making your Kumihimo weaving bracelet. The labels are printed flat on the bed, so the disc is rotated upside down. If using an AMS, the labels are pre-colored and will be printed using a color for the disc and a second for the labels. Without an AMS, the labels will still be visible through the trick of the labels being recessed by one layer height (0.2mm), this embeds the outline of the labels even without color as shown below. If desired, you could trace the etching using a permanent marker after the print. Instructions No assembly is required for the print. Simply print it, get some strings of silk, yarn or rope and you're ready to go. Patterns and instructions on how to use a Kumihimo disc to make rope/bracelets can be found online with several websites dedicated to it and many instructional videos. Print Settings Supports / Brim: No Layer height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15% cubic for strength Walls: 2 + alternating Wall generation: Arachne Top/bottom pattern: Monotonic Orientation: Flat on the bed, printed upside down for the embedded labels to print nicely Material: PLA AMS recommended for multicolor print for the labels Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets If you're interested in making round bracelets, you can check out my Round Kumihimo disc for round bracelets which allows you to make some beautiful round patterned bracelets. 64-slot Large Kumihimo disc for complex pattern bracelets If you are looking for a way to make more complex patterns with more than 16 strings in a single weave, check out my 64-Slot Large Kumihimo disc for complex bracelets which allows you to make Kumihimo bracelets up to 40 strings, which is the practical limit for round Kumihimo braids.

Modular Shoe Rack I have created this modular shoe rack to organize our footwear better. The whole model was designed to be modular and customizable in width. The framework is 3d printed from PLA and takes in five wooden round rails of 19 mm diameter per compartment. Depending on your location you can use these examples (DE: OBI , Bauhaus ) or anything similar. Make sure the rails don't fit too tightly. If you cant push them in relatively easy sand them down using some sandpaper. If you try to squeeze them in too hard the layers of the frame might seperate! The model measures 300 mm in depth. There are two sizes for the frame height: 150 mm and 200 mm. You can stack them modularly however you please and need. For the top compartment there is also an endpiece to give the whole rack a rounder appearance. TPU feet for a softer stand are also included. Printing and Assembly To print the model you should get an exaple wood piece that you plan to use. Test: I included a test part on plate 5 to verify the measurements. Start by printing one compartment by printing the same plate (plate 1 for 150 mm, or plate 2 for 200 mm) twice. Cut the wooden rails to the length you want your Rack to be. You will need five rails per compartment. Please note that 28 mm of the rail go into each side of the frame. The total width of the rack will be the length of your rails + 4 mm. For cutting I suggest using a stopper so you can always adjust your rails to exactly the same length. Make sure you sand down three centimenters at each end of each rail untill the glide in with some resistance. Then mount all five rails to one side of the frame. Make sure they all went in the same depth. Place the other side of the frame on the other ends of the rails. I mounted with the rails pointing up and used a piece of wood which I hit gently with a hammer. Repeat steps 1. to 4. for each compartment you need. Make sure the compartments couplers on the frame bottom fit into the slots on the top of the other compartments. Don't clip them in before making sure the setup is correct. The clips are tight and very hard to remove. Print the end pieces by printing plate 3 twice. Print the TPU feet. I suggest printing them by object for optimal quality, however I included a profile for people whose printer can only print by layer. Assemble the whole thing by placing the rack compartments on top of each other and gently hitting it from above (I used just my fist) until they clip in. Place all the footwear you have in it. If you run out of space: EXPAND! Voilà: Order in the shoe section!

description: Make your own text stamp for clay, soap, leather, play dough, fondant, and normal ink-pad stamping. Up to three lines of custom text, round or rectangular head, emboss or deboss, optional border, and a comfortable twist-lock handle. Prints support-free. Type your text and print a personal stamp. The rigid PETG/PLA version presses crisp, readable impressions into polymer clay, air-dry clay, soap, soft leather, play dough, fondant, and similar soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping, a tested option is to split the stamp face in the slicer and print the actual raised letters/rim in TPU, with the base and handle in PETG, so the letters flex slightly like a softer stamp face. Features: - Up to three lines of text, automatically centered. - Mirrored text by default, so the stamped impression reads correctly. Turn mirroring off to print a readable display plaque instead. - Two impression styles: "raised" presses your text INTO the material (debossed impression), "recessed" leaves your text standing proud (embossed impression). - Round or rectangular head with adjustable size and optional border ring - the border stamps a clean frame around your text. - Adjustable text depth (0.8-3 mm) for shallow or deep impressions. - Comfortable mushroom handle with a bayonet twist-lock: insert into the head back and twist clockwise to a firm stop. The locked handle cannot pull off, even when lifting the stamp out of sticky clay. Print one handle and many heads: name stamps, date stamps, logo text, gift tags. - Tested TPU-face workflow: print the raised letters/rim in TPU and the base + handle in PETG for a softer face that also works better as a normal ink-pad stamp. - Console warning if your text is too wide for the chosen head size. - Both parts print flat with no supports. The model checks your text width against the head size and prints a note in the customizer console if a line will not fit. Note: rigid PLA/PETG stamp faces are best for clay, soap, leather, dough, and other soft materials. For normal ink-pad stamping on paper, the tested TPU-face workflow gives a more forgiving contact surface than a hard FDM face. Results still depend on ink pad, paper, layer height, and surface finish, so test first. Customization Notes - line_1 / line_2 / line_3: your text; leave lines empty to use fewer lines. - font_name: keep the default Liberation Sans Bold for reliable width warnings; other bold fonts work, but check the preview. - mirror_text: leave ON for stamping. Turn off only for display plaques. - text_style: "raised" = pressed-in (debossed) impression, "recessed" = raised (embossed) impression. - text_depth: 1.5 mm default; use 2-3 mm for soft doughs, 1-1.5 mm for firm clay and leather. - head_shape / head_diameter / head_width / head_height: face size. Bigger faces fit longer text. - border_enabled / border_width / border_inset: frame ring around the text. - border_depth: rim height, independent of text_depth. Match text_depth for a classic one-level stamp, or make the rim taller than the text so it contains the material and controls impression depth like a cookie-cutter frame - useful for wax-seal-style stamps and uniform clay medallions. - fit_clearance: twist-lock clearance. Increase by 0.05-0.1 if the handle is hard to insert or twist; decrease toward 0.05 for a tighter lock. - part: "all" prints both pieces; "head" alone for extra stamp faces for a handle you already printed; "fit_preview" is preview-only - do not print.

🇪🇸 Férula Termoformable 3D de Ostec3D: Guía Oficial Descripción del Producto La Férula Termoformable de Ostec3D es una solución ortopédica avanzada, diseñada para sustituir las escayolas tradicionales. Fabricada mediante impresión 3D, esta férula se imprime de forma completamente plana y adquiere flexibilidad al sumergirse en agua caliente. Esto permite un moldeado anatómico directo sobre el paciente, garantizando un ajuste perfecto, peso ultraligero y excelente ventilación para la piel. Parámetros de Impresión 3D Para garantizar la flexibilidad correcta durante el calentamiento y la rigidez estructural una vez fría, la férula debe imprimirse estrictamente con la siguiente configuración: Altura de capa / Perfil: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Densidad de relleno: 8% (Relleno poco denso) Patrón de relleno: Rectilíneo Nota de fabricación: El uso del relleno rectilíneo al 8% es crucial. Si el relleno es más denso, el plástico no se ablandará de manera uniforme; si es diferente al rectilíneo, la férula podría perder su integridad estructural al doblarse. Guía de Uso y Moldeado 1.Calentar el agua: Temperatura del agua: 80°C - 95°C. Calienta agua en un recipiente lo suficientemente amplio para que quepa la férula plana. El agua debe estar a una temperatura de entre 80°C y 95°C. Es muy importante tener en cuenta que esta es la temperatura del agua, y no pasa con esa misma intensidad al material plástico. El propósito de usar el agua a esta temperatura es, simplemente, permitir que el plástico llegue a su punto de ablandamiento de forma mucho más rápida y sencilla. 2.Proteger al paciente: Antes de colocar la férula, cubre la extremidad del paciente con una malla tubular de algodón (vendaje tubular) para proteger la piel del contacto directo y del calor residual. 3.Sumergir la férula: Introduce la férula impresa en el agua caliente durante 1 a 3 minutos. Observarás que el material rígido comienza a volverse flexible y maleable como la goma. 4.Moldear sobre la anatomía: Retira la férula del agua (usa pinzas o guantes si es necesario), sacude el exceso de agua y comprueba rápidamente la temperatura tocándola ligeramente. Colócala sobre la extremidad del paciente y moldéala suavemente para que copie la anatomía exacta. 5.Enfriar y fijar: Mantén la férula en la posición deseada mientras se enfría a temperatura ambiente. Este proceso es muy rápido y tomará solo de 1 a 2 minutos. Una vez fría, recuperará su rigidez total. Fíjala con correas de velcro o vendaje según sea necesario. 💡 Modificaciones y Re-termoformado: Si la férula no queda perfecta en el primer intento o si el paciente requiere un ajuste posterior por cambios en la inflamación, el material puede volver a calentarse. Simplemente sumerge la férula (o la zona específica que deseas ajustar) nuevamente en el agua caliente, y podrá ser termoformada nuevamente para cualquier modificación. 🇬🇧 Ostec3D Thermoformable 3D Splint: Official Guide Product Description The Ostec3D Thermoformable Splint is an advanced orthopedic solution designed to replace traditional plaster casts. Manufactured via 3D printing, this splint is printed completely flat and becomes flexible when submerged in hot water. This allows for direct anatomical molding onto the patient, ensuring a perfect custom fit, ultra-lightweight feel, and excellent skin ventilation. 3D Printing Parameters To guarantee the correct flexibility during heating and structural rigidity once cooled, the splint must be printed strictly using the following settings: Layer Height / Profile: 0.24 mm Standard BBL Infill Density: 8% (Sparse infill) Infill Pattern: Rectilinear Manufacturing Note: Using an 8% rectilinear infill is crucial. If the infill is too dense, the plastic will not soften evenly; if a different pattern is used, the splint may lose its structural integrity when bent. Usage and Molding Guide 1.Heat the water: Water temperature: 80°C - 95°C (176°F - 203°F). Heat water in a container wide enough to fit the flat splint. The water must be heated to a temperature between 80°C and 95°C (176°F - 203°F). It is important to note that this is the temperature of the water, and it does not fully transfer to the plastic material. The purpose of using water at this temperature is simply to help the plastic reach its softening point much more easily and quickly. 2.Protect the patient: Before applying the splint, cover the patient's limb with a cotton tubular stockinette to protect their skin from direct contact and residual heat. 3.Submerge the splint: Place the printed splint into the hot water for 1 to 3 minutes. You will notice the rigid material begin to turn flexible and rubber-like. 4.Mold to anatomy: Remove the splint from the water (use tongs or gloves if necessary), shake off the excess water, and quickly test the temperature by touching it lightly. Place it over the patient's limb and gently mold it so it contours to their exact anatomy. 5.Cool and secure: Hold the splint in the desired position while it cools to room temperature. This process is very fast and will take only 1 to 2 minutes. Once completely cool, it will regain its full rigidity. Secure it in place using velcro straps or bandages as needed. 💡 Modifications and Re-thermoforming: If the splint doesn't fit perfectly on the first try, or if the patient needs an adjustment later due to swelling changes, the material can be reheated. Simply submerge the splint (or the specific area you wish to adjust) back into the hot water, and it can be thermoformed again for any required modifications.

description: 3D printed SKADIS for BambuLab P1S and X1C I thought to utilise the rather empty space of my P1S to mount a SKADIS board, but none of the available original SKADIS sizes fit the P1S / X1C side panel. Therefore, I created this model which fits on the side of a BambuLab P1S or X1C. 💡Features: almost everything is 3D printable, needs only 3 M4x10 screws (even those are optional) keyed dovetail connection between the boards for strong fit significant clearance between the board and printers side panel + TPU spacers to prevent scratching mounted using printed hooks on a stock printer setup rigid and universal The SKADIS itself was generated from the parametric model by user @Line Arc Line from printables ( Parametric SKADIS Board Generator ). Kudos to the designer! Dimensions of the final SKADIS: 32 x 42 x 5.3 mm Most parts can be printed out of PLA but the mounting hooks need to be printed out of PETG, ASA or another less brittle material than PLA . The reason is, that those parts need to be flexed quite a lot to snap into place during mounting. 📜Part list and filaments: You will need the following printed parts. All are present in the submitted print profile and split into plates ( see below ). 4x SKADIS plates labelled 1-4 - PLA or any other material 6x spacers with three pins - PLA or any other material 3x spacers with a M4 hole - PLA or any other material 3x thin washers with a M4 hole (can be replaced by metal washers as well) - PLA or any other material 9x spacer caps - TPU (optional) 2x top mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) 2x bottom mounting brackets - PETG, ASA or other non-brittle material ( PLA won’t work! ) Non-printed parts 3x M4x10 screws 🖨️ Print instructions: Before you print all the pieces consider printing the TEST model first (see print profile). It's a quick 20 min to check if the settings fit your printer tolerances and setup. The provided print profiles have all settings dialed in and are ready to print (Bambu Handy App friendly). Just print each plate once and you should have everything you need: Plates 1-4 (PLA, ~350g total, 2h30min each): SKADIS parts labeled 1-4. Plate 5 (PLA, ~7g, 22 min): 6x stand-offs with pins, 3x normal standoffs and 3x spacers Plate 6 (TPU, ~4g, 22 min): 9x TPU caps for the stand-offs Plate 7 (PETG/ASA, ~12g, 30 min): 3x top and 3x bottom mounting hooks ( only two needed each, the other ones are spare ) 🔩 Assembly: A picture-assisted assembly and mounting guide is provided in the description. I strongly recommend to use that. You will find the text-based instruction below. Depending on the tolerances of your printer, the SKADIS pieces may go together either quite tight or be a little bit loose. I dialed the tolerances in for my P1S and the pieces grab onto each other quite well. Glue is not required for the assembly but is strongly recommended to prevent the whole thing from disassembling if you plan to hang something heavy from it. DO NOT use cyanoacrylate-based superglue especially if you printed the parts out of black (or dark) plastic. In my experience the glue emits some kind of vapour while drying which stains the plastic white. Instead, use a little bit of dedicated PLA glue or two-component resin glue. If the pieces go in quite tight you may use a rubber hammer to jam the pieces together which would probably hold quite well even without glue. Place piece 1 on a flat surface with the number 1 facing upward Hold piece 2 with the marking facing the top and slide into piece 1 from the top Repeat steps 1 and 2 for pieces 3 and 4 respectively Connect all pieces together by sliding the 1-2 piece into the 3-4 piece Insert the spacers with 3 legs into respective holes on the back of the board. The use of glue is advised if you are certain that you assembled the pieces right. Place the small spacers at the indicated spots at the front of the board. Insert the M4x?? screw from the front through the spacer and through the SKADIS hole. Screw in the remaining long spacers onto the M4 screws Cover all spacers with the TPU caps by inserting them into the respective holes 🪜Mounting: Remove the top glass of your P1S or X1C printer Hold the top mounting bracket with the SKADIS hook facing to the left. Flex the bracket and slide the right hand latch onto the frame where the glass sits on top. Straighten the left side of the bracket so it snaps into place. Repeat the same process for the other top mounting bracket Hang the assembled SKADIS onto the top brackets as indicated. Insert the bottom brackets into the indicated holes. Flex the right side of the bracket so it passes the bottom edge of the printer chassis and snaps into place. Repeat for the second bracket Now you are done and ready to go! Have fun! If you encounter any issues, feel free to comment or write me a DM, maybe I'll be able to help you. Post your makes, I'm curious how yours will look like ;) Cheers and all the best!😉 Fun fact: I finished the project in 2024 and it has been mounted on my P1S since without any issues. I just now finally found the time to document and release it properly. I hope you find it useful ;)

# 🧰 bentopeps — Rugged Vial Box (Parametric) ### Build a rugged storage box that fits *your* exact kit — not the other way around. **bentopeps** is a fully parametric, snap-shut rugged box for **peptide & hormone vials, syringes, and alcohol wipes**. You tell it what you carry and it builds the box around you: a **bento-style grid** interior, a **personalised two-colour lid**, a **click-stop hinge** that holds itself open, and an **ergonomic thumb latch** — all auto-sized, all support-free. > 👉 **Press the “Customize” button** to open it in MakerWorld’s parametric editor and dial in your own box right in the browser — no software to install. Then download your `.3mf`/`.stl` and print. --- ## ✨ Highlights - 🧩 **Bento-grid interior** — drop vials, syringes, or wipe slots into a Row × Column grid; the box **auto-sizes** around your loadout. - 💉 **Holds your whole kit** — 3 / 5 / 10 ml vials (standing *or* laid on their side), open syringe bins, and vertical wipe slots. - 🏷️ **Personalised lid** — flush **two-colour text + graphics** (great with Bambu AMS), 40+ fonts including bold, aggressive display faces. - 🔗 **Click-stop hinge** — the lid **holds open** at set angles instead of flopping, and is engineered to survive **thousands of open/close cycles** in PLA. - 👍 **Ergonomic latch** — a smooth thumb-pry lip pops the lid with one finger; still snaps shut securely. - 🖨️ **Prints clean** — watertight and **support-free**; tuned for Bambu Lab and every FDM printer. --- ## 🧩 The Bento Grid (how the interior works) The inside is a grid of **`grid_rows × grid_cols`** quadrants. You drop a **component** into each cell, and the box grows to fit: | Component | What it is | Footprint | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | **vial1 / vial2** | pockets of your two chosen vial sizes | `cols × rows` | **auto-fills** the compartment; each can stand up **or lay flat** | | **syringe** | an **open deep bin** for U100 syringes | `count×20 × 130 mm` | floor→ceiling, no wasted solid; syringes lie in & stack | | **wipe** | a **vertical slot** for 50×50 mm wipe packets on edge | `(count×5) × 50 mm` | ~5 mm ≈ 10 wipes; +5 mm per count | | **empty** | a solid spacer | — | for gaps / future use | **How the sizing works (so it always fits):** - **Column widths** grow to the widest cell in that column; **row lengths** grow to the longest cell in that row — a clean table layout. So a 130 mm syringe makes its whole row 130 mm long, and the vial cell next to it **auto-fills** that length with more vials. - **Box height = your tallest item** (a standing 10 ml is 54 mm; a standing wipe is 50 mm — whichever is tallest sets the height so the lid still closes). - **Partition walls** turn each cell into a real compartment. `partition_level` sets their height: **0 = none, 1 = 25 %, 2 = 50 %, 3 = 75 %, 4 = full**. ``` grid_cols ───────────────► Example default 2×2: ┌──────────────┬───────────────┐ │ vial1 (3 ml) │ syringe bin │ r1c1 = vial1 (3 ml) r1c2 = syringe ×2 │ auto-filled │ ▭▭ open/deep │ r2c1 = vial2 (10 ml) r2c2 = wipe ×3 ├──────────────┼───────────────┤ │ vial2 (10 ml)│ wipe slot ▮▮ │ └──────────────┴───────────────┘ ``` ### 💊 Vial catalog | Vial | Size | Pocket | |---|---|---| | **3 ml** | Ø16 × 40 mm | Ø17 | | **5 ml** | Ø22 × 40 mm | Ø23 | | **10 ml** | Ø22 × 54 mm | Ø23 | Pick which two sizes you want with `vial1_type` / `vial2_type` (sizes are editable in **`[Content Catalog]`**). --- ## 🎛️ How to use the parametric controls Open **Customize** and you’ll see the settings grouped into sections. Here’s what each group does: ### `[Grid]` — the layout skeleton - **`grid_rows` / `grid_cols`** — how many quadrants (e.g. 2 × 2). - **`partition_level`** — divider-wall height, `0`–`4` (none → full). ### `[Row 1] / [Row 2] / [Row 3]` — fill each cell - **`r1c1` … `r3c3`** — the component in each cell: `vial1`, `vial2`, `syringe`, `wipe`, or `empty`. - **`r1c1_n` …** — the **count** (vials wide, syringe width, or wipe thickness). - **`r1c1_rows` …** — vial **rows deep** for *that* quadrant (`0` = use the default), so every cell can have its own R × C. ### `[Vial Types]` — vials behaviour - **`vial1_type` / `vial2_type`** — `3ml` / `5ml` / `10ml`. - **`vial1_orient` / `vial2_orient`** — `standing` or **`flat`** (lays the vials in round side cradles). - **`vial_pack`** — `fill` (maximise how many fit) or `exact` (place exactly your R × C). - **`vial_align`** — `spread` (outer vials hug the walls, evenly indexed) or `center` (centred block). - **`vial_wall_clear`** — gap kept to the walls so pockets never break out. ### `[Box Height]` - **`height_override`** — `0` = **AUTO** (sized to the tallest item). Set a value to force a total height. - **`extra_height`** — add head-room above the auto height. ### `[Output]` — what to render - **`show_bottom`** — the tray. **`show_top`** — the lid. **`show_combined`** — lid sitting on the box (preview). - **`show_contents`** — draws translucent mock vials/syringes/wipes so you can eyeball the loadout. **Turn it OFF before exporting** — it’s preview-only. - The **console report** tells you the grid, box W × L × H, what each cell holds, and warns if anything is too big for your plate. > 💡 **Tip:** export **once with `show_bottom`** and **once with `show_top`** — that’s your tray + lid. --- ## 🏷️ Personalise the Lid — flush two-colour Text & Graphics The lid top can carry a **flush, co-planar** label — *not* embossed or engraved, but a second-colour region in the same surface (perfect for **Bambu AMS / MakerWorld multi-colour**). **Text** and **Design** are independent — use either or **both**, each with its own colour and placement. **Orientation frame:** picture the closed box with the **latch toward you** (front) and the **hinge at the back**. Everything is placed in that frame — `halign` = your left/right, `valign` `top` = hinge / `bottom` = latch. ### `[Lid Text]` - **`lid_text_on`**, **`lid_text`** (+ optional **`lid_text_line2`**), **`lid_text_color`**. - **`lid_font`** — a dropdown of clean classics **plus aggressive / manly display faces**: Oswald, **Anton**, **Bebas Neue**, **Archivo Black**, **Black Ops One**, Bungee, Bangers, Teko, Russo One, Orbitron, Audiowide, Staatliches, Monoton, Permanent Marker, **Alfa Slab One**, **Ultra**, **Bevan**, **Passion One**, **Titan One**, **Squada One**, **Rajdhani**, **Chakra Petch**, **Wallpoet**, **Goldman**, **Michroma**, **Stardos Stencil**, **Special Elite**, **Rye**, **Metal Mania**, **Pirata One**, **UnifrakturCook**, **New Rocker**, **Germania One**, and more. - **`lid_font_custom`** — type **any** font name to use it instead (this is a searchable **font picker** in MakerWorld’s editor). - **`lid_text_weight`** — Regular / Bold / Black / … ⚠️ **Set this to `Regular` for single-weight display fonts** (Anton, Bebas Neue, Bangers, Black Ops One, Alfa Slab One, etc.) or they fall back to the default. - **`lid_text_size`** — a real font size in mm (`0` = no text); it **auto-shrinks to fit** so long words never run off the edge. - **Alignment + padding** — `lid_text_halign` / `lid_text_valign` **anchor the text to that edge and grow it inward** (right-align fills right→left, left-align fills left→right — never cut off). **`lid_text_pad_l/r/t/b`** inset each side in mm to nudge it perfectly. - **`lid_text_orient`** — `horizontal` or `vertical`. ### `[Lid Design]` - **`lid_design_on`**, **`lid_design`** — `molecule`, `helix`, `honeycomb`, `logo`, or full-lid tilings `helix-full` / `honeycomb-full`. - **`lid_design_orient`** — horizontal / vertical / corner-TL/TR/BL/BR, plus **`halign` / `valign` / `pad`** (same edge-anchored behaviour as the text) and **`lid_pattern_scale`** for size. - **`lid_design_color`** — the design colour. **Layering:** where text and a design overlap, the **text reads on top** (the design is relieved out from under the letters), each in its own colour. > 🎨 **To print in two colours:** render the lid (`show_top`) and **export as 3MF** — each colour region becomes its own material for the AMS. (A single-material STL is also fully watertight.) --- ## 🔗 Hinge & Latch — engineered, not guessed **Ergonomic latch pry-lip** — a smooth, rounded ridge you hook a thumb under to pop the lid. Hulled (no sharp edges), self-supporting underside, and clear of the snap bump so the **secure close is unchanged**. Set with `latch_relief` / `latch_relief_size`. **Click-stop detent hinge** — the open lid **clicks and holds** at set angles instead of flopping. A rounded nub on the lid drops into rounded dimples on the barrel ends — and because the detent lives on the **hinge end faces**, it needs **no supports at any angle**. - **`detent_angles_deg`** = `[90, 120, 140, 160, 180, 210]` (210 = full-open back-stop) — edit to taste. - **`detent_phase`** nudges the click angles; **`detent_nub_proud`** firms the click; **`detent_bore_extra`** adds local relief *only* if a test print snaps on too stiffly. - This design survived a **multi-pass adversarial stress-test** — it’s tuned to flex the long lid spring by only a few tenths of a millimetre per click (low strain) with filleted features for fatigue life. **Third (center) hinge** — on wide boxes the long barrel can sag, so a center support cradle is **added automatically** when the box `width ≥ third_hinge_width_threshold` (160 mm) or when you set `enable_third_hinge`. The lid still snaps on in one motion and prints support-free. > 🧪 **Pro tip:** print a quick **one-knuckle test coupon** first to feel the snap + click, then fine-tune `detent_phase` / `detent_nub_proud` before committing to a big box. --- ## 🖨️ Print settings & tips - **Material:** PLA is great; **PETG** is tougher for the hinge. - **Layer height:** 0.20 mm. **Supports:** ❌ none needed — everything opens upward. - **Orientation:** print the **tray on its floor**, the **lid on its rim / top-face-down** (the slicer plates them correctly from the exported files). - **Two-colour lid:** assign the text/design region a second filament in the AMS (use the **3MF**). - **Vial fit:** `vial_clearance` controls the radial gap; `vial_z_clearance` is the air gap above a vial so the lid clears a crimp/flip cap. - **Hinge stringing/snapping at layer lines?** Slow the top layers, raise min-layer-time to ~10 s, or bump temp +5 °C. --- ## 📦 What’s included - The **parametric model** (`.scad`) — the whole project, fully customizable on MakerWorld. - A set of **ready-to-print example STLs** (various grids). - The built-in **lid designs** (molecule / helix / honeycomb) and the optional logo. --- ## ❤️ About / License Designed from scratch by **Keaton Hoskins** — MakerWorld **@thehoskins**. description: 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。 项目背景 在过去很长一段时间里，每次准备焊接，我都需要把电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡丝、烟雾净化器等工具一个个搬到桌面。 焊接结束后，又要逐一收回。 随着焊接工作越来越频繁，我发现真正浪费时间的并不是焊接本身，而是 准备焊接和整理桌面 。工具越来越多，桌面越来越拥挤，不仅影响工作效率，也让整个工作环境显得杂乱无序。 另一方面，我一直使用空气净化器作为临时方案处理焊接烟雾。随着焊接时间增加，我希望增加专业的焊烟过滤器，但市面上的产品大多是独立设备，这意味着桌面上又会增加一个新的设备，进一步加剧原本就混乱的焊接环境。 我开始意识到，我真正需要解决的问题，并不是增加一个新的工具，而是 重新组织整个焊接环境。 愿景 于是，我开始构思一个新的概念—— 焊接坞（SolderDock） 。 它不仅仅是一台焊烟过滤器，更应该成为焊接工作中所有常用工具的”停靠点”。 我希望它能够同时承担以下几个角色： 焊烟过滤 常用工具挂载 焊接工具收纳 模块化扩展平台 更重要的是，希望焊接结束后，我只需要移动一个设备，就能快速完成整个焊接环境的收纳，让工作台能够迅速从 焊接模式 切换到 装配、拼接、测量 等其它工作模式。 设计思考 既然希望所有工具最终都能围绕同一个主体展开，那么首先需要确定整个系统的核心。 观察整个焊接环境后，我发现焊烟过滤器本身就是体积最大的设备，也是所有工具中位置最固定的一部分，因此决定以焊烟过滤器作为整个”焊接坞”的核心。 随后，我开始寻找市面上的现成方案。 经过一段时间的调研后，我基本放弃了现有产品，原因主要有三个： 1. 体积与成本 过滤效果较好的产品通常体积较大，价格也相对较高，不适合作为桌面长期使用的中心设备。 2. 滤芯成本与维护 很多产品使用专用滤芯，不仅需要重新验证过滤效果，后期更换时也难以保证长期稳定购买，维护成本较高。 3. 扩展能力不足 市面上的焊烟过滤器几乎都是独立产品，并没有预留安装其它工具的可能，更无法作为整个焊接环境的中心。 因此，我希望最终的方案能够满足几个目标： 使用价格低廉且容易获得的标准滤芯； 成本尽可能低； 能够方便集成其它焊接工具； 保留后续模块化扩展能力。 实现方案 基础选型 整个设计首先从滤芯选型开始。 我希望直接采用已经成熟、供应稳定的标准滤芯，这样不仅能够降低成本，也方便后期长期更换。 最终，我选择了小米车载空气净化器所使用的滤芯。 原因很简单： 市场保有量大； 原厂、副厂滤芯供应充足； 更换成本低； 后续维护几乎没有压力。 确定滤芯之后，我曾考虑直接改造小米车载空气净化器。 不过很快发现两个问题。 第一，原机采用多面进风设计，作为焊烟过滤器时，无法将吸力集中到焊接区域。 第二，原机出风方向与理想结构并不一致，同时也没有预留任何工具挂载空间。 相比继续修改原机，重新设计整个外壳显然更加合理。 随后，我开始研究风扇和驱动方案。 最初计划单独购买离心风扇和驱动板，再重新设计整体结构。 但在比较价格时，我突然意识到： 直接购买二手小米车载空气净化器，反而比单独购买风扇和驱动电路更便宜。 于是最终选择拆解整机，仅保留： 风扇 驱动板 电源系统 除此之外，这块驱动板还带来了意外收获： 它不仅支持三档风速调节，还可以连接米家 App，通过蓝牙查看简单的空气质量信息，为整个产品增加了一些不错的交互体验。 结构设计 确定核心硬件后，整个设计开始围绕”焊接坞”这一理念展开。 优化风道 重新设计外壳，使进风口与出风口保持相对方向，让烟雾能够沿着更合理的路径流动，提高吸烟效率。 精准反向工程 由于原厂风扇安装孔位和接口均为异形结构，为保证装配精度，我通过 3D 扫描获取原始模型，并进行反向工程设计，使电机卡扣准确入位。 模块化扩展 外壳预留了大量标准 M3 安装孔，方便后续增加新的功能模块，也方便用户根据自己的需求进行扩展。 焊锡支架 顶部增加挡风罩，并将标准焊锡丝线轮集成其中，在保证风道效果的同时，也方便焊接过程中直接取锡。 焊锡分装收纳盒 整卷焊锡丝负责储存，分装盒负责使用。 通过可挂载的焊锡分装盒，让焊锡丝在 储存、收纳与焊接 之间自由切换。 PCB 夹具 通过金属万向软管安装 PCB 夹具，使夹具能够直接固定在焊接坞主体上，进一步减少桌面设备数量。 铜丝球清洁挂载 在侧面预留铜丝清洁球盒的挂载位置，将烙铁头清洁功能集成到焊接坞中，减少桌面独立设备。 电烙铁挂架 右侧设计了倾斜式电烙铁挂架。 这样的设计不仅符合日常使用习惯，还能够让烙铁余烟继续被吸入过滤器，同时降低误碰烫伤的风险。（这个设计来自一次真实的教训。） 图：电烙铁挂载图 快拆维护 采用快拆卡扣结构，更换滤芯无需拆卸整机。 同时，滤芯还能定期旋转角度，使滤材利用更加均匀，进一步延长使用寿命。 成品验证 最终，这套”焊接坞”基本实现了最初设定的目标。 电烙铁、PCB 夹具、焊锡等常用工具全部集中到一个主体上，现在只需一只手即可移动整个焊接环境，大幅降低了部署和收纳成本。 实际测试中，在关闭空调和风扇的室内环境下，焊烟能够在距离进风口约 12 cm 的位置被稳定吸入，满足日常焊接需求。 后续优化 目前，电烙铁和焊烟过滤器仍然采用独立供电。 下一阶段，我希望进一步整合供电系统，使整个焊接坞只需要一根电源线即可完成部署。 同时，也计划增加顶部辅助照明、更多可扩展模块以及统一的供电接口，让整个系统真正成为一个可持续扩展的模块化焊接平台。 本模型仅供个人下载使用，您不得以任何形式出售此模型的数字及物理打印版本。

Mein Hauptziel war jedoch, eine Lösung zu finden, die auch bei einem Kippfenster in den schmalen Spalt zwischen Fenster und Wand (ca. 3 cm ) passt. Für einen sicheren Halt sollte der Schlauch mit einer Metallschelle oder alternativ einem Kabelbinder befestigt werden. Hierfür wurde am Anschluss eine umlaufende Nut integriert, die verhindert, dass die Schelle oder der Kabelbinder vom Anschluss abrutschen kann. 🖨️ Druckprofile Dem Modell liegen zwei Druckprofile bei: Lange Version – ausschließlich für die Bambu Lab H2-Serie und A2-Serie geeignet. Diese Version ist für Kippfenster gedacht, bei denen der geöffnete Fensterflügel den Mauerüberstand um mindestens 3 cm überragt. Kurze Version – für alle übrigen Bambu Lab Drucker , mit Ausnahme des A1 mini . So kann je nach Drucker das passende Profil ausgewählt werden. 🌬️ Luftstrom Beim Design wurde darauf geachtet, dass der freie Querschnitt möglichst groß bleibt. Dadurch wird ein Luft- oder Wärmestau im Rohr vermieden, was das Risiko einer Überhitzung des angeschlossenen Geräts reduziert. 🖨️ Filament-Empfehlung ⚠️ PLA ist nur für kalte Abluft geeignet. Für warme Abluft , beispielsweise von Klimageräten, sollte unbedingt ein Filament mit höherer Wärmeformbeständigkeit verwendet werden. 🚦 Temperaturbeständigkeit (Richtwerte) 🔴 PLA: bis ca. 55–60 °C – nur für kalte Abluft geeignet 🟡 PETG: bis ca. 70–80 °C – für viele Anwendungen mit warmer Abluft gut geeignet 🟢 ASA: bis ca. 95–105 °C – empfohlen für höhere Temperaturen Ich selbst habe den Adapter aus PETG gedruckt und konnte damit bisher sehr gute Erfahrungen machen. 👍 ⚠️ Wichtiger Hinweis Bitte achtet darauf, dass es weder im Abluftrohr noch im angeschlossenen Gerät zu einem Wärmestau oder einer Überhitzung kommt . Ebenso sollte die Stelle, an der die Abluft ins Freie geleitet wird, ausreichend Platz bieten, damit die warme Luft ungehindert entweichen kann. Jede Einbausituation ist unterschiedlich. Prüft deshalb bitte vor der Verwendung, ob der Adapter für euren Anwendungsfall geeignet ist, und verwendet bei warmer Abluft stets ein entsprechend temperaturbeständiges Filament. A fully 3D-printed folding wall shelf that tucks flat against the wall when not in use and deploys a load-bearing support arm when you need it — practical, space-saving, and finished with a honeycomb underside for style. -- Why I made this - Most wall shelves are permanent fixtures. I wanted something that earns its space — a shelf that disappears when you don't need it and holds its own when you do. This design is 100% 3D printed (minus the wall screws and anchors you'll source locally) and built around a real folding mechanism rather than a novelty hinge. -- What it is - The shelf folds on a set of printed hinge knuckles: fold it up and it sits flush against the wall, fold it down and a pivoting support arm locks it into a horizontal position capable of handling real everyday loads. The underside of the shelf panel features a honeycomb pattern — so the face you see when it's folded up looks intentional, not bare plastic. All the structural work is done by the shelf panel, the support arm, and the hinge knuckles. The only hardware you need are wall screws and anchors appropriate for your wall type. -- Design details **Folding hinge knuckles** — printed-in geometry, no metal hardware at the pivot **Pivoting support arm** — braces the shelf against downward load when deployed **Honeycomb underside** — decorative and visible when the shelf is stowed -- How to print - Print in PLA+ for a lightweight indoor shelf or PETG if you want better humidity and temperature resistance. Either material works well here. ORIENTATION MATTERS, ALWAYS ORIENT IN A WAY WHERE LOADS WONT SHEAR THE Z LAYERING OF THE PRINT. - **Shelf panel** — lay flat on the bed, largest face down. - **Support arm** — lay flat on face so layer lines run along the arm's length; this puts the strongest layer orientation against bending loads, which is exactly where you need it. - **Hinge knuckles** — This is the trickier one, check overhanging geometry in your slicer before printing; orientation matters. - **20-30% infill** on all structural parts and many walls 4-5 (support arm, hinge knuckles, and cradle). ### Tips - Run a test fit of the hinge knuckles before final assembly — tolerances can vary slightly between printers; a quick pass with a small file cleans things up in seconds. - When mounting to drywall, use wall anchors rated for at least the load you plan to put on the shelf — the print will hold, so make sure the wall fastening matches. - PETG is the better choice for garages, laundry rooms, or anywhere with temperature swings or moisture. ### Assembly / Instructions 1. Print all parts: shelf panel, support arm, hinge knuckles/wall brackets and cradle. Check orientation notes before slicing. 2. Dry-fit the wall bracket onto the shelf panel. Verify smooth pivot motion; lightly sand or file any tight spots. 3. Attach the wall brackets shelf panel and place against the wall, level it out and mark the holes for each wall bracket. 4. Drill out marked holes and install anchors. 5. Place shelf with attached wall brackets against wall and screw into newly installed anchors (verify swinging action of shelf before installing) MY SHELF HAS BEEN INSTALLED FOR OVER 2 MONTHS WITH A SMALL PLANTER ON TOP, EVERYTHING IS HOLDING UP WITH NO SIGNS OF DEFORMATION OR STRESS. description: SnapHooks is a modular wall-mounting system, designed with flexibility in mind to provide a simple and secure solution for mounting items on the wall. description: Overview A customizable Skadis holder for round stuff, where you set the diameter and it does the rest. It hangs a row of round cups on an IKEA Skadis pegboard and holds just about anything cylindrical: glue sticks, markers, highlighters, screwdriver handles, small bottles, hobby paints, spray cans and WD-40. You really only set two things, the object diameter and how many cups you want. From there the customizer sizes the cups, packs them in next to each other and puts a Skadis hook behind each one at the nearest real slot. Heavy or wide cups get a second peg on their own so they can't tip out, and everything else is optional. Measure the object itself and type that number in, the model adds the fit gap for you so you're not left guessing tolerances (the optional floor hole works the same way). One thing worth doing before a big run: print a single cup first. Printer tolerances vary, so even if you know yours it pays to slice one cup at your diameter and check the object actually drops in before you print a whole row. A two-minute test is a lot cheaper than redoing a full board that came out a hair too tight. If the fit is off, nudge the Clearance a little (0.2 is snug, 0.3 is the default, 0.4 is looser) and reprint that one cup. Set the diameter — the customizer sizes every cup to fit. Highlights Diameter 10 to 80 mm, 1 to 12 cups in a row. Mixed sizes in the same row, so a wide can sits happily next to slim glue sticks. Heavy cups get a double peg automatically, and there's a thin-profile mode for short rows. Optional hole through the floor to pass a tool or screwdriver through. Native Skadis hook that fits both real Skadis (5 mm) and printed boards. Dimensions. The default 3 cup, 21 mm row comes out around 100 x 35 x 30 mm. Yours will depend on the diameter and count you choose. Compatibility. IKEA Skadis and Skadis-compatible printed pegboards (5x15 mm slots on a 40 mm grid). Cylinders up to 80 mm outside diameter. Printing. Print it standing up, with the panel flat on the bed and the cups opening upward. Any material is fine (PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA, PC). PETG is a solid all-rounder and PLA works perfectly well. Use a 0.4 or 0.6 mm nozzle and skip 0.8, which softens the detail and the fit. A bit of support on the rear pegs, none under the cups. Full customizer guide Every setting, if you want to fine-tune. What the settings control — diameter, clearance, wall, cup height, floor. Setting Default What it does Object diameter 21 mm The object's exact body diameter, 10–80 mm (any decimal). Measure it — the model adds the fit gap for you (set by Clearance). Count 3 Number of cups in the row, 1–12. Cup height 30 mm How far the cup wraps the object, 5–100 mm. Taller = steadier for tall/heavy items. Warns if a cup is too short for its diameter. Per-cup size off (0) Optional: give one cup its own diameter and/or height (0 = use the main size). Sits right under the main size. Pegs per cup auto (0) 0 = auto: 1 peg for light items, 2 for heavy/large. Or force 1–3. Heavy threshold 40 mm A cup at/above this diameter auto-gets a second peg. Single peg row off Thin-profile mode — forces all pegs into one row for the lowest backboard (best for short, light items). Clearance 0.3 mm The fit gap added to the diameter — applied to both the cup bore and the floor hole (a 30 mm object → a 30.3 mm bore). Measure exact and let the model add it. 0.3 (default) suits most prints — snug but slides in; 0.2 is very snug (only if you trust your printer); 0.4 plays it safe (looser). Wall 2.4 mm Cup wall thickness. Gap between cups 4 mm Spacing between neighbouring cups. Floor thickness 2 mm Every cup has a closed floor; this sets it. Floor hole 0 (off) The exact diameter of a tool/device to pass through every cup's floor (or to drain) — the model adds the same clearance as the cup. Any decimal. Per-cup override available. Plate thickness / margin / radius 3 / 5 / 7 mm Back panel: thickness, border around the cups, corner rounding. Board thickness 5 mm The Skadis board the pocket fits, 4–7 mm (standard Skadis is 5). Setup tips Measure exact, leave the tolerance to the model. Enter the object's true diameter, and if you use the floor hole, the true diameter of whatever goes through it. The model adds the Clearance to both, so you don't need to pad your own measurement. 0.3 (the default) suits most prints, snug but it still slides in. 0.2 is very snug, only worth it if you trust your printer. 0.4 plays it safe. One cup, two pegs. A single cup on one peg sits snug on the board, but with only one peg it can rotate a touch and a knock can twist it. For a steady single holder, set Pegs per cup to 2 so the two stacked pegs lock the rotation. (Auto already does this for heavy cups, and a row of three or more braces itself anyway.) Heavy or tall items. Keep it on auto (or force 2 pegs) and use a taller cup. Don't put a full can in single peg row mode, because it really wants the double peg. Thin profile. Turn on Single peg row for short items, like a tray of stubby markers, to get the lowest backboard possible. The pegs snap to the 40 mm Skadis grid, so a peg can sit slightly off a cup's centre and very close cups will share a peg. That's fine for light rows. Board grip. The default 5 mm board thickness fits standard Skadis. Drop it a little for a firmer grip on a thinner or printed board. How the pegs work Each cup gets a native Skadis hook that fills a 5x15 slot and catches behind the board. Heavy or wide cups (at or above the heavy threshold) automatically get a second peg stacked one slot below the first , a vertical pair that stops a full can from tipping out. Slim cups keep a single hook. Either way, every peg drops into a real slot at the same time. Turning on Single peg row overrides all of that and forces one thin row. The native hook catches behind the board. Hooks straight onto an IKEA Skadis board. Mixed sizes in one row Every cup uses the main diameter unless you give it one of its own. Set just the cup you want bigger and a wide can will still pack in tight next to a slim glue stick, with every hook landing in a real slot. The panel sizes itself to whatever row you build. Any size in one row — a fat can beside slim cups. anno_mixed.png Floor holes (optional) Cups are closed by default. You can open a hole through the floor, on every cup or just one, for a few reasons: to pass a screwdriver or tool through (handle in the cup, shaft poking out the bottom), to let a long object stick out the bottom, or to push something up from below to pop it out. Measure the exact diameter of whatever goes through and the model adds the same fit gap as the cup (the hole comes out as your diameter plus clearance), so it's a clean, snug pass-through. Print settings Setting Value Material Any. PLA, PETG, ABS/ASA or PC. PETG is a great everyday pick (fine indoors too) and PLA is perfectly fine. There's no real material limit here. The pricier engineering filaments just add heat and strength you probably don't need. Nozzle 0.4 or 0.6 mm (both print cleanly). Avoid 0.8 because it loses fine detail and the fit tolerances don't come out right. Layer height 0.2 mm Walls 5 at a 0.4 mm nozzle, 3 to 4 at 0.6 mm Infill 15 to 20% Supports None under the cups, light support on the rear pegs only Orientation Standing up, panel flat on the bed, cups opening upward Plate Single piece, no assembly More like this: part of my IKEA Skadis Organizers & Holders collection — more holders for the same board.

I've always had a soft spot for the SKÅDIS pegboard system — cheap, endlessly flexible, and there's an accessory for pretty much everything. But there was one thing I could never find for it: a version of one of my favorite pieces of design history, an iconic modular storage unit from the late 1960s, originally made as a single molded block of compartments and hooks. You can actually buy the original — it's a single molded block holding all the compartments at once — but it's pricey and pretty bulky for what is, at the end of the day, a desk organizer. So I decided to reinterpret it for the SKÅDIS ecosystem instead: I redesigned the whole thing from scratch as a set of separate, 3D-printable modules, each with its own hook built directly into the print, so they clip straight onto a vertical 37×56 SKÅDIS panel. The result is a family of 13 individual modules . Arrange them close together in the original grid layout and you get a look that's a clear nod to the source of inspiration — or spread them out, mix them with other SKÅDIS accessories, or use just a handful of them, however suits your desk and your workflow. Since each piece hangs independently, you're never locked into one fixed configuration the way you would be with a single molded block! You can use PLA or PETG (I actually used Pla Tough). Some modules need supports, but they're minimal and pop off cleanly with no visible marks afterward, because it's all internal. 🌬️ Tronic TLK 7000 C2 Zwei-Schlauch-Adapter | Massiver Effizienz-Boost! 🚀Hole das absolute Maximum aus deinem Tronic TLK 7000 C2 (Lidl Hausmarke) oder baugleichen mobilen Klimageräten! Dieses smarte, zweiteilige Upgrade verwandelt deine ineffiziente Einschlauch-Klimaanlage in ein hocheffizientes Zwei-Schlauch-System . Das Ergebnis: Der Raum wird deutlich schneller kalt, das Gerät verbraucht weniger Strom und du kannst spürbar größere Flächen kühlen. 💡 Warum ist dieses Design ein Gamechanger? (Die Physik dahinter) Das Problem im Originalzustand (Einschlauch): Mobile Klimageräte nutzen die mühsam gekühlte Raumluft, um den heißen Kompressor im Inneren zu kühlen, und blasen diese Luft durch den originalen Abluftschlauch nach draußen. Dadurch entsteht in der Wohnung ein massiver Unterdruck . Die Folge: Knallheiße Sommerluft (30°C+) wird permanent durch jede Türritze, jedes Schlüsselloch und jede Fensterdichtung von draußen wieder in die Wohnung gesaugt. Ein endloser, extrem ineffizienter Kampf! Die Lösung mit diesem Adapter (Zwei-Schlauch): Dieser zweiteilige Aufsatz kapselt das untere Ansauggitter (den Heißluft-Kreislauf des Kompressors) komplett ab. Über den neuen, zweiten Schlauch (Zuluft) saugt das Gerät die Luft zur Kühlung der Technik direkt von draußen an. Über den originalen Schlauch wird sie wieder nach draußen geblasen. Der Clou: In deiner Wohnung entsteht kein Unterdruck mehr! Die Raumluft wird im Inneren nur noch im Kreis gesaugt, eiskalt gefiltert und wieder abgegeben. Die Kälte bleibt im Raum, die Hitze bleibt draußen. Die Effizienz steigt um bis zu 50%! 🔩 Benötigtes Zusatzmaterial (BOM) Für den Zusammenbau und die Montage benötigst du folgendes Zubehör: 8x M3 Einschmelzgewinde (Gewindeeinsätze / Heat-Set Inserts, z.B. Ruthex) 8x M3 Zylinderkopfschrauben (M3x10mm oder M3x12mm sind ideal) Mindestens 6x Kabelbinder (um den Basisrahmen am Gitter der Klimaanlage zu fixieren) 1x Zusätzlicher flexibler Schlauch (Abluft-/Zuluftschlauch, Durchmesser passend zum gedruckten Stutzen wählen) (Zudem vielleicht ein Abdichtband für Fenster - bekommt man in jedem Baumarkt) Disclaimer: Notfalls lassen sich die zwei Teile ebenfalls mit dünnen Kabelbindern zusammenfügen OHNE die Einschmelzgewinde (ist so nur eleganter) 🛠️ Montageanleitung Das clevere, zweiteilige Design macht die Installation und spätere Wartung kinderleicht: Gewinde vorbereiten: Schmelze die 8x M3 Gewindeeinsätze mit einem Lötkolben vorsichtig in die dafür vorgesehenen Löcher des flachen Montagerahmens . Rahmen fixieren: Setze den Montagerahmen auf das untere Gitter der Klimaanlage. Nutze mindestens 6 Kabelbinder , um den Rahmen bombenfest am Kunststoffgitter zu verzurren (siehe Projektbild). Knipse die Enden der Kabelbinder sauber ab. Trichter aufschrauben: Setze den großen Trichteraufsatz auf den Rahmen und verschraube ihn mit den 8x M3 Schrauben. Vorteil: Für Filterreinigungen oder den Wintertransport kannst du den Trichter jederzeit abschrauben, ohne die Kabelbinder zu beschädigen! Schlauch anschließen: Stecke deinen neuen Zuluftschlauch auf den Stutzen und führe ihn (zusammen mit dem originalen Abluftschlauch) nach draußen – am besten durch eine feste Rollladen- oder Fensterblende. 🖨️ Empfohlene Druckeinstellungen (Print Settings) Material: PETG (ABS oder ASA) absolut empfohlen! Da die Schläuche und die Rückseite des Klimageräts im Hochsommer sehr warm werden können, ist normales PLA nicht hitzebeständig genug und könnte sich mit der Zeit verformen. Wände / Peripherie (Walls): Mindestens 3 bis 4 Wandlinien . Das Bauteil muss absolut luftdicht sein, damit keine Falschluft gezogen wird. Infill: 20% - 25% (Gyroid oder Grid) Support: Empfohlen! description: Most trash bag holders are either too bulky, too weak, or only designed for small bags. This one is different. The Full-Size Trash Bag Wall Holder is a compact wall-mounted solution designed to hold a large household trash bag securely while taking up almost no floor space. It is perfect for garages, laundry rooms, workshops, storage rooms, kitchens, cabins, utility spaces, 3D-printing areas, or anywhere you need a real trash bag without a full bin standing in the way. The main idea is simple: the bag is clamped evenly between the green frame and the black locking bars, then tightened with the blue knobs. This keeps the bag open, stable, and properly held in place without slipping down like many simple hooks or loose bag holders. Unlike many existing solutions, this is designed for full-size trash bags — not just small grocery bags or lightweight desk waste bags. It gives you the function of a large trash bin, but in a much cleaner and more space-efficient wall-mounted format. Why this is useful Traditional trash bins take up floor space, are awkward to clean around, and are often bigger than needed. Simple bag hooks save space, but usually do a poor job of keeping the bag open and secure. This design solves both problems by giving the bag a solid frame and a proper clamping mechanism. The open frame also makes it easy to see when the bag is full, remove it quickly, and replace it without fighting with a bin liner. Key features Full-size trash bag support Space-saving wall-mounted design Secure clamping with screw knobs Keeps the bag open and easy to use No bulky floor bin needed Great for garages, workshops, laundry rooms, storage rooms and kitchens Printed in separate parts for easier printing and color customization Strong geometric frame design with low material use Easy to mount to a wall Design notes The frame uses a lightweight geometric structure to keep the design strong without making it unnecessarily bulky. The bag is held between the front locking bars and the main frame, with the knobs tightening everything in place. This is especially useful because there are not many full-size trash bag holder solutions like this on MakerWorld right now. Most designs are either small bag holders, simple hooks, or bulky bin-style prints. This model is meant to fill that gap: a practical, printable, household-size trash bag holder that actually holds the bag properly. If you have any suggestions for improvements, feel free to let me know :) Installation Pictures and video shows assembly of the two sides. Mount one of the sides first securely to the wall using suitable screws for your wall type. The click in the second side and screw it in as well. Insert the bag between the frame and the locking bars, then tighten the knobs until the bag is held evenly at the corners. Do not overload the bag beyond what your wall mounting and material choice can safely handle.

description: Press the Customize button to customize! A fully parametric open-top mesh basket: pick a rectangle or ellipse boundary, a solid border frame, and one of five interior grid patterns. Add an optional snap-fit lid, printed as a separate piece, that clicks onto the basket with a continuous printable ridge/groove around the whole rim. Looking for a flat mesh panel with mounting screw holes instead? That's a separate listing: Parametric Mesh Panel Generator . Key Features Rectangle or ellipse boundary: set overall width and depth (or diameter, for a circle) directly Five grid patterns: square, diagonal (45 degree square), hexagonal honeycomb, triangular, and staggered circular holes; every pattern tessellates edge to edge with a uniform strut width between holes Open-top basket: solid bottom panel plus mesh side walls; 4 flat walls for a rectangle, one continuous wrapped curved wall for an ellipse Solid bottom / solid sides toggles: make the bottom panel or the side walls solid (no mesh) independently of each other Snap-fit lid: an optional separate piece (switch the Customizer's view to lid) with a skirt that slides inside the basket opening and clicks into place Solid lid top toggle: make the lid's top plate solid instead of meshed 3D-printable snap ridge: the ridge/groove is a single continuous triangular bead wrapped around the entire rim, tapered to a self-supporting 45 degree slope so it prints with no supports on either the basket or the lid Auto-sized holes and struts: hole_size and strut_width default to 2.5x your nozzle diameter when left at 0, so a fresh copy prints cleanly without any tuning Pattern rotation: rotate the whole grid independently of the panel's default orientation Print Settings Setting Recommended Basket orientation Print flat, bottom panel down Lid orientation view = "lid" already outputs it flipped, plate-down on the bed Supports Not required for either piece Perimeters 2-3 Infill 15-20% Material PLA or PETG Download the optimized print profile from this page, delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STL into it. How to Use Outer Shape: set shape to rectangle or ellipse, then outer_x, outer_y, and thickness. Border: set border_width; 0 removes it entirely. Basket: set basket_height for the side wall height. Use basket_solid_bottom or basket_solid_sides if you want part of the basket solid instead of meshed. Lid (optional): turn on lid_enable, set lid_skirt_height and lid_fit_clearance to match your basket opening, and leave lid_notches_enable on for the snap fit. Switch view to lid and re-export to get the separate lid STL. Pick a pattern: choose pattern and, if you want a specific look, set hole_size and strut_width; leave both at 0 to auto-size from nozzle_diameter. Export the STL (once for view = "model", once more for view = "lid" if you enabled the lid), delete the sample models off the plate, and import your STLs into it. Customization Use the MakerWorld Customizer. All parameters are grouped and annotated. View - view: model renders the basket, lid renders the separate lid piece (only produces geometry when lid_enable is also on) Outer Shape - shape: rect for a rectangle, ellipse for an ellipse or circle - outer_x: overall width, X axis (mm) - outer_y: overall depth, Y axis (mm) - thickness: panel / wall material thickness (mm) Border Frame - border_width: solid border frame width around every face (mm); 0 = no border Basket - basket_height: height of the side wall(s), measured up from the top of the bottom panel (mm) - basket_solid_bottom: make the bottom panel solid instead of meshed - basket_solid_sides: make the side wall(s) solid instead of meshed Lid - lid_enable: add a snap-fit lid - lid_solid_top: make the lid's top plate solid instead of meshed - lid_skirt_height: depth the lid's skirt reaches down inside the basket opening (mm) - lid_fit_clearance: gap between the skirt and the inside of the basket walls, per side (mm) - lid_notches_enable: add the continuous snap ridge/groove around the rim - lid_notch_depth: how far the ridge/groove projects past the nominal skirt/wall surface (mm) - lid_notch_band: vertical height of the ridge/groove's tapered profile (mm); must be at least 2x lid_notch_depth for a printable 45 degree slope - lid_notch_offset: distance from the top of the wall/skirt down to the center of the ridge/groove (mm) Mesh Pattern - pattern: square, diagonal, hex, triangle, or circle - hole_size: hole size (mm); flat-to-flat, edge length, or diameter depending on pattern; 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - strut_width: wall width between holes (mm); 0 = auto (2.5x nozzle diameter) - pattern_rotation: extra rotation applied to the whole pattern (degrees) Printer - nozzle_diameter: drives the auto strut/hole sizing and minimum-feature warnings (mm) Pattern Notes Every pattern is built as a continuous solid lattice rather than a punch-through grid of disconnected holes, so the remaining material always stays one connected piece. Triangular and circular holes sit on the same tightly-packed triangular lattice as the hex pattern, so every hole is equidistant from its six neighbors and the gap between any two adjacent holes is a uniform strut width. Snap-Fit Lid Notes The lid's skirt slides inside the basket's top opening, and a continuous triangular ridge on the skirt cams past the basket wall until it seats into a matching groove cut into the wall, holding the lid down with a light friction snap. Both the ridge and the groove taper at a 45 degree slope (never more), so the whole feature prints cleanly with no supports on either piece. If the fit feels too tight or too loose, adjust lid_fit_clearance; if the snap feels weak, try increasing lid_notch_depth a little (keeping lid_notch_band at least 2x that value). Sizing Tips If holes print closed or clogged, increase hole_size well above 2.5x your nozzle diameter. If struts look flimsy or go missing, increase strut_width; anything thinner than 2.5x your nozzle diameter will not print as designed.

An open-source clamshell holder generator for openGrid , using the openConnect system. The holder can be used to mount objects either under a desk, often in combination with the Underware system, or on a wall. A common use case is holding power strips, but the dimensions and openings can be adjusted for a wide range of object shapes. Several example .stl files are included, with the parameters used to generate them in the file names. Customization guide: Measure the item. Set "item_width" , "item_height" , and "item_depth" . Adjust "item_corner_rounding" based on the item's shape. Add a little clearance if you want the item to slide in easily. For a heavy item, you may want to increase "holder_thickness" to make the holder sturdier. Set "holder_slot_position" . "Top" makes the item face forward when mounted on a wall, or downward when mounted under a desk. You can also choose "Front", which makes the item face sideways when mounted under a desk. Adjust the front opening. Use "front_opening_side_margin" and "front_opening_end_margin" . Larger margins create a smaller front opening, which may interfere with use, such as blocking the outlets of a power strip. Adjust the side openings. Use the "side_opening_x_margin" parameters. The side opening can be enabled on one side, both sides, or disabled completely. The position and size of the opening are highly customizable. Set "holder_slot_column_limit" . This value defaults to the minimum of 1, which saves filament and helps with heat dissipation. Increase it if you want the holder to cover more of the item. Set "slot_slide_direction" . "Left" and "Right" are usually used for under-desk mounting, while "Up" and "Down" are usually used for wall mounting. Choose the direction that lets the holder slide onto the openConnect slots from the accessible side. "generate_holder_part" : "Both" shows a good preview of the result, so it is recommended during customization. The "Left" and "Right" options allow different parameters for each part and automatically orient the model for 3D printing, which is convenient when exporting the result. The model is open-source under the CC-BY-SA license. Like all the OpenSCAD models I've designed for openGrid, it can be found in this GitHub repository . Feel free to use the code; feedback and suggestions are welcome.

description: Esta muleta para niños fue diseñada por Montmaker.3D, el diseño contempló la evaluación mecánica para el material PETG, dando como resultado que es recomendable imprimir en PETG o superior. Es importante resaltar que no deben modificar el archivo, si lo hacen no nos hacemos responsables por cualquier perjuicio ocasionado. Consideraciones de impresión: Material : PETG o Superior (No usar PLA). Usar TPU para la base. Descarga el .3mf y usa las configuraciones tal como se presentan ahi, si no tienes bambu studio, por favor, instalalo y adapta el modelo antes de imprimir, este modelo tiene modificadores que aseguran la rigidez. Personaliza con stickers, coloca mensajes de aliento, esto va para niños. Imprime SOLO si es necesario, siempre recomiendo usar una de aluminio, si no esta disponible usar esta temporalmente. Paso a paso: 1. Debes imprimir el aro para que asegures que el diametro del palo de escoba coincida con el modelo, en caso que no, reduce maximo un 2% del modelo, para incrementar el tamaño no hay problema. El diámetro correcto es el que ofrece fricción suficiente para moverlo, no debe quedar suelto. No imprimas el modelo sin hacer este paso, el modelo debe coincidir con el diámetro del palo que estes usando. No imprimas el modelo genericamente, ya que, el diametro no coincidirá. 2. Coloca la pieza de TPU abajo como si fuera una escoba normal, no es necesario apretar mas de lo suficiente. 3. Introduce la primera tuerca con la parte ancha hacia abajo y la parte fina hacia arriba, colocala a la altura del paciente (Proximamente mas recomendaciones de esto sobre las alturas). 4. Introduce el mango inferior. 5. Aprieta la tuerca gentilmente hasta que ya no gire gentilmente, luego girar 1/4" de vuelta con la mano, no usar herramientas, asegurate que no deslice. NO SOBRE APRIETES, SI SE DEZLIZA ES QUE NO SEGUISTE BIEN LAS RECOMENDACIÓN DEL PASO 1 6. Introduce la 2da tuerca tal como el paso #3. 7. Introcuce el mango superior. 8. Repite el paso 5. 9. Con un destornillador, introduce 02 tornillos tirafondo de drywall de maximo 3/4" (20mm) de longitud en el mango superior. (usa los de color negro que venden en la ferreteria mas cercana). 10. Aprieta los tornillos tirafondo con un destornillador hasta que entre en el palo, asegurandote de que quede a la altura del paciente. Note: Para el preensamblado por favor no colocar los tornillos. Selección del palo de escoba: -Evitar el uso de palos que sean de madera comprimida (blancos). -Evitar el uso de palos astillados o con fisuras. -Evitar el uso de palos con nudos. -Evitar el uso de palos doblados. -Evitar el uso de palos viejos o desgastados. -Golpear el palo a 10cm de altura y dejar caer para prueba de sonido, debe sonar como algo sólido. Con amor❤️: Ing. Mecánico Fernando Armas. SÍGUEME EN: INSTAGRAM / TIKTOK
