description: ****Please read the full description before you ask any questions in the comments because chances are I already answered it in the description! If you’re unable to view the description for some reason, I highly recommend using the MakerWorld website/browser version so you can access as much information about the model as possible before printing anything! *****In case it isn’t obvious, DON’T (I repeat, DON'T) try to print the fully-assembled figure included in the project! It's only there as a REFERENCE for what the final assembled figure should look like! It’s not a “print-in-place” version, and if you try to print the example reference assembly, it won’t be able to articulate whatsoever and it’ll basically just be a statue, and that’s IF it even prints successfully at all without totally failing! You have been warned! If anyone asks me about it in the comments then that means they didn’t read the description, and I highly recommend you read the description because there’s some pretty important info in here! This updated, newly-articulated V2 version of my original V1 Customizable Minecraft Skin Figure is my entry into the 2026 MakerWorld Children’s Toy Design Contest. Inspired by my childhood love for designing my own Minecraft Skins on “Miners Need Cool Shoes” as well as my desire to have a perfect Jazwares action figure of my own custom Minecraft character, this fun and interactive MakerWorld project allows Minecraft fans of all ages to learn how to pixel-paint and customize their very own Minecraft figures using the provided template figure (just like making a Minecraft Skin using a Skin Editor website) and 3D-print a fully-articulated game-accurate action figure of their own Minecraft character! To help explain how to customize the template figure, and to prevent any unnecessary confusion for any other MakerWorld users, I recorded a full video tutorial showcasing how to use Bambu Studio to pixel-paint and customize the template figure, as well as how to use the brand new Customizable 3D Hat Item Head to custom-“model” your own 3D Player Head, and how to virtually “assemble” your painted figure within the project as an example reference to help you get a better idea of how your figure will look once all the pieces are printed and put together! (***NOTE: the virtually “assembled” figure is just an example reference and is NOT intended to be printed on one plate! It is not a “print-in-place” model, and it will not feature any articulation if you attempt to print it fully-assembled!) The tutorial video can be found embedded on this project page, as well as on my YouTube channel “Jaebii’s Media Center” (feel free to subscribe, but be aware not all of my channel content is Minecraft/3D-printing related and some of it might not be particularly suitable for younger viewers). Included as an additional print profile for this project is my custom “Jaebii” figure, which I designed during the tutorial video based on my own custom in-game Minecraft Skin! If you’d like, feel free to print your very own Jaebii figure to display and play alongside your own Minecraft characters! In addition, feel free to add your own customized figure projects to this post as new print profiles if you’re comfortable with sharing them for other users to download and print! I’d love to see what everyone else is able to come up with, and I think it would be really fun to print other users’ figures myself to include as additional examples of ways the template figure can be used to design unique Minecraft action figures! You can also use the Jaebii print profile as a reference for how I personally decided to orient the pieces I ended up printing for my figure, although depending on the color placement of your pieces, you might want to orient your pieces differently from mine. Be sure to pay close attention to your supports, your plastic presets, temperature settings, object placement and orientation, and all other printer settings or preferences you may prefer. Compared to my V1 Customizable Minecraft Skin figure design, which used square assembly pegs and was more of a “poseable statuette” than an articulated “action figure,” this new V2 design is upgraded to have a full range of articulation similar to official Jazwares/Mattel Minecraft figures, while maintaining the seamless game-accurate Minecraft character model without any noticeable joints or articulation points! These new articulation joints also make the assembly process so so so much easier and more intuitive than it was before (though I’d still suggest using a hairdryer to slightly heat up the joint sockets during assembly to make everything easier to plug in, but NOT the joints themselves), and they allow for much easier swappability between alternate parts and replacements for broken parts (the neck can even be printed either attached to the torso or separated from the torso as an individual piece in order to make it easier to replace if the neck breaks). The arms can rotate 360 degrees around and stretch outwards slightly, the legs can stretch forward and backward (and somewhat outwards), and the head can rotate, look up and down, tilt side to side, and pop upwards slightly to create enough clearance for the arms to pose diagonally without bumping into the corner of the head! Much like the V1 design, the only way to make the legs able to achieve a “sitting” pose is to use the special “sitting” torso variant, where the legs connect into the front of the torso instead of the bottom of the torso. But unlike the V1 figure, the sitting variant is able to achieve the sitting pose a lot more effectively and accurately! The joint sockets mostly use negative object cutouts to print the holes, and it seems like the sockets will ALWAYS print as the base color the OBJECT is set to no matter what you pixel-paint on the outside. This can definitely prove to be a little inconvenient for pieces like the Item Holding Arms, which will have both a shoulder joint socket and an Item/Accessory Holding cutout, which will both be whichever color the Arm Object is set to. You might find it easier to simply use the “Mesh Boolean Subtraction” tool to subtract either the negative object shoulder socket or the hand cutout in order to paint/place manual supports inside the holes. UNFORTUNATELY, using ANY Mesh Boolean function on a pre-painted object will erase ALL painting from it (which is why I tried to use negative objects instead, since it’s easier to modify if necessary), so I only recommend doing that if your Arms/Legs are as easy to pixel-paint as my Jaebii Skin Figure design. My suggestion would be to make the cutout Arm styles the base color of whatever your HAND needs to look like, since you won’t really be able to see inside the shoulder joint sockets anyway. I know it might result in making the multicolor printing process take unnecessarily longer and use more material than preferable, but as long as you print as many styles of Arms on the same plate as possible, your multicolor printing waste should be comparatively minimal, relatively-speaking. This new V2 version of my design also includes a brand new type of Head option: a Customizable 3D Hat Item Head! This piece is similar to the normal 2D Cube Head geometrically, but it includes an outer layer of half-height individual pixels placed along each side of the cube (except the bottom), allowing you to essentially custom-“model”/“sculpt” your own unique 3D Player Head by deleting/recoloring each pixel until you have an exact replica of your Minecraft Skin’s 3D Hat Item! In order to do this, you’ll need to be able to click on each individual pixel object included in the merged object group (which can be accessed by switching from “global” to “object” on the left menu panel). Unfortunately, the only way I was able to figure out how to click on each specific pixel I wanted to delete was to first switch from clicking on the object group itself to clicking on the individual parts of the group, which to my knowledge can only be done by first clicking on any of the object parts within the object group on the left panel, and THEN clicking directly on the individual pixel you want to delete inside the plate. If anyone else knows an easier way to switch to a mode that allows you to click directly on an individual part within a merged object group on the plate rather than automatically defaulting to clicking on the full assembled object group, then by all means use that method instead! And tell me how to do it in the comments while you’re at it! And if you’re confused about the method I tried to explain, then be sure to watch the customization tutorial video I recorded and pay close attention to where I’m clicking so you can learn how to do it too! I also discovered that sometimes a Minecraft Skin’s Player Head has more than four colors including the colors for the eyes, which are usually white and whichever particular eye color. For that reason, I wanted to design a few additional Head options with removable separated eyes, which can be printed separately as individual pieces (each with four maximum colors) and plugged into the eye sockets, which allows for four total colors on the Separated Eye Head options without needing to waste any of your colors on the eyeballs! There are four Separated Eye Head styles, each with a different variation of eye size/position, which is hopefully enough to cover a majority of desired Player Skins. For assembly, I’d definitely suggest using a hairdryer to heat up the eye sockets and maybe even the eyeballs themselves a little bit, then just press the eyes all the way into the eye sockets! For reference, I included an example customized 2D Head for each of the styles of Separated Eye Heads, featuring skins that I’ve either already designed for personal commissions, or that I personally like! These include LadyAgnes (Agnes Larsson from Mojang, often seen during Minecraft LIVE), Super Mario (previous commission), my Player Head from the ORIGINAL version of my Minecraft Skin (which I have a very old Shapeways 3D-printed statuette of, the precursor to all my endeavors on my quest for the perfect customizable Minecraft Skin action figure), and MineyLO (previous commission). You can also combine the Separated Eye Head options with the Customizable 3D Hat Item Head! To do this, simply place both Heads on one plate, then right-click on the plate and press “select all” then click “merge,” and once both Heads are combined into a single merged group, use the “move object” tool to move the Separated Eye Head to the exact same X,Y,Z coordinates of the normal Cube Head inside the Hat Item Head, then delete the spare Cube Head and leftover neck joint negative object. Alternatively, before merging the objects, you can attempt to right-click & “center” both Heads to the middle of the plate, then merge them and delete the duplicates. By combining the 3D Hat Item Head with the Separated Eye Head, you can effectively print a custom 3D Head with a maximum of 4 colors without worrying about the colors for the eyes taking up part of that limit! Also, if your Player Head needs separated eyeballs but one of the eyes is covered up or obscured by the character’s hair, you can try using one of the example customized 2D Separated Eye Heads with the eyeballs ALREADY inserted and simply delete whichever eyeball you need to print separately as an individual object (which can be done through the object group panel on the left), and use the “fill by connected object” paint tool to recolor the inserted eye to be the same color as the hair/skin/whatever. That way, you’ll have a customizable 2D Head with only ONE separated eye socket, which you can reposition inside the 3D Hat Item Head assembly to replace the default 2D Cube Head. It ain’t perfect, but sometimes 3D design requires a lot of creative finagling and out-of-the-box thinking to solve problems in unique ways, and it’ll make your skills as a designer even stronger as a result! If necessary in order to avoid your printer’s color maximum limitations, it might be feasible to print your Player Head’s 3D Hat Item layer SEPARATELY from the 2D Cube Head underneath. To do this, you would simply need to access the object group for your customized 3D Head and delete the inner Cube Head, leaving behind only the layer of 3D pixels. You can then attempt to print the Hat Item layer on its own as long as EVERY pixel is still connected and touching every other pixel. If your Hat Item piece has floating pixels or pixels that aren’t attached to any other pixel, then it probably won’t work. In order to achieve the maximum number of multicolor pieces per Player Head, you could attempt to combine a Separated Eye Head (with attachable multicolor eyes) with a separated Hat Item layer, which would allow for the highest amount of individual multicolor pieces available to assemble your 3D Player Head using as many colors as you might need! However, 3D Hat Item pieces may not assemble perfectly onto the 2D Head geometry when printed separately, since that wasn’t really the design intention when I created it. The 3D pixels are partially embedded inside the 2D Head, meaning if you attempt to print the Hat Item Layer separately and attach it like a hat or helmet, the pixels might not fit OVER the 2D Head. You can attempt to experiment with increasing the size of the Hat Item layer to make it fit overtop the Cube Head, as well as using the Mesh Boolean Subtraction tool to cut out the 2D Head from the rest of the Hat Item pixels in order to make them geometrically fit over the edges of the 2D Head OR try converting the 2D Head object into a NEGATIVE OBJECT to make it cut out the size of the Cube Head from the 3D pixels (theoretically), but either way, attempting to print the 3D Hat Item layer as a separate piece from the Cube Head itself is an unintended and untested process and may not result in the desired outcome. Printer discretion is advised. Print at your own risk. You have been warned. While assembling the Separated Neck Piece option for my customized Jaebii figure, I noticed that the square neck peg sat too far/deep inside the torso, which slightly prevented the arm joints from plugging into the shoulder sockets all the way and made the arms look like they were sticking out too far. In order to resolve this, I made an updated version of the Separated Neck that has a shorter attachment peg which won’t reach as far inside the torso, meaning the arm sockets won’t be blocked by the neck anymore. The neck ought to be able to stay connected to the torso easily enough, but once you have the head attached to the neck and you’re sure the neck hasn’t been squished or twisted or broken, you MAY want to consider glueing the neck peg inside the torso, just to help prevent the neck/head from popping off the body since the neck peg is so short. But you might not need to. The updated Separated Neck Piece is now downloadable as an additional print profile if your figure requires it! Let me know if you notice any other weird geometric inconsistencies that I might have missed while printing my example figures and I’ll do what I can to create a fix for it! Another thing I wanted to briefly mention was the figure’s scale. By default, all of my Minecraft figures are designed to scale accurately with the original Jazwares Minecraft toys, because those were the Minecraft toyline I personally grew up with. However, I realize that the current Mattel Minecraft toyline is also very prominent and features its own separate scale compared to the Jazwares toys, so I wanted to quickly provide an easy measurement formula to help with rescaling the figures/parts to scale more accurately with the Mattel figures instead. The calculated virtual height of the fully-assembled default/Jazwares-scale template figure is 2.68 inches (6.08 cm, or 68.0837 mm). The official height of the Mattel Minecraft Player figures is roughly 3.25 inches (8.25 cm, or 82.5515 mm), meaning the fully assembled template figure would need to be rescaled using the object sizing tool to be a height of 82.5515 mm, which results in a 121.25% scale increase. In order to apply this scale increase to the individual body parts (as well as any compatible accessories), I’d suggest right-clicking on a plate with at least two objects on it at the same time and clicking “select all” and THEN using the sizing tool while multiple objects are selected. This is because some of the objects MIGHT be slightly rescaled in the project already (for example, some parts might be sized at 99% instead of 100% to help with articulation tension), so in order to make sure you’re resizing the parts starting at “100%” it’s a good idea to select multiple objects at the same time, which will grab them all at “100%” of their current size (regardless of whatever their current size percentage is). I’m an artist, not a mathemagician, so when it comes to percentages and measurements, this is sorta the best I can do. Geometrically-speaking, these V2 figures are fully compatible with the accessories I designed previously for the V1 version, including all the tools and weapons, and the Customized Capes which are available as a separate print profile on the V1 figure upload. description: I am happy to present the “Infinity Infill Cube” , my very own version of the famous fidget combining my take on the hinge mechanism while showcasing 16 different infills with accompanying text . This model is simply a must to have next to your printer, as an infill display while also being the most popular and fun fidget . Overall, this model turned out way better than I expected and I could not be happier to share it with you all! Membership If you want to sell this model you can do so by joining the Membership for a commercial licence. The Model I started by making my own version of the Infinity Cube Fidget mechanism, trying to minimize the size of the hinges . For printability, the model contains a number of support “points” which makes the model printable. This results in some minor trimming being required after printing. Similarly, some “brim” structures are included in the print profiles, to minimize issues for people with bed adhesion issues. After making my own version of the Infinity Cube , I continued all work within Bambu slicer . Here I added 16 different “infills” to be shown within the fidget. In addition, the name of each “infill” was also added to the fidget. While I set out to make a multicolour version of this fidget (which looks great), I really ended up liking the single colour version the most. If you do not have a multi-nozzle printer, I really recommend printing the single colour version . Compared to most fidgets of this design , this model generates a heavy 50g fidget which takes a while to print (with my profiles). The weight was a result of the design choices, but I really think the “Infinity cube” feels better in the hands when heavy . While I provide a number of print profiles for the “Infinity Infill Fidget”, I can only provide a single .STL file of the “Base” Infinity Cube model. The model showcases 16 different infills available in Bambu Slicer: Gyroid - 15% Concentric - 40% Archimedes Chords - 40% Hilbert Curves - 30% 3D Honeycomb - 15% Honeycomb - 20% Octagram Spiral - 30% 2D Lattice - 15% Aligned Rectilinear - 30% Tri-Hexagon - 30% Cross Hatch - 20% Cubic - 30% Zig Zag - 25% Grid - 30% Adaptive Cubic - 30% Triangles - 30% Printing As all Infinity Cubes, this one might be a little demanding to print . That being said, I have had no issues at all. I expect that poor bed adhesion will be an issue, and have for this reason slowed down the first layer of the print profiles. I recommend printing the single colour version as the text looks the best in this version (in my opinion). If you have a printer with multiple nozzles , the multicolour prints are nice, although I which I could have made the font larger. If you decide to print the multicolour versions with a single nozzle, I have also added a print profile (Multicolour profile - Plate 3) which includes a second “Infinity Cube” used as a purge object (giving you 2 fidgets for the price of 1). Post-processing As with all versions of this fidget, playing around with it will make it move more smoothly . In addition, I would recommend some trimming with a sharp blade . In particular, the 4 brim structures needs to be removed . In addition, some trimming of the many minor support structures will make it both look and feel nicer. Overall, compared to other similar models I have printed, this one is relatively loose and smooth to move . Overall, I am just so happy with how this turned out! I am really looking forward to see photos of your colour combinations and hope you will enjoy this print as much as I have! If you make changes to the infills, I also look forward to additional print profiles !! description: Nosk is a terrifying shape-shifting spider creature from Hollow Knight, faithfully recreated as a detailed 3D printed figure capturing its iconic spider body, long curved legs, and the haunting false mask dangling from its chest. Its intricate details, from the flowing mane to the glowing red accents that make Nosk one of the most unsettling bosses in Hallownest… and… it glows oO I also realized I did not print out and attach the front arms before making the cover photo… sigh . After you print them, get some hot water (per instructions below) dip the end of the leg to soften and place where and how the arms should face. Then after it hardens, dip again in glue and secure it. INSTRUCTIONS This is an annoying one, but if you ever assembled my models; you know you are in for some frustration and glue on your fingers :D Print everything out, and assemble the legs. Remember if you are using superglue, very tiny amounts are needed to join the legs together. The legs come in two variations, with a cable run to pass a wire for the inner glow, and solid. The cable ones are much much more annoying to glue. The cable must be ultra fine, since you only have 4mm of space. I used aRGB and a addresable LED controller for mine (more details an pics to follow) once done, glue the torso together, inserting the orange belly. Try your best to keep it as aligned as possible. Later insert the legs and spines. If legs dont seem to fit, or the legs are not all aligned to the floor DO NOT PANIC! For this one, hot water, hair dryer or a blowtorch lighter is a must. Soften the plastic a bit and insert it to get the correct shape or bend the leg so it is flat to the ground. The holes were designed to be symmetrical, but after gluing, they are not going to be.. and thats fine, Nosk is weird, so heat it and bend his legs any way you want to make it unique (its a feature!) Any issues, shoot me a comment.

description: A push bike that rolls on four empty spools, fully 3D printed with zero hardware. The basics: Snap-together assembly: no hardware or tools required Wheels: 4× empty filament spools Rider: ages Toddler to 6, up to ~60 lb Sized for P1S and up: segmented to fit with no supports Never printed anything this big? Most people haven't - plenty of us never get past desk trinkets, and that's exactly who I built this for. The part count might look intimidating, but for a vehicle a kid actually rides, it's remarkably lean. It took a fair bit of design and testing by my kids to get it there. Assembly is styled like your favorite brick system: a big illustrated, step-by-step PDF that walks you through it part by part. If you can print and follow pictures, you can build this. Beyond filament, you need nothing. No bolts, no bearings, no glue, no trip to the hardware store. Every joint snaps or threads together with printed parts. The only "extra" item is plastic-safe lubricant (not WD-40, a non-spray silicone or white lithium grease, such as "Plastic Gear Grease") which makes steering significantly easier. It can be added after assembly or skipped entirely and the bike still works, your kid just has to stand up to change the steering angle. It's a system, not just a bike. This is the Panda kit of the Spoolster system. I built the blacked-out Nightfall kit first, my kid took one look and decided it needed to be cuter, so here's the Panda: black-and-white with a panda face up front, and upcoming accessories adding a little bamboo flag, and a cupholder. The seat, front, and attachments all swap on the same core, so the bike can be updated to become whatever your kid's into. On the spools: I designed the hubs around Bambu and SUNLU (reusable V3) spools since those are what I had piling up. Other plastic spools will likely work: skip the hub adapters and run the axle straight through the spool's center hole, or print a custom hub to fit yours. I'd be wary of cardboard spools though; I haven't tested any and can't vouch for them holding up. Why I built it: After printing an entire wheelchair for charity I saw the power of large prints cleverly segmented with bed sized chunks. Between that and two kids, my empty spools were piling high and I wanted to find a functional use for them. Turning a pile of garage trash into something my kid can actually ride felt like the right kind of mission. What's next: more kits, and whatever you all come up with — the bike has accessory points (documented in the build appendix) and is remixable, so build a kit for whatever your kid loves and tag me. I want to see them. Safety Note ⚠️: Adult supervision, helmet, flat ground, and mind the 60 lb rider limit. It's a toy, not a way to get to school. Not responsible for any injuries or accidents that may occur.

BOOBY-TRAP - Bookcase Edition BOOBY-TRAP Bookcase Edition aka OH SNAP! Is a classic game of the 60's featuring a BOARD with a SPRING BAR pulled back with dozens of SMALL CIRCULAR PIECES held under the pressure of the spring bar. Play consists of removing pieces from within the spring bar "trap" in hopes of not making it move. Different sized pieces removed are worth points each. Point penalties are incurred if the bar moves or pieces snap out. The player who has accumulated the most points at the end of the game is the winner. GAME COMPONENTS The BOOBY-TRAP Bookcase Edition set includes: 12 Red pieces worth 3 points each 12 Blue pieces worth 2 points each 12 Yellow pieces worth 1 point each 1 Board and Board End Cap 1 Pull Spring Bar Assembly 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The BOOBY-TRAP Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the all the game tiles. To store the parts, first gentle release the pressure of the spring bar by retracting the bar into the game board. Then add the playing pieces to the board behind the spring bar. Place the board in the box. Place any spare parts also in the box. Slide the box lid onto the box. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. INFORMATION, PARTS & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued. The book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. IMPORTANT NOTE: I've turned off the prime tower in order to upload the model but turning it on (if it will fit on your plate) will help the quality of your prints. Pull Bar Assembly The Pull Bar requires 6 springs from the Bambu Store: 2 packs of 0.6x8x80mm Helical Compression Springs (Part BB019) . STEP 1: Print the Pull Bar Assembly parts. Gently sand off any rough edges on the round pull bars. STEP 2: Test thread the 3 pull bar posts together and thread into the bar, do not overtighten. Once satisfied, unthread all. Glue on the triangular support to the bar and re-thread two pull bars (2 and 3) onto the bar with a drop of superglue at each thread. However, do not connect or glue on pull bar 1. Refer to the pictures for alignment. STEP 3: Add 3 springs to each of the two spring rods and insert the spring rod (knob first) into each slot of the board until the knob end rests into the small hole. STEP 4: Insert the Pull Bar Assembly into the end of the board while lining up the springs and spring rods with the holes in the pull bar. STEP 5: Insert pull bar 1 into the small hole on the end of the board and thread onto the pull bar assembly. STEP 6: Line up the board cap with the spring rods and with a slight downward rotation, inset the board cap onto the board. NOTE: I recommend that you print two sets of the Pull Bar Assembly and store one extra set unassembled in the box as spare parts. This part will be under stress and may get damaged over time. description: Bring the spirit of the Pirate Hunter to your collection with this fully articulated 3D printable figure of Roronoa Zoro, the legendary swordsman of the Straw Hat Pirates. description: A warm and cozy country loaf, fresh from the bakery! 🥖 Clicky Bread – Country Bread is a cute fidget toy inspired by rustic handmade bread. The round and hearty country loaf rests inside a tiny proofing basket with a soft liner, creating a warm miniature bakery scene. Press the bread to activate the hidden MX-style mechanical keyboard switch and enjoy a satisfying click with springy feedback. It works as a relaxing little desk toy, a charming bakery-themed decoration, or a cute addition to your Clicky collection. This is the second model in the Anda Lab Clicky Bread series. Features Satisfying Clicky Action Press the country bread to enjoy a satisfying clicky fidget experience. The bread is the main interactive part of the model, while the proofing basket hides the internal switch and completes the bakery-themed design. Warm and Rustic Country Bread Design The bread features a round and hearty shape inspired by traditional European-style country loaves. Its natural scoring pattern and slightly irregular surface give it a warm handmade bakery feel while keeping the design cute and easy to recognize. Proofing Basket-Inspired Base The base is inspired by a traditional proofing basket , also known as a banneton . These baskets are commonly used to support and shape bread dough during its final rise. For this model, the proofing basket has been reimagined as a cute miniature display base for the finished bread. The distinctive circular ridges around the basket also give the model an artisan bakery look. Separate Proofing Basket Liner The proofing basket liner is a separate part and can be printed in a different color from the basket. It adds a soft visual layer between the bread and the basket while allowing you to create your own color combinations. Standard and Keychain Versions Included The download includes two versions: Standard Version – suitable as a desk fidget toy, decoration, or collectible. Keychain Version – includes a keychain attachment point so you can carry your Clicky Bread with you. Both versions use the same country bread and proofing basket liner parts. The main difference is the proofing basket base. Please note that keychain hardware is not included in the printable files and must be prepared separately. Separate Parts for Easy Color Printing The model is divided into the following printable parts: Country Bread Proofing Basket Liner Standard Proofing Basket Keychain Proofing Basket Each part can be printed in a different color, so no additional painting is required. A multi-color printer is not necessary. The parts can be printed separately and assembled afterward. Additional Parts Required One MX-style mechanical keyboard switch is required to create the clicky movement. For the keychain version, you will also need your own keychain ring or suitable keychain hardware. The mechanical switch and keychain hardware are not included with the printable model files. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the proofing basket. Place the proofing basket liner in the correct position. Connect the country bread to the switch. Press the bread several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. For the keychain version, attach your own keychain hardware to the connection point. Please refer to the assembly images on the model page for the correct part orientation and installation order. Welcome Back to Clicky Bread This is the second model in the Clicky Bread series, following the French Bread design. The first model features a long French bread served in a woven display basket, while this model introduces a round and rustic country loaf paired with a traditional proofing basket-inspired base. description: ⛴️ Deep Regrets and Even Deeper Regrets (expansion) insert / organizer This is an insert / organizer for the wicked fishing board game “Deep Regrets" (2025) and the expansion "Even Deeper Regrets" (2026) . It will also hold Kickstarter promo cards and the “Lamentable Tentacles” (2025) mini-expansion . 🪝Main features Supports sleeved cards No lid lift Highly decorative yet functional parts that double for storage and enhance gameplay at the same time (check photos!) No supports needed (one part has a smallish support prompted by Bambu Studio but it could be turned off safely) Some organizers out there put everything in the main box, but my design philosophy behind this model was to fit the game art and ideas. The inner boxes have beautiful art too, so I didn't want to neglect the expansion box either. Having a little more box estate space, I decided to have my insert function as in-game accessories too. The trays for the port cards resemble fish crates; the dink card holders are little anchovy / sardine cans! The regrets card holder can be opened and assembled to function as both draw tray and discard pile holder. The shoal trays feature portholes when you reach the bottom of a shoal deck, and so on… 🏗️ Print & assembly instructions I printed this with a Bambu H2S, but you should be able to print the insert with any smaller format printers without issue You will need to glue portholes to the shoal/river trays. I tried a multicolor approach on the same model but I noticed some quality issue since the bottom of the tray and the portholes are very thin. Printing the two pieces as separate models turned out much cleaner and better. I have used a brush-applied superglue to glue the pieces together and if done with just a little patience you won't be able to tell that the two were separate pieces. I highly recommend to print these portholes in some metal-like filament (I used brass basic PLA from Bambu) for added realism and a nice touch. Otherwise you could paint them in a metallic color. Likewise, if you print the dink boxes / sardine cans in PLA metal (I used Iridium Gold, but probably you can try some silk PLA with some aluminum finish) for added realism. For these parts specifically I also recommend using ironing, but it's optional (I have set mine to 60mm/s and 30% for the metal PLA, but your settings may differ). At the bottom of the trays (river, shoal, loch) you'll notice some smallish hole/marks: I have put those in case you decide to add rubber/foam feet to those models so they don't slide on the board. They're optional anyways. 🖌️ Optional weathering In the photos I published in the gallery you may notice that I decided to weather some of the models: this is entirely optional, but the components of this insert really lend themselves to this kind of treatment. If you want to try the same route, you can use some washes and other grime/mold effects as you like. The port crates feature some holes that can pass through a small rope (2-3mm thick: I have used 2.5) to create handles: these are non-functional and merely decorative but they're really a fun feature that's really easy to add. You will be able to store the trays normally even with these small appendages on. 📦 Packing instructions Check the gallery for visual references. Main box Place the 4 ship trays for the shoals and the river filled with cards as per game setup instructions (typically 13 per shoal slot and all, evenly distributed, for river slots): you'll shuffle these at every game together with the other cards that go in the other box but this separation is intended to optimize space. You'll notice that the river tray is taller than the sea shoal trays and that's intentional because there are a few more river cards. Place the player aid cards tray next to the ship trays and the loch tray on top of it, filled with the respective cards each. Next to the player aid + loch trays assembly you'll notice there's some space left: you should put the anchor and lifesaver tokens there. Place the regrets tray next: this pieces can be opened and then slid into each other half to create a draw/discard tray assembly when in play. Place the 5 player colored components trays and the 6th tray for the round marker and omen die next, in rows of 3 and 2 stacks. Place the 2 dink trays (the sardine cans) on top of each other in a corner, and the cloth bag that came with the game in the other. I tend to put the metal fish coin next to the bag as well. Finally, cover everything with the manuals, the ocean survey leaflets, and the three game boards (port, ocean and river/loch from the expansion). Expansion box Place the large tray (the largest piece) at the bottom: this will hold all the extra cards you won't be normally playing in a game but only draw from to create the shoal decks. Put all the cards that didn't fit the individual trays here. On top, place the 3 port crates for supplies, rods, reels. On the side, place the cloth baggie that came with the expansion containing clout tokens. description: Un tenero coniglietto puzzle 3D stile Montessori , pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il coniglietto si sostiene anche in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo che un simpatico personaggio decorativo. È ideale per bambini, attività creative, giochi educativi, camerette, scuole, asili o semplicemente per chi ama stampare piccoli oggetti colorati e divertenti. Ogni singolo pezzo può essere stampato con qualsiasi colore a scelta, permettendo di creare combinazioni personalizzate e rendere ogni coniglietto unico. Puoi realizzarlo tutto dello stesso colore, in versione bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto più allegro e creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il puzzle diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. description: Un tenero orsetto puzzle 3D stile Montessori , pensato per unire gioco, creatività e manualità. Il modello è composto da singoli pezzi che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, l’orsetto si sostiene anche in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo che un simpatico personaggio decorativo. È ideale per bambini, attività creative, giochi educativi, camerette, scuole, asili o semplicemente per chi ama stampare piccoli oggetti colorati e divertenti. Ogni singolo pezzo può essere stampato con qualsiasi colore a scelta, permettendo di creare combinazioni personalizzate e rendere ogni orsetto unico. Puoi realizzarlo tutto dello stesso colore, in versione bicolore oppure con più colori diversi per un effetto più allegro e creativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere: puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue preferenze, allo spazio disponibile o all’utilizzo che vuoi farne. Aumentando la scala, il puzzle diventa più grande e scenografico; riducendola, diventa più compatto e veloce da stampare. Anche il riempimento/infill può essere aumentato per rendere i pezzi più robusti e resistenti, soprattutto se il puzzle viene utilizzato spesso. Con un infill più basso, invece, si ottiene una stampa più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è pensato per una stampa rapida, indicativamente in circa 1 ora, a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA, anche con piatto texturizzato, per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e dall’aspetto più professionale. Prima di consegnare il puzzle a un bambino, verificare che la stampa sia resistente, liscia e priva di bordi taglienti o piccole parti fragili.

description: How to Play Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe is a strategic version of the classic game. Instead of playing one simple match, you are playing nine mini-games at the same time to win a giant mega-board. The Goal Win three mini-boards in a row (horizontally, vertically, or diagonally) on the large board. The Setup The main board is broken up into nine large squares. Each of those large squares contains its own small 3x3 tic-tac-toe grid. Player One takes the white pieces. Player Two takes the red pieces. The Core Rule (The Twist) The Opening Move: Player One places a small token in any square on any of the nine grids. Sending Your Opponent: The square you choose inside a small grid forces your opponent to play in that same relative section on the large board. Example: If you place your piece in the top-right corner of a small grid, your opponent is forced to make their next move somewhere inside the top-right mini-board. The Chain Reaction: Player Two then plays a piece in that designated mini-board. Whichever square they pick determines where Player One has to go next, and so on. Winning a Section When you get three small pieces in a row inside one grid, you win that specific board. Once a grid is won, clear it or flip it, and place one of the large X or O markers over the entire section to permanently claim it. What if a Grid is Full or Already Won? If a player's move sends you to a mini-board that has already been won and covered by a large marker, you get a free move. You can place your piece in any open slot on any other grid. The same free move rule applies if you are sent to a grid that is completely full and tied. Winning the Game The game ends the moment a player captures three mini-boards in a row to complete a 3-in-a-row line across the main mega-grid.

Spielvorbereitung Jeder Spieler erhält je nach Spieleranzahl seine Capybaras: 2 Spieler: je 20 Capybaras 4 Spieler: je 15 Capybaras 6 Spieler: je 10 Capybaras So wird gespielt Die Spieler würfeln nacheinander. 🎲 Eine 6/Capybara gewürfelt? Spielende Sobald ein Spieler alle seine Capybaras sicher in die Mitte gebracht hat, endet das Spiel und er gewinnt. Viel Glück! Ideal für den nächsten Ausflug oder Zuhause mit Freunden Instructions: The capybaras want to get to safety! Your task is to help them. Game Setup: Each player receives their capybaras depending on the number of players: 2 players: 20 capybaras each 4 players: 15 capybaras each 6 players: 10 capybaras each How to Play: Players take turns rolling the dice. 🎲 Rolled a 6/Capybara? Great! The 6 means one capybara is safe. Place one of your capybaras directly in the center. It stays there until the end of the game. 🎲 Rolled a 1 to 5? Place one of your capybaras on the game board with the number rolled. Is the playing field already full? Then things get exciting! Instead of discarding a capybara, you must collect all the capybaras from this playing field. Sometimes luck has a plan of its own! End of Game As soon as a player has safely brought all their capybaras to the center, the game ends and they win. Good luck! Don't be discouraged if you get capybaras back just before reaching the finish line. These unexpected twists and turns are what make every round exciting – right up to the very last throw!

Make a solid pen vanish before their eyes! It’s a 3D-printed take on a classic optical illusion, engineered with a mechanical twist. I tested this on my family, and it completely baffled the kids! The Illusion: You show your audience a completely solid, standard ballpoint pen and a plastic case. You slide the pen horizontally into the case. But when you snap open the front door... the middle of the pen is completely gone! All the audience sees is an empty chamber with a stretched spring across it. You can even slide the ends of the pen back and forth to prove it's still moving. Close the door, pull the pen out, and it is 100% intact. No magnets, no electronics—just clever mechanical geometry and a little bit of misdirection!

32-Piece Spherical Sliding Fidget This is my most advanced fidget design so far: a 32-piece spherical sliding fidget built around a twisting internal guide system. Each piece is repeated evenly around the sphere and is designed to slide along the curved shape while staying captured inside the model. A lot of the work went into balancing three things at once: smooth movement, strong enough walls, and a clean outside shape that still looks like a finished sphere. Design Story This project started as a personal challenge. After seeing the idea of spherical sliding fidgets, I wanted to see if I could design my own version from scratch and push the concept further. My first version used 20 pieces, but after feedback asking for more slices, I took it as a challenge to keep improving the design. I tested higher piece counts, including a 35-piece version, but it did not hold onto the rail as well as I wanted. That led me to rethink the spacing, clearances, and piece count. The 32-piece version became the best balance between size, movement, and printability. A lot of the work went into making the pieces slide smoothly while staying captured inside the sphere, without making the outside look messy. The goal was not just to make something that moves, but to make the movement feel intentional. The internal geometry does most of the work while staying mostly hidden from the outside. Design Features 32 individual sliding sections Spherical twist-style motion Hidden internal guide/catcher geometry Designed with FDM printing in mind Improved clearances to reduce fusing Smooth curved outside shape No supports required Print-in-place style assembly Printing Notes This model has tight moving clearances, so a well-calibrated printer is recommended. Make sure your first layer is not over-squished, because too much elephant foot can affect the moving gaps. Recommended settings: 0.16 mm layer height for a safer first print 0.12 mm layer height for a cleaner showcase print Supports off Brim off Arachne wall generator recommended PLA or PLA+ recommended Check Preview before printing to make sure the moving gaps are not being fused This model represents a lot of trial, failure, redesign, and testing. It is the smoothest and most complete version of this fidget concept I have made so far.

description: The second iteration of the AMS Speeder is here ! Designed for the P2 and X2 series, and still compatible with the AMS, AMS 2 Pro, and the AMS Flipper by Jakob_K_Design , this advanced mod aims to reduce filament loading times by shortening the PTFE tubes behind the printer, while also providing neat and clean cable management. Features Faster Filament Changes: Used with shorter PTFE tubes, this holder cuts filament swap time by about 24 seconds, making your 3D printing process quicker and smoother. Strong and Reliable: Although PTFE wear is slightly higher than usual, the better performance makes filament handling more efficient. Printing and preparation You can use the provided 3MF, no supports required. For both main parts, I recommend using at least PETG to avoid deformation due to the chamber/AMS 2 Pro heat, and for the optional TPU seal, I recommend using TPU 95 HF. As for the assembly, you will need to cut PTFE tubes. For that, carefully use a sharp cutter and make sure to cut it straight. The PTFE tube lengths I recommend are : For X2D : ~118mm for the AMS output, 240mm for the buffer output, 400mm for the external spool holder output and 380mm for the auxiliary extruder input. For P2S : ~118mm for the AMS output and 240mm for the buffer output. For this mod to work, you will need an extension cable for the internal cable of the buffer . Don't worry, you will not have to open the back panel of the printer. You can order it here on Aliexpress : Buffer internal cable extension for AMS Speeder 2 , thanks to the WEPRO team for their help ! Please note that this cable was made specifically for this mod, so it will work without any issues as long as it's installed properly. Installation 1 - Turn off and unplug the printer. 2 - Unscrew and unplug the AMS Buffer. For this step, don't hesitate to refer to the official Bambu Lab Wiki : For P2S : Filament Buffer Replacement Guide for the P2S | Bambu Lab Wiki For X2D : Filament buffer Replacement Guide for the X2D | Bambu Lab Wiki 3 - Route the male side of the extension cable in the AMS Speeder and plug it into the buffer Make sure that the connector makes a “click” sound when you connect it ! 4 - Screw the buffer into place on the AMS Speeder 5 - Put the AMS Speeder in position on the AMS and route the AMS and External Exhaust Fan cables in the notches 6 - Install the cover and plug the female side of the extension cable in the printer cable Put the optional TPU Seal in the cover, and install the cover just as if it was the buffer, be careful to let the connector pass through ! Then use regular Bambu M3 machine screws to fix it in place. Connect the buffer cable and the external exhaust one, and manage the cables using the cover slots, make sure that the buffer connector makes a “click” sound when you connect it ! 7 - Cut and install the PTFE tubes Here are the ideal lengths for the tubes, feel free to experiment and make sure to cut them straight to avoid problems. 8 - Adjust Bambu Studio Settings To see faster print times, update the Filament Load/Unload durations in the slicer (Bambu Studio → “Prepare” tab → Printer Settings → “Basic Information” tab → Filament Load/Unload Time). You can adjust the load and unload times as needed, I personally use 8 seconds for each, which I’ve found to be optimal. Your AMS Speeder 2 is now ready to reduce your print times !

description: A refined take on the filament clip. True flexi filament clip. Dual flex arms, a comfortable height and chamfered edges provide smooth handling and a secure hold. Fits most standard filament spools, including Bambu Lab, SUNLU and common cardboard spools. How it works The internal filament path follows a serpentine S shaped geometry. This increases the contact length and creates a secure friction fit without additional locking features. The square opening is intentionally designed for printability and a good-looking mirror symmetry. Insert the filament into the clip, squeeze the sides and snap it between the spool flanges. The filament is securely held by friction, making accidental tangles virtually impossible. Unlike clips attached to the spool rim, the spool remains free to rotate during filament drying. Keeping the filament close to the spool core also minimizes bending stress, helping to prevent brittle filament from breaking even after long term storage. Compatibility Standard Clip (fits 56 mm to 65 mm inner spool width) Tested with: ACCCREATE, Anycubic, Bambu Lab, Bambu Lab Clear, Bambu Lab HT, Bambu Lab HT Cardboard, ELEGOO, Filamentwerk, GratKit Cardboard, Polymaker Cardboard, Prusament, SUNLU V1, SUNLU V2 and SUNLU V3. Small Clip (fits 48 mm to 56 mm inner spool width) Tested with: ERYONE Cardboard, eSUN Cardboard, Flashforge, GEEETECH, GEEETECH old, GIANTARM, JAYO Cardboard, MATERIAL4PRINT, SUNLU Cardboard Material Since the clip relies on elastic deformation, PLA is not recommended. While it does work, PETG, ABS, ASA, PC and unfilled PA provide significantly better flexibility and durability. If you want to leave the clip on the spool during filament drying, make sure the selected material can withstand the required drying temperature. TPU Special Edition Multi material printing with PETG and TPU for AMS works well on virtually any printer. I recommend getting a dedicated 0.4 mm nozzle for TPU and keeping it exclusively for flexible materials. Avoid using the same nozzle for PLA whenever possible, as PLA residues are one of the most common causes of TPU related clogs. I even scratched a small "T" into my TPU nozzle so I never mix it up. A1mini tested successfully: PETG Basic + TPU for AMS on A1mini. If the A1mini can do it reliably, almost any modern printer should. Use Textured PEI build plate with Glue Stick or suffer. Multi material printing with ASA and TPU for AMS (or TPU 90A) is intended for advanced users. ASA and TPU require very different nozzle temperatures and TPU is also sensitive to excessive chamber temperatures. Before printing, make sure to read the Bambu Wiki recommendations for this material combination. In my testing, a chamber temperature of 30 °C worked reliably. Running an enclosed chamber at typical ASA temperatures can soften the TPU before it reaches the nozzle, significantly increasing the risk of extrusion problems or nozzle clogs. X2D tested successfully: ASA (secondary nozzle) with TPU 90 a (primary nozzle) on my X2D. Chamber temperature set to 30 °C! Both spools from external spool holder. Use Textured PEI build plate with Glue Stick H2C tested successfully: ASA (primary nozzle) with TPU 90 a (secondary nozzle) on my H2C. Chamber temperature set to 30 °C! TPU 90a from external spool holder. Use Textured PEI build plate with Glue Stick History 2026/07/08 - v2 initial release of TPU special 2026/07/08 - v2 improved teeth, increased flex gap length 2026/07/07 - v1 initial release About Inspired by @LemonArts Flex Filament Clip concept, this model was completely redesigned from scratch with a focus on improved usability, flexibility and compatibility.

model_name: Noodle Nexus 2: Modular AMS Stacker Drawer
description: Introduction Another one? Yes. Clear up some desk space by stacking your AMS's! This version uses 45mm steel slides to slide out the lower AMS, making a super compact stacker. This is compatible with the original AMS and the AMS 2 Pro. The top AMS is positioned forward to ensure that the lid can open fully. Even so, with 350mm slide travel, the AMS lid will open enough to stay open without falling closed. The dimensions are: Height including an AMS 2 Pro on top: 475 mm Width: 443 mm Depth excluding handle and optional counterweight basket: 355 mm Handle adds 32mm of depth Counterweight basket adds 45mm of depth If this isn't exactly for you, check out this collection for alternatives. Modules Feet extensions to put this on top of your H-series printer 3rd/4th AMS Extension (link coming very soon!) Upcoming: AMS HT adapter Upcoming: Various Storage attachments, perhaps a tool drawer? Difficulty This project is designed for beginners . It is easy because: All parts print with minimal supports and all overhangs are easy to print. There is minimal post-processing required. There is only one type (and length!) of fastener needed with no heat-set inserts, no glue and no other specialty fasteners. You don't need "advanced" materials such as ABS. The challenging aspects are: Large parts, even PLA and PETG parts, can warp and your build plates need to be clean. You may even consider using some glue if you have had issues with your particular material and plate. You need to be able to print TPU, and to do this cleanly, you will need a filament dryer. Filament I recommend: PETG for the frame PETG or PLA for the drawer (if you plan on putting this on top of a printer though, do not use PLA) TPU 90A or similar for the feet If you use ABS or ASA, you must consider shrinkage compensation as the parts are large and the overall dimension can be affected by 2-3mm. Please feel free to post your print profile. Add lots of pictures and a detailed description please! It will help other people decide which one to use. Hardware for Assembly Only one type and length of screw is needed: BT3x14 BHCS Self Tapping Screw (AA223). This is a 3mm diameter, 14mm long screw designed for plastic with coarse deep threads that cut into and grip well onto holes in plastic. They are not expensive extremely easy to use as you don't need to embed heat set inserts or seat little M3 nuts. They also make the printed parts simpler and use far less material than using printed fasteners or bowtie joints. Alternatives: If you have 12mm screws or the socket head style of BT3 screws, they will be perfectly fine too. If Bambu doesn't ship to your country, the key words to search are “3mm self-tapping screw hex socket”. Try to get some without a pointy tip as they have a slightly longer usable thread length and a head height of 2mm or less. I found some products on AliExpress ( Listing 1 , Listing 2 , Listing 3 ) which look promising, but I have not tried them. Do NOT use countersunk screws as most holes in the design are parallel to the print bed plane and the screws can split your layers if you're not careful with tightening. You will need: 43 for the frame assembly 10 for the drawer assembly 16 to attach the steel slides to the frame and drawer assemblies 8 to attach the AMS's Optional: 4 to attach the counterweight basket 81 screws total (if I counted correctly…). If you ever wanted an excuse to buy an electric pencil screwdriver, here it is! In the bill of materials, I have put 5 packets of 20 screws but I suggest ordering extra if you are interested in making the future modules. You will also need 350mm or 14-inch nominal length, 45mm nominal width (can be a little wider as there is nothing below the slides), 12.7mm thick full extension slides. Here in Germany, I got Stahlia branded slides direct from their website , also available on Amazon.de . You do not need to get exactly the same one. I took specs from several different brands and accommodated for them all in the design and you just need 3-4 holes that line up. Worst case, you might need to make some new holes but I think that's unlikely as slide manufacturers just copy each other. IMPORTANT : If you are using soft-close slides, check that they are truly full extension and extend 400mm. Many 3-section slides that are labelled “full extension” are not really full extension, particularly some of the soft-close ones. Slide designers, when taking their regular slide and making a soft-close version, need to decide whether to reduce the load rating of their slide or reduce the extension to try to fit the extra mechanisms into the design. Some brands have lowered weight ratings (say, 35kg down from 45kg), some reduce their travel. Parts for Installation You will need a longer PTFE tube than typically supplied with printers (or a coupler to connect two shorter ones) as the AMS travels forward and back. The length needed depends on your particular setup. If the tube is brand new and tightly-wound for shipping, they will need to be relaxed to form gentle curves. Don't get the "star shaped" tubes, that's a gimmick. If you use a coupler, note that there is an entry side (tapered inlet) and an exit side (not tapered). You may also need longer 6-pin AMS connectors depending on your printer and AMS arrangement. Print Settings General Tips Flow rate calibration is highly recommended for every spool you use! Many clearances in the design are 0.1mm. For proper fit, the parts should not be under or over-extruded. Dry your filament (even PLA) to minimise risks with dimensional accuracy. Aux fan OFF if you've had issues with part warping. Don't worry, all of the overhangs are super easy. Specific Settings These are all set in the print profile. However, if you download it on PC and change the printer, some of these may get overwritten so I will list them here. These are the settings I use and are quite conservative and a little slow for a clean print with sharp corners, it's a balance between Bambu's “High Quality” and “Standard" profiles. Feel free to deviate as you see fit. Speeds Outer wall: 70 mm/s Inner wall: 150 mm/s Top Surface: 120 mm/s Everything else: default for your favourite profile Accelerations Normal printing: 4000 mm/s² Outer wall: 2000 mm/s² Inner wall: 0 (same as Normal) Top surface: 2000 mm/s² Sparse infill: 8000 mm/s² Everything else: default for your favourite profile Strength Parts are designed for a 0.4mm nozzle printing 0.2mm layer heights. Wall loops Top/bottom shell layers Infill Frame Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern Slider Parts 3 7/5 10-15%, your choice of pattern TPU feet 6 5/3 Your choice All other parts 2 5/3 10-15%, your choice of pattern Bonus tip If you want the perfect 🧑🍳👌🏼fit between parts, make sure your beds are trammed! They're not always trammed out-of-factory; 3 of the printers I got in 2026 were not trammed. Manual Bed Leveling / Manual Bed Tramming | Bambu Lab Wiki P2S & X2D Heatbed Manual Bed Leveling | Bambu Lab Wiki Assembly and Installation As all screws are the same, this is quite straight forward. Just one thing to note: screws can get hot while tightening; tighten them most of the way and give them a minute before final tightening. Frame Assembly Assemble each half first. Use the screws to attach the 5 pieces of one side together. Insert the TPU feet - they are press-fit and should stay-in firmly without glue. Remove the inner part of the slide and attach to the frame using at least 3 screws. When tightening, push the slides up to the flat parts on the frame - this ensures that the left and right slides are parallel and level. Repeat for the other side and put the two halves together with more screws. Attach the top AMS with 4 screws. This will stiffen up the frame assembly considerably. For some versions of the original AMS, there are some small pieces of plastic that need to be trimmed. This is not necessary for the AMS 2 Pro and some original AMS variants. Drawer Assembly Assemble the drawer assembly with more screws. Attach the inner slides using at least 3 screws on each side. When tightening, try to get the two inner slides parallel. You can look at the unused holes to determine the positioning. If the holes are too big, you can use some washers (mine is OK without, this is just for illustration). Now slide this into the frame. Attach the lower AMS Put some filament inside the top AMS to provide some counterweight. Pull out the drawer and place the second AMS. Use 4 more screws to secure it in-place. And finally, post a picture here! Counterweight Options As you can guess, the whole assembly can tip forward when the drawer is opened fully. I have 3 options to reduce this risk. You can use one or more of the methods at the same time. Option 1 - Counterweight Basket Attach the counterweight basket using 4 screws (same screws as above!). The file for this is in a separate print profile, on this page. Fill an empty filament box with heavy stuff - try to get at least 2kg in there (a bag of sand, depleted uranium, a brick, whatever you have around the house). Put the box into the basket. You can make the box smaller too. Option 2 - Feet extensions These extensions extend the front by 95mm - if you have the table space these work great. Option 3 - Add another AMS Coming soon™! Support If you make one, please share a pic on social media! Facebook, Reddit, Twitter, whatever! It really helps me out. And of course: Changelog 25/06/2026 Original release

description: Bambu Lab P2S / X2D Chamber Exhaust Plenum – Sealed Poop Chute Sistema di convogliamento e scarico fumi progettato specificamente per integrarsi con la Chamber Exhaust Fan delle stampanti Bambu Lab P2S e X2D . Questo progetto non è un semplice contenitore per gli scarti (poop chute), ma un plenum di aspirazione sigillato che unifica lo scarico del vano stampa e lo scivolo dei rifiuti in un unico percorso d'aria controllato. Il vantaggio principale è la possibilità di utilizzare il sistema con i filtri e sistemi di filtraggio già disponibili su MakerWorld: non è necessario sostituire o riprogettare il proprio sistema di filtraggio . Il plenum si installa tra la stampante e la ventola di scarico, convogliando i fumi provenienti da entrambe le zone verso il filtro esistente. A differenza dei classici sistemi aperti, che lasciano disperdere odori, microplastiche e fumi dal retro della stampante, questa camera sigillata sfrutta la pressione negativa generata dalla ventola per aspirare anche l'aria proveniente dal poop chute, riducendo le dispersioni nell'ambiente domestico. Caratteristiche principali: 🌬️ Flusso d'aria canalizzato e forzato Il contenitore dei rifiuti e il plenum comunicano tramite una feritoia interna progettata per creare un percorso d'aria controllato. La Chamber Exhaust Fan genera una depressione all'interno del sistema, richiamando i fumi dello scivolo prima che possano disperdersi all'esterno. 🔒 Sistema completamente sigillato Il progetto utilizza un set completo di guarnizioni in TPU 95A dedicate, progettate per garantire una tenuta elevata e minimizzare eventuali perdite d'aria. ⚙️ Incastri meccanici di precisione Il collegamento alla stampante utilizza un sistema a coda di rondine ( Dovetail_Chute_Adapter ) progettato per garantire stabilità e un accoppiamento preciso. 🧩 Compatibilità con sistemi di filtraggio esistenti Il plenum è pensato come un elemento di integrazione: permette di sfruttare i sistemi di filtraggio già presenti per la Chamber Exhaust Fan senza doverli modificare. 🎨 Design funzionale Il cassetto inferiore rimane removibile per lo svuotamento dei rifiuti. Il logo Bambu Lab è riprodotto in bassorilievo e il componente è ottimizzato per essere stampato in un unico pezzo senza supporti. Nota sul progetto L'obiettivo non era creare l'ennesimo poop chute, ma migliorare la gestione del flusso d'aria della stampante utilizzando un componente già presente: la Chamber Exhaust Fan. Il risultato è un sistema più ordinato, più pulito e integrabile con le soluzioni di filtraggio esistenti. 🛒 Componenti Necessari (BOM) Per completare il montaggio avrai bisogno di: Viti per il Plenum (Precamera): Servono 6 viti testa cilindrica con esagono incassato. Si possono utilizzare i modelli BT2x5 (o M2x5) oppure BT2x6 (o M2x6) . Viti per l'Adattatore Dovetail: Servono 2 viti BT3x8 . Consiglio pratico: io ho utilizzato direttamente quelle del braccio dove si monta il supporto della bobina esterna della stampante. Filamento Flessibile: Un piccolo quantitativo di TPU 95A per la stampa del set di guarnizioni ermetiche. 🔧 Istruzioni di Montaggio (Passo-Passo) 1) Fissaggio del Plenum: avvita i denti alla precamera, monta la guarnizione. Posiziona il Plenum (collettore d'aria) sul retro della stampante. 2) Installazione dell'Adattatore: Inserisci il Dovetail_Chute_Adapter bloccandolo in posizione con le 2 viti BT3x8 (recuperabili dal supporto bobina). Inserisci la guarnizione allungata sul Plenum, e anche sull' Adattatore. 3) Installazione Chamber Exhaust Fan : a questo punto si può già montare la ventola di estrazione della camera: 4) Montaggio dello Scivolo Superiore: Fai scorrere il Waste_Container_up lungo le guide a coda di rondine fino a farlo agganciare con il Plenum. Sono presenti due blocchi a scatto sopra e sotto la feritoia interna. Quando fai scorrere il Waste_Container_up nel Plenum, si incastreranno saldamente in posizione con un 'click' udibile, garantendo una connessione perfettamente sigillata e bloccata. (Consiglio pratico: aggancia prima quello inferiore, con le dita da sotto e poi quello superiore) 5) Inserimento del Cassetto Scarti: inserisci la guarnizione in TPU sul cassetto porta scarti. Successivamente, aggancia il cassetto inferiore con il logo ( Waste_Container_down ) posizionandolo sotto lo scivolo. Nota: le guarnizioni dell'adattare a coda di rondine e del cassetto degli scarti sono identiche. 6) Sistema Completo: Ora il tuo sistema è sigillato e pronto a stampare tutti i materiali senza l'odore di plastica, senza microplastiche e composti organici volatili (VOC). Se il montaggio è avvenuto correttamente il sistema dovrebbe avere questi giochi: 💡 Il Consiglio del Maker: Per un accoppiamento fluido e senza sforzo, si consiglia di applicare una piccola goccia di olio per macchina da cucire sulle slitte a coda di rondine, prima di fare scorrere i componenti in posizione. Se volete potete accoppiarlo al mio Filtro HEPA + Carboni Attivi Bambu Lab P2S : 📝 Nota sulla Compatibilità X2D La mod è stata verificata con successo anche sulla Bambu Lab X2D . Un ringraziamento speciale a @strikerwa per aver testato la compatibilità e per aver fornito un feedback fondamentale, contribuendo alla verifica del corretto adattamento del progetto alla piattaforma X2D. ⚠️ NOTA TECNICA IMPORTANTE SULLA GRIGLIA DELL'ELETTRONICA: Mi è stato chiesto più volte di inglobare nel Plenum anche la griglia laterale destra dell'elettronica (o le griglie, nel caso della X2D). Quella griglia NON è stata collegata intenzionalmente al collettore. Quelle prese d'aria servono esclusivamente per il raffreddamento della scheda madre (un sistema passivo per la P2S e un sistema attivo per la X2D, dove la ventola aspira aria fresca dall'esterno per raffreddare i componenti). ATTENZIONE: Sigillare questa griglia o convogliarla nel circuito di estrazione dei fumi caldi può alterare gravemente il raffreddamento dell'elettronica, con il rischio di surriscaldare o danneggiare la scheda madre. Lasciatela libera di respirare aria fresca!

description: Hello, I'm Lee, and I'd like to share my design for a side-mounted enclosed Dry Box for the Centauri Carbon 2. I have really enjoyed my new CC2, but I have always felt that it was lacking an enclosed MFS. I felt like all my filament was getting dusty and absorbing moisture. So, I visited all the maker websites looking for a solution, but I found that most designs were somewhat lacking or cumbersome to use. After coming up short in my search, I decided to make one myself. This design is mostly airtight and can maintain humidity levels at least 15% to 20% lower than the surrounding environment. It utilizes the existing retracting spools and mounting points, and I also tried to preserve the printer's unique design and aesthetic. It took a lot of effort and time, but I am quite proud of the outcome. I designed every piece to print without supports and tried to make assembly as easy as possible. Almost everything screws together, and glue is used only as a sealant, not for structural strength. I have included a customizable plate to hold a hygrometer, and I designed the enclosure to mount to the side of the printer so it does not need to be disassembled for routine maintenance or when the printer needs to be moved. With all that being said, I've decided to share this design for free, and I hope you all love it as much as I do. Update: I added a version for the Centauri Carbon 1. I don't own one of these printers so please verify mounting locations before printing. I found a very accurate model of it online so it should be good. I added new instructions but the only difference between the 2 is the mounting locations of the main body. Features All parts of this model are designed to print without supports and were printed in PLA. All pieces screw together, and glue is used only for sealing purposes, not structural support. The box mounts to the side of the CC2 using the existing spool retraction mounting holes. It is designed with two large desiccant boxes to help keep filament clean and dry. Many of the parts require a multi-filament system to print the graphical designs, but they can also be printed without one. Assembly instructions are attached. model_name: X2D Dual AMS 2 Pro Glass Riser
description: No supports, no glue, no screws, only about 1.1kg of filament, and 2 days of print time! I wanted something simple that raised the glass and got my 2 AMS 2 Pro units off of my desk. This is what I came up with… This is by far the largest model I have created to date. I recently purchased the X2D and wanted a place to mount my 2 AMS 2 Pro units. I also was very annoyed by the sound the PTFE tubes made hitting the glass all the time. This riser raises the glass by 18mm which, for me, has provided more than enough clearance to solve the anoying clicking sound and prevent wear on my tubes. My final product ended up with a bit more sag in the middle than I was hoping for, but I am very happy with its strength. I am not using any glue or fasteners. The way this thing is designed, it will not dissassemble itself unless something was to fail. I could probably get some sag out if I glued the parts together, but I want to be able to take it apart and make improvements in the future without having to repint the whole thing! Besides, I don't think these AMS units are going anywhere. There is a depression for the feet to prevent them from walking off the edge. I have run about 50 hours of prints since I put this thing up and it is holding up well so far. During design, I printed some parts of an earlier version on my A1 and the parts fit together VERY tightly. Without changing the tolerances of the model, my final version was printed 100% on the X2D. These final parts fit together with a bit more wiggle room. While this can probably be partially (or majorially) attributed to the difference between a bed slinger and a core xy machine, I think this is also a good example of the differences you might experience from printer to printer. I am happy knowing that even with two different machines, I am able to put the thing together successfully. The sides are SKADIS boards because I was lacking creativity and thought this was a decent solution for accessories storage. The boards are at 45 degrees so you will have to pick and choose what you use accordingly, but this is the 3D printing community after all - if what you want doesn't exist just create it! There is a little pin that gets inserted in the front corner brackets to hold the SKADIS boards in place when taking things on and off of it. The parts are numbered to assist with assembly and I would be happy to provide instructions for assembly if needed, but it is honestly very self explanitory. The parts only go together one way. However, I will say the last things to go on are the supports that go front to back (blue in my printed version). I assembled the glass riser first, put in the TPU gaskets, built the front rail, then the back rail, connected them with the SKADIS boards, connected them with the front to back supports, then slid the whole thing down onto the sides of the glass riser. If you plan to use glue, I would certainly recommend making sure you understand how everything goes together first!

description: This is a filament guide to help retain tension on the filament when using external spools and spools over the print head. This guide prevents the filament drifting outside the spool and causing tangles and failures. The model has eyelets in 3 sizes (26,36 and 46mm) and should fit a variety of spool holders / cross beams. There are pips (dentents) on the cross beam to secure the width and optional pins are provide to provide extra security. Suggest printing in PETG for strength but not required. no bearings or external parts. Instructions: Print two arms with the appropriate eyelet size slide onto your spool rail / holder with arms on either side of the spool. Insert the cross bar in the sockets. Pips (detentes) should be spool facing so the smooth taurus shape receives the filament. Secure with pins if necessary. Feed filament through the hole. The pips are a bit oversized to account for shrinkage / warpage / material variation. They may need slight filing to fit perfectly (don't over file). Hopefully you will have care free TPU printing. description: Here is an updated model of my Vacuum Bag Valve Tool . It has a tapered stronger neck, more durable than the previous model. Same functionality, just better robustness. I got a batch of vacuum bags that I was really struggling to get an initial vacuum started. I discover if I gently inserted the tip of my forceps in the valve I could break the initial seal and get my vacuum pump working. It is tricky to do and not damage the valve. So I created this tool that is much gentler and easy to use. From the inside of the new vacuum bag gently insert the tip of the tool flatly in the opening of the valve, plate side up and debossed text down. Il Deflettore Scarti “CACCHE” è un accessorio progettato per la stampante 3D A2L con lo scopo di intercettare, guidare e raccogliere automaticamente i residui generati durante le operazioni di pulizia dell'ugello, cambio filamento e procedure di spurgo. Tali scarti, comunemente denominati "cacche", vengono normalmente espulsi dalla testina di stampa e possono accumularsi sul piano di lavoro o all'interno della macchina, causando problemi di pulizia, possibili interferenze con le stampe successive e perdita di materiale. Il sistema è costituito da una struttura di supporto fissata al montante laterale della stampante e da un meccanismo deflettore mobile che si posiziona automaticamente nell'area di espulsione degli scarti. Durante le operazioni di purge, il deflettore intercetta il materiale estruso e lo convoglia verso una zona dedicata di raccolta, evitando che i residui ricadano casualmente all'interno della macchina.
