description: This is a lower profile Chamber Exhaust Fan than the official Bambu “ P2S Chamber Exhaust Fan Kit ”. It uses the same $20 Bambu P2S chamber exhaust fan kit parts . Though design may appear similar to the Original Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan in some ways, it is an entirely different, scratch built design. This design is not in any way associated with Bambu, so use this design at your own risk. No warranties are given. This project was a collaboration with MadMopar (over on MakerWorld). MadMopar had the original idea for a lower profile exhaust duct for the P2S, ran multiple prototypes, provided suggestions and feedback to refine the design, and also provided all the images of the printed design. So a big thanks goes out to MadMopar ! PLEASE NOTE: This profile does not include the poop chute shown in the pics (and the baseplate included here is not compatible with that poop chute design). This model only includes a basic (flat) plate for the poop chute. If you want to use Mc2.project3D's “ Inspectable Waste Chute – Series P / X / H2 ” which is shown in the pics , you will be able to find a remixed backplate and slide which are compatible with that designat the link below (due to the MakerWorld Exclusive License): https://makerworld.com/en/models/2920654-baseplate-only-for-the-inspectable-waste-chute#profileId-3267976 Between MadMopar and myself, many hours have been spent polishing the design, testing and improving it. I feel it is completed, and the one of these ducts in operation currently (with the 2" duct) has been performing well. But if you make or use this design and see anything that could be improved, please provide feedback (positive or negative). I cannot guarantee that the changes will be made, but I will check the comments. I don't own the P2S myself, so if you have a problem, providing pics and accurate measurements would be very helpful. Functionally, this design differs from the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust Fan design in the following key ways: This design has a lower overall profile, which can help in setups with limited room behind the printer. This design uses magnets to hold the duct on, instead of the latches on the stock Bambu design. It was thought that the magnetic attachment would make the duct easier to install or remove when there is limited space behind the printer. This design shifts the whole Exhaust Fan to the left a few mm, which allows for more poop chute options. This does however move the poop chute mount a bit away from the printer, which could be a problem with some poop chute designs (YMMV). This design has an optional TPU gasket, or can be used with 1/16" (1.58mm) thick foam tape, between the backplate and printer, to reduce air leakage. This design does not have room for a HEPA filter , which the official Bambu Chamber Exhaust design does allow for. This design is strictly for venting the chamber either outside or to a separate air cleaner. This design is a bit more complex and expensive to build, since it uses 16x 10x3mm cylinder magnets to hold the duct on, and requires more filament. Currently there are only ducts for a 2" or 2.5" (inside diameter) hose, with options for ducts that angle out at 45°, 90° and straight out from the printer. The 2.5" ducts are untested , and you can find them at the following link: https://www.printables.com/model/1754424-25-ducts-for-bambu-p2s-and-p1-exhaust-see-descript I may add additional ducts in the future, but I plan to upload the STEP models for this design to help with remixing the design. I may upload this in the future to MakerWorld, so I kindly ask that you please do not upload this design to MakerWorld. Thanks for understanding. To build this, the following hardware is needed (in addition to the Bambu P2S Exhaust Fan Kit): 2x M3x20 FHCS (Flat Head Cap Screws) 2x M3x14 (upto 20mm long) FHCS 4x M5x10 Self-Tapping Case Fan Screws 16x 10x3mm Cylinder Magnets 1/16" foam tape (optional) and not needed if using the TPU Gasket Superglue Printing: There are two main profiles available for the main parts. One of the main profiles is set up for ABS and uses brims and mouse ears to help with bed adhesion. The other main profile is set up with PETG, and does not use brims. Both profiles use a textured build plate, however both also specify an Engineering Plate for the optional TPU gasket. The Engineering Plate for TPU is just a suggestion, but I recommend using a smoother plate with glue as a release agent, since TPU tends to aggressively stick to the textured plates. There are additional profiles for the 2" ducts. Any future duct sizes will also have a separate profile. The image below shows the layout of the profile. The only options, aside from the TPU gasket, are the three L-Clip choices. The L-Clips mount into the baseplate, and help to hold the vent fan to the back of the printer, along with 2 screws around the poop chute. The L-Clips are available in different lengths, depending on how the vent fan is configured. There are different L-Clip sizes for using 1/16" foam tape, the optional TPU gasket, or no tape and no TPU gasket (which will probably allow more leakage of air). These options are described below the image: Referring to the above image, the L-Clip options are: A. L-Clips used with 1/16" foam tape (plate 04) B. L-Clips used without the foam tape or TPU gasket (plate 05) C. L-Clips used with the TPU gasket on plate 06 (plate 04) The 3mf profiles included were set up using Bambu Studio v2.7.1.57 and include the following: 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_PETG_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile without brims, for PETG) 92mm_Fan_Cover_v95_ABS_w_BRIMS_no_Ducts.3mf (base profile with brims, for ABS) v6Z_2in_Ducts_only.3mf (45°, 90°, dual, and straight through 2" ducts) V1F_2-5in_Ducts.3mf (UNTESTED 45°, 90°, and straight through 2" ducts) The individual STEP models will be added later, when the license is changed to allow for remixing. Assembly: First decide if you plan to use the optional TPU cover, or 1/16" foam tape before gathering the parts. This will determine which type of L-hook is used, and which plates need to be printed. See the above information under “Printing” to decide which size L-Clips you need to use. Start by installing the L-Clips into the baseplate. These will need a bit of glue to hold them in place. Next, remove the two screws around the poop chute. These will be re-installed in the following steps, through the baseplate. If the TPU cover (shown in orange) is going to be used, install it on the baseplate: Install the baseplate onto the back of the printer. First start the right side L-Clip hooks in the corresponding holes on the printer metal backplate, then start the left side hooks. When both are in place and the baseplate will sit flush to the printer, slide the baseplate leftward until it stops. At this point the holes on the plate should align with the holes for the screws around the poop chute which were removed in step 3. These two screws can now be re-installed through the baseplate to help secure it to the printer. Install 8 of the 10x3 cylinder magnets into the cover as shown. Pay special attention to the polarity of these magnets, and how they are installed, so they will attract the magnets which will be installed in the duct. It can help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. I recommend installing the magnets so the poles are all pointed in the same direction, which will make things easier later. A drop of superglue will help secure them. Install the fan into the cover of the printer, using the M5x10 self-tapping fan screws. Make sure the fan power cable wraps either around the top or bottom side of the fan, and will not become pinched. Connect the fan cable to the board from the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit. Use the 3 screws included with the P2S Exhaust Fan Kit to install the board into the cover. You can use the small wire management slot (circled in green) to manage the extra wire. Double check that the wiring is connected and none of the fan wires are pinched (or will get pinched during the next assembly steps). Install the cover (with the fan and board previously installed) onto the baseplate using the M3 flat head screws: Install 8 of the 10x3mm cylinder magnets into the fan duct. Pay special attention to the polarity of the magnets here, since they should all be set up to attract the magnets already installed in the fan cover. It may help to set the magnets onto the fan cover magnets, prior to installing, so you can verify they will attract and not repel. If your magnets are not all set up as north or south on the fan cover and duct, be sure to orient the duct in the final position before installing magnets in it, otherwise it may attract on some and repell on others. It can also help to mark one pole of the magnets with a sharpie before starting, so there is a visual indicator of their polarity. A drop of superglue may help them stay. Install the duct onto the fan cover. Please provide feedback on this design (positive or negative), so it can be improved, thanks! A robust, print-in-place reusable spool designed specifically for eSUN/Sunlu PLA/PETG Refills (1KG) . Tired of the same old honeycomb hexagons and basic dots found on every single 3D printed spool? This design breaks the mold by introducing a unique, stylish geometric pattern that makes your setup stand out while still offering great filament visibility. Unlike standard Bambu-style spools that rely on alignment pins or over-engineered locking clips, this model features a heavy-duty triple-start thread system. It provides an incredibly secure, stable, and wobble-free grip, making it a reliable drop-in replacement for your AMS or standard spool holders. Features Unique Geometric Aesthetics: Designed for those who want something different and stylish. No more boring hex patterns or basic dots! Integrated Filament Anchors: Features 5 specialized holes distributed along the perimeter of each side. This allows you to easily secure the loose end of your filament at multiple angles, keeping it neat, organized, and safe from tangles during storage. Perfect Fit for eSUN/Sunlu: Designed according to eSUN/Sunlu refill core dimensions (59mm inner width, 200mm total diameter, and 82.2mm center core diameter). Triple Thread System: Fast, smooth fastening with high torque resistance. Once tightened, it locks firmly without needing extra safety parts. No Over-engineering: Clean, efficient, and simple. Just slide the refill in, twist the sides tightly, and you are ready to print. 100% Support-free: The geometry is fully optimized for 3D printing. No supports are needed for either half. Print Settings & Profile Info My uploaded print profile is optimized for a fast and material-saving print. Extreme mechanical resistance isn't necessary for my use case since I handle my spools with care and don't use active heated dryers inside my AMS. My Profile Settings (Works perfectly for me): Material: PLA Infill: 10% Walls/Perimeters: 2 walls Supports: None / NO Want some extra strength? If you prefer a sturdier spool, plan to drop it around, or use it in high-heat environments, feel free to bump it up to 3 walls and 20%+ infill . The choice is yours! Assembly Instructions: Insert your eSUN/Sunlu refill onto the wider core side. Important: Do NOT cut the plastic refill straps yet! Screw the opposite side tightly until it locks down firmly against the filament core. Note on Fit: Depending on how tightly the factory filament is wound, the two plastic halves may not flush together 100%, leaving a tiny gap. This is completely normal and expected due to slight variations in refill batches. Just ensure the triple thread is screwed down tightly to squeeze the filament securely. Once completely secure, snip and remove the refill straps. Happy printing!

This is a remixed model originally created by the very talented https://makerworld.com/en/@morph91. Original model link: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2749412-bc-250-gaming-pc-case-mk-ultra-uno . I'm naming this model the MK Ultra Uno Plus : ) I wanted to mod the original to fit my psu, but along the way I started tweaking a bit of everything and scope creep just kinda took over lol. As a note, there are two versions of the back half of the case. One fits the FSP500-30AS psu, and the other fits apevia itx flex psu's. The apevia version has one less internal clip when attaching the two case halves together so it may be less rigid when put together. Also dimensions for the apevia version I grabbed from lolheyaj 's print profile - I don't have an apevia psu myself to test, but it should work. Let me know if anyone is interested in a metalfish variant. Also, there's two versions of the fan shroud. Please print only one depending on your use case, see the print instructions for more info. Here's a list of all the modifications I did to the original: Changed front face design Changed front to use 12mm button Changed rear side design (small holes similar to actual pc cases) Removed rear side external psu latch and changed to internal psu lock instead Changed back design to fit FSP500-30AS Created another variant of back half of case to fit apevia flex psu's Changed back design to fit 40mm exhaust fan(s) Added interior clips/latches to connect the two halves of the case more securely Added stick on heatsinks next to fan shroud Changed fan shroud to have a small slit allowing for active airflow to the added heatsinks (this improved temps by 3-7C ingame with 40CU unlock and 2000MHz GPU OC) My Part List: BC250 PSU (fsp500-30as or apevia itx flex) makerworld.com/en/models/2527214-bc-250-scooper fin scooper to straighten fins https://a.co/d/0hZ28ifs for 12mm latching button (you may need a wire stripper, wire crimper, and dupont connectors if you copy me 1:1) https://a.co/d/0jdT5jNV arctic p12 pro pst (optional) https://a.co/d/063cMg66 noctua NF-A4x20 (optional) https://a.co/d/00RnzoEo stick on heatsinks, I bought 2 of these kits and used 3 out of the 4 heatsinks (optional) https://a.co/d/066uYDJ8 rubber anti vibration screws used to mount noctua 40mm fan Print Instructions: Print in PETG, and dry filament for 8 hours before printing (reduces stringing). Also only print one of the fan shrouds! If you plan to use stick on heatsinks like I did, then print the “heatsink variant” fan shroud plate. Otherwise, print the original fan shroud plate. Same with the print plates for the back half of the case, if you have a fsp500-30as psu then print that version. If you have an apevia flex psu, then print that one. The front half of the case fits both. Assembly Instructions: Take off IO shield and small bracket next to cmos battery Use the fin scooper to straighten the fins underneath where the fan shroud is gonna go. After straightening the fins, use an air duster to make sure any debris is blown off. Also if you haven't already, repaste the chip - it lowered my temps by 5C! Attach fan (recommend arctic p12 pro pst) with pins to fan shroud. Then attach fan shroud to pcb. Make sure the two small latches are pushed as far up as possible (in pic below you can see the one latch is in the corner of the pcb). Optionally here, if you have the stick on heatsinks (120x40x20mm), you can stick them right next to the fan slit. VERY IMPORTANT NOTE: If you do not have/don't plan to use stick on heatsinks print the plate with the original fan shroud instead! Put PSU into back half of case: Add psu latch on left side: Mount any 40mm fans now (both screws or rubber mounts work): Slide bc250 on alu backplate onto the back half of case. Plug in exhaust fan to the Y splitter of main fan. Plug in the 8 pin power cable: (This step is for FSP500-30AS psu, idk what pins to short for apevia psus but you can probably find out on reddit) Plug in latching button to PS_ON and GND. I crimped the wires into two male dupont connectors and put them in a 2pin housing. I slightly have to bend the metal pins to fit into the psu which creates enough friction where the pins don't fall out. There's probably a better solution for this… Attach front half of case, until both halves attach:

model_name: Will it stick? Adhesion / Warping Torture Test
description: Everyone runs their own warp/adhesion tests. Nobody else ever learns from them. Every time someone figures out whether a filament sticks to a plate, that answer stays in their head, and the next person burns time and filament rediscovering it. You end up getting people in discord or reddit or forums having their own tiny bit of anecdotal evidence, and everyone cargo cults it. Will It Stick fixes that: print one standard model, report what happened, and your result joins a free, searchable matrix of build plate × filament × surface prep results at willitstick.fyi . Because every data point comes from this exact model, results are directly comparable across plates, materials, and brands; one shared test instead of a thousand private ones nobody can see. One short print, three answers 1. First-layer adhesion: did the first layer grip without sliding or lifting? 2. Warping: are the corners and long edges still flat when the print finishes? 3. Ease of removal : does it release cleanly once cool, without damaging the plate? Your result feeds the community adhesion matrix at willitstick.fyi ; crowdsourced, like-for-like data on which filaments stick to which build plates, with which surface prep. Every result comes from this exact model, so combos are actually comparable. Submitting takes about two minutes and no account: snap one photo, record pass/fail for the three checks at https://willitstick.fyi/submit . Full protocol (with photo examples) at https://willitstick.fyi/how-to-test ⚠️ Because this model is deliberately brutal, a failure doesn't mean your plate or filament is bad! It's a way to compare plate performance with evidence instead of feels. Print Settings: A 3mf for OrcaSlicer 2.4.1 is available in “Download STL/CAD files” Layer Height 0.2mm Walls 4 Top Layers 2 Top Shell Thickness 0.4mm Bottom Layers 2 Sparse Infill Density 50% Sparse Infill Pattern Aligned Rectilinear Infill/Wall Overlap 20% Example results: printed with (extremely warp-prone) Bambu Lab PA6-GF The forbidden dorito: A much more slight warping failure (glue helps!): And a perfect pass: There's also useful overview information for each plate in the database! btw, the firethorn is the only plate so far that didn't warp with Bambu PA6-GF without glue . Contribute to 3d printing community science at https://willitstick.fyi !

description: VERSION FRANÇAISE Support AMS HT pour Simple AMS Flipper de Jakob — fixation directe sur l'ossature, réversible G/D Mon nouveau AMS HT venait d'arriver, il me fallait un support compatible avec le Simple AMS Flipper de Jakob : 🔗 https://makerworld.com/fr/models/1815860-h2-simple-ams-flipper Pourquoi ce design plutôt que le support officiel de Jakob ? Le support AMS-HT de Jakob se fixe sur le châssis de l'imprimante. Le mien s'accroche directement sur l'ossature du Flipper, en s'appuyant sur la structure triangulée du bras — comme on le voit sur le rendu CAD ci-dessus. C'est une approche différente, pas un remplacement : à toi de voir laquelle correspond le mieux à ton montage. Caractéristiques Fixation par clipsage / insertion sur les triangles du bras, aucun outil ni visserie nécessaire Réversible gauche/droite : un seul design en miroir, mais je fournis directement les 2 fichiers STL prêts à imprimer (pas besoin de mirrorer toi-même dans Bambu Studio) Compatible avec le bras droit court (version ventilée) — même système de fixation par triangles Profil pensé pour rester compact et garder le Flipper pleinement fonctionnel une fois l'AMS HT en place Hauteur du support calculée pour laisser entièrement libre la fenêtre de visualisation intérieure de l'imprimante Matériau recommandé Imprimé et utilisé en PETG-CF chez moi — bon compromis rigidité/qualité de finition, et la teinte cuivrée rend plutôt bien sur la pièce. Je n'ai pas testé en PLA et je ne le recommande pas pour cette pièce : c'est un élément structurel qui supporte le poids de l'AMS HT (1.2 kg) + 1 bobine pleine , mieux vaut une matière rigide. A peine de fléchissement malgré les + de 2kg de poids : Impression Le fichier nécessite des supports, mais l'orientation a été pensée pour les limiter au maximum : la pièce est positionnée à l'envers sur le plateau (dessus contre le plateau) Mise à jour : amortisseurs TPU anti-vibrations Pour limiter les vibrations entre le support et la carrosserie de l'imprimante, j'ajoute deux petits amortisseurs en TPU qui s'insèrent par friction (sans colle) sur le cadre bas du support, au point de contact avec l'imprimante. Le support n'étant pas forcément parfaitement parallèle à la carrosserie, chaque cale a un côté de 8 mm et l'autre de 10 mm : il suffit de la retourner pour s'adapter à l'écart réel de ton montage. Ce support fait partie d'un écosystème de pièces développées pour le Simple AMS Flipper H2D : TPU Flipper mount: Right bearing roller mount F eet for Flipper without top glass AMS HT-Direct mount on Flipper arm Simple AMS TPU Feed Assist for AMS Flipper simple Si ce mod te rend service, un boost fait toujours plaisir 🙂 Et si tu l'imprimes, je serai heureux de voir vos prints et photos de montage, ça fait toujours plaisir 🤩 ENGLISH VERSION AMS HT mount for Jakob's Simple AMS Flipper — mounts directly on the flipper frame, left/right reversible My new AMS HT had just arrived, so I needed a mount compatible with Jakob's Simple AMS Flipper: 🔗 https://makerworld.com/fr/models/1815860-h2-simple-ams-flipper Why this design instead of Jakob's official AMS-HT mount? Jakob's AMS-HT bracket attaches to the printer's frame. Mine clips directly onto the Flipper's own arm, using its triangular truss structure — as shown in the CAD render above. It's a different approach, not a replacement: pick whichever fits your setup better. Features Clip-on mount onto the arm's triangle frame, no tools or screws needed Left/right reversible: one mirrored design, but I provide both STL files ready to print directly (no need to mirror it yourself in Bambu Studio) Compatible with the short right arm (vented version) — same triangle mounting system Compact profile that keeps the Flipper fully functional once the AMS HT is attached Mount height calculated to keep the printer's internal viewing window fully unobstructed Recommended material Printed and used in PETG-CF on my own setup — good balance of rigidity and finish quality, and the copper tone actually looks great on the part. Haven't tested it in PLA and wouldn't recommend it for this part: it's a structural piece carrying the AMS HT's weight, so a rigid material is preferable. Only a few flex even under 2kg+ of load : Printing This part does require supports, but the orientation has been worked out to keep them to a minimum: the part is positioned upside down on the bed (top side down) Update: TPU anti-vibration dampers To reduce vibration between the mount and the printer's body, I'm adding two small TPU dampers that press-fit (no glue) onto the bottom frame of the mount, right where it contacts the printer. Since the mount isn't always perfectly parallel to the printer's body, each damper has one side at 8 mm and the other at 10 mm — just flip it around to match the actual gap on your setup. description: Ever buy a used printer and not be confident that it works as advertised? Don't take that gamble! Send the seller this test model to run prior to you arriving, and request that they leave it on the build plate as proof that the printer works as advertised. There is no denying that the printer printed it, if its still stuck to the build plate when you arrive! This model is not a calibration model , it does not test over hangs, extrusion, nothing like that. This test was designed to make sure the printer can print most of the build plate, as well as show that the Z axis is clean and not bend. You can scale it up or down, but going too small will make that first layer pretty thin. I recommend scaling so the bottom is only 1 layer thick. That will show you how even the bed is and if the printer can print big flat models. The vertical part will show the z axis wear and tear, as well as show layer shifts, VFAs, ghosting and overall print quality. Check around the engraved letters for ghosting and VFAs, check around the corners to see proper extrusion and cornering and ringing, check the circle section to see if there are visible layer shifting. Finally check the pyramid top to ensure it can complete a top without knocking the entire model below over. Again, this is not a test of calibration, just a simple test model for you to be confident that the used printer you are buying can perform basic 3D printer tasks. Here we are again, 3D printing enthusiasts! It's mid-2026 and, after more than a year, I'm back with a new version of the "Great Calibrator," thanks to the success of previous versions. The model has undergone a redesign, losing some of the components that had been added to the main model over time and acquiring new ones (few, but effective). But the most impressive aspect is its compactness, precision, and ease of reading the tests, all while, of course, providing a good amount of stress to both your printer's steppers and nozzles, as well as the filament you're testing. Use is as simple and intuitive as ever: once printing is complete, let the print bed cool completely , then fold it and remove the main base. If your printer (or filament, or both) are already well calibrated, you'll notice that many parts will remain attached to the bed or will move away from it without remaining connected to the main base. This should (definitely) happen for the hinge and the bolt, as well as (probably) for the pins with the widest tolerance. Pins 3 and below may require a little pressure on the top. Caution: Don't use excessive force or tools to force a pin out. The goal is to read the tolerance allowed by the printer/filament combination under the conditions you printed under. An extreme unsuccessful print A successful print Let's review the model's components. Walls: The walls surrounding the main base should measure 0.8 mm , consisting of two 0.4 mm walls (the width of the standard nozzle). Turrets: As in previous versions, there are two turrets with a suspended sinusoidal upper part for support testing. You can therefore easily distinguish which method you prefer based on the results obtained. NOTE: There are two versions: the standard single-material version and the dual-material version that uses PETG and PLA for support separation. You'll notice some differences… Bridges: The bridge test is always present (the one on the far left with slopes of 45°, 60°, and the dreaded 75°) which, in theory, shouldn't pose any problems for your printers. I remind you that a "bridge" is a joint distance between two support points , and the different slopes are supported by two side walls. Half-bridges: Just like the bridges, to their right, at the center, you'll find the slopes for testing a half-bridge . What is it? Very simple, it's an overhang supported by a support on only one side , and the Great Calibrator gives you the ability to check the results for both sides. Overhang: A classic among classics, located to the right of the half-bridge, it has always been the biggest problem for a 3D printer: the "suspended" filament, meaning it's printed in "air" without any support. It depends on the extrusion capacity, filament cooling, rigidity, and the airflow system to your nozzle. The slopes don't change, but the 75° slope is more or less where the limit of what a filament printer can achieve stable overhanging ends. To verify them, it's not only important to note whether the lower part is aligned and not "spaghetti-like," but also to verify that the upper part can be completed with a good-looking top surface. Blades: The so-called "blades" have always been a distinctive feature of the Great Calibrator , as they allow for verification, and therefore adjustment, of the complexity of an extrusion balanced between thicknesses and spacing. These "blades" have a thickness that, from top to bottom, gradually decreases from 1.2 mm to a minimum of 0.4 mm (standard nozzle), with minimum distances that also decrease ( down to 0.05 ). The last distance may not be read at the slicer level, unless corrections are made or extrusion is somehow forced. This test (slicer stress) can therefore be verified already during the slicing phase without having to force printing in priority (the parameters provided with the model ensure that the last two blades are joined). Stringing stress cones : Here's another classic, placed in the center of the base, with the peculiarity that has always distinguished the Great Calibrator : the cones are not parallel to each other and not all perpendicular to the base. Obtaining a clean, smooth slin, complete cones, and no stringing will depend greatly on the quality of the filament, the extrusion temperatures, the quality of the nozzles, and so on. As you can see from the images, I managed to achieve excellent results with a simple A1 and a basic PLA filament from Bambulab . M-K-Nick : It's not the name of a rapper or a DJ, but the name of the "mechanical" innovation of the calibrator. Its shape and thickness are very unique and were specifically designed to be "easy" to print. The result should be a piece with properties that are elastic enough to be removed from the base without any effort (if your fingers aren't very fine, try using a simple tweezers, but don't force it. It should come out easily, despite the mechanical "block" caused by its particular shape). Bolt with its Nut: Here it is again, the essential bolt for testing the nut printed in the base circle. A well-calibrated printer should not cause any problems, so the nut should be easily screwed and unscrewed onto the bolt. The thread is standard, but the tolerance is approximately 0.2 mm between each wall, resulting in a total tolerance (circumference) of 0.4 mm. Som e problems may arise from the overhang required by creating the nut thread and/or the bolt itself . Parallelepiped dimensions : The block, as you can easily see, should measure 50 mm wide and 10 mm high and deep. Take the measurement, avoiding getting too close to the Base. Hinge: The other mechanical part of the Great Calibrator is this sort of "3-plate hinge" that can be used to test the possibility of performing some "on-plate direct printing" operations on mechanical parts. The plates that make up the hinge must be able to release with minimal effort and, once released, after a few bends to the left and right, they should have a fluid movement. Finally, don't forget the writing on the base, which must be perfectly legible: “ THE GREAT CALIBRATOR V1.0 BETA 04/2026" (yes... exactly, I started redesigning it in April lol)”. Try it, send me the print results and let's compare them. Together, we'll find solutions to the most common 3D printing problems and, above all, let's make "THE GREAT CALIBRATOR" a unique and indispensable model for all enthusiasts. description: X2D Support Test – Multi-Material Support Benchmark Dieses Modell wurde speziell entwickelt, um die Qualität von Supportstrukturen und Multi-Material-Drucke objektiv zu bewerten. Durch die verschiedenen Überhänge, Aussparungen, Brücken und Kontaktflächen eignet sich der Test hervorragend, um die Druckqualität unterschiedlicher Materialkombinationen zu vergleichen und optimale Einstellungen für saubere Support-Oberflächen zu finden. Was wird getestet? Oberflächenqualität über Supportstrukturen Maßhaltigkeit kritischer Geometrien Qualität von Überhängen und Brücken Trennbarkeit der Supports Einfluss verschiedener Interface-Materialien Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch Vorteile von Multi-Material Supports Durch die Verwendung eines separaten Support-Interface-Materials lassen sich deutlich sauberere Unterseiten und Kontaktflächen erzielen als mit Supports aus dem gleichen Material. Besonders bei anspruchsvollen Überhängen können dadurch: glattere Oberflächen bessere Maßhaltigkeit weniger Nacharbeit einfachere Supportentfernung erreicht werden. Empfohlene Druckvarianten Variante 1 – Nur Support-Interface in anderem Material (empfohlen) Hier wird das Modell und die eigentlichen Supportstrukturen mit dem Hauptmaterial gedruckt. Lediglich die Support-Schnittstellen (Support Interface Layers) werden mit einem zweiten Material erzeugt. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports: PLA Support Interface: PETG Diese Methode bietet in der Regel das beste Verhältnis aus Druckqualität, Materialverbrauch und Druckzeit. Variante 2 – Komplette Supports in anderem Material Alternativ können sowohl die Supportstrukturen als auch die Support-Schnittstellen vollständig aus einem zweiten Material gedruckt werden. Beispiel: Modell: PLA Supports + Interface: PETG Diese Variante kann die Trennbarkeit weiter verbessern, erhöht jedoch den Materialwechsel erheblich. Wichtig: Durch die vielen Werkzeugwechsel zwischen den Materialien verlängert sich die Druckzeit deutlich und es entsteht zusätzlicher Materialabfall durch Spülvorgänge. Für die meisten Anwendungen ist daher Variante 1 die sinnvollere Wahl. Empfohlene Materialkombinationen PLA ↔ PETG PETG ↔ PLA ASA ↔ Support Material ABS ↔ Support Material Viel Spaß beim Testen! Teile gerne deine Ergebnisse, Einstellungen und Materialkombinationen in den Kommentaren, damit andere Nutzer von deinen Erfahrungen profitieren können. Hinweis Die Vorschaubilder und Darstellungen in diesem Eintrag wurden mithilfe von KI-generierten Grafiken erstellt und dienen ausschließlich der Veranschaulichung des Druckkonzepts. Das tatsächliche Druckergebnis kann je nach Drucker, Material und Einstellungen abweichen.

model_name: Light and Fast Dual AMS Mount for H/X/P Series
description: I wanted a mount that didn't take too long to print or require too much material so I designed a mount that utilizes the weight of the AMS itself to help the mount clamp against the machine and keep the structure light. Unfortunately, the machines are not exactly the overall dimensions that Bambu cites. To accommodate this, the structure is broken into pieces that can be connected at various lengths to accommodate various printer sizes. This also makes them compatible with various models of Bambu machines. I also managed to fit all the parts in a single X/P series bed. H2C/H2S/H2D P2S X1C /X1E P1S/P1P AMS 2 AMS (3 Cavity) AMS (5 Cavity) Verified X X X X X Compatible X X Incompatible Note for High Temp Users: High temp printing with chamber heating will heat the printer glass beyond the glass transition temperature of PLA. This will cause warping of the structure. Please print the mount from a high temp plastic if you plan on printing chamber heated materials. If you only print PLA, this should not be an issue. Here is how the structure works: AMS weight hanging over the edge of the machine pushes down, forcing supports to pivot around the edge of the machine. Supports are retained by central tension member, which drives force into the side of the machine. Forces driving into side of machine increase friction between support and machine, improving grip. Small nubs on the central support posts retain both AMS units against each other, and prevent them from moving when the printer shakes. Size the frames so they are snug to the machine. If the notches only allow a slightly loose or slightly tight fit, choose the tight one. Once the weight of the AMS is loaded on top, any bowing in the structure will flatten out. The assembly utilizes toothed connections which are finely tuned to slide together and retain themselves with the layer lines of the print. If parts are too tight, they can likely be tapped together with a hammer without issue, just dont expect to get them back apart. model_name: Parametric A1 PTFE Guide w. Ball Joint, for A1/A2L
description: Bambu A1 and A2L Swiveling PTFE Tube Guide - Parametric, with Print-in-Place Ball Joint If you've ever glanced over mid-print and noticed your drybox or your AMS Lite slowly sliding toward the print bed - pulled there by a taut filament tube - this one's for you. PTFE tube management is one of those details that seems trivial until it isn't. A loose or unsecured tube puts real tension on whatever it's attached to: a desktop spool holder, an AMS Lite, or a drybox on a shelf. Some existing guides rely on a dovetail joint or a friction fit that works fine in theory - until the repeated motion of printing slowly works the joint loose, and by the time you notice something is wrong, your setup has already been dragged somewhere it shouldn't be. I learned this the hard way so I designed my own. My design uses a fully print-in-place ball joint: it articulates freely so the tube always follows the print head without resistance, but the ball is physically captured inside the housing - there's no clip, no friction fit, nothing that can pull apart under load. The lever is printed horizontally so its strength doesn't rely on layer adhesion at all. And the C-clip uses a carefully angled opening that holds the tubes in place during normal use. Fully Parametric Configure four values to match your setup: Guide placement - top of the printer (usually for external spools) or towards the front (usually for a side-mounted AMS Lite) Guide diameter - size the C-clip to your tube count and diameter Lever length - a short lever works for most prints; increase it if you frequently print very tall models and need more slack Ball joint offset - position the guide towards the front, center, or back of the top bar Pre-configured standard variants are published alongside this model, so if your setup is typical you can go straight to printing without touching a single parameter. Printing note After printing, gently move the lever in the joint until it becomes loose and starts swiveling. Longer lever variants require a small horizontal bridge support under the lever. The included print profiles handle this automatically. Happy printing !

model_name: Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite - TPU Replacement Strap
description: A quick and durable replacement strap for the Xiaomi Redmi Watch 5 Lite, designed in Fusion 360 to be printed in flexible TPU. Instead of buying third-party hardware, this design allows you to reuse the metal pins and the buckle from your old, broken strap by embedding them directly inside the print! 📌 What You Need Your old, broken Xiaomi Watch 5 Lite strap. A utility knife / hobby knife (Cutter). TPU Filament (Shore hardness 95A recommended for comfort and durability). 🛠️ Step-by-Step Instructions Step 1: Salvage the Original Hardware Take your old strap and use a utility knife to carefully slice open the TPU/rubber around the connection points. Extract the two metal tubes/pins from the watch-connecting ends. Extract the buckle mechanism (the plastic/metal locking clasp at the end of the strap). Step 2: Slicer Setup & Printing (Crucial!) To securely trap the original hardware inside the new strap, you need to set up two pauses in your slicer (e.g., Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) at the specific layer heights where the internal cavities close. Pause 1 (Buckle Clasp): Set a pause right before the cavity for the end buckle closes. Slide the original clasp into the designated slot (I use tape to secure it) and resume printing. Pause 2 (Strap Pins): Set a second pause right before the printer covers the slots for the metal connecting pins. Drop the salvaged pins into place and resume printing. ⚠️ Important Note: Make sure the salvaged metal pins and buckle are completely flush and seated deep within their slots during the pauses. If they stick out, the print head might collide with them when resuming! ⚙️ Recommended Print Settings Material: TPU (95A) Infill: 15% - 20% (Gyroid or 3D Honeycomb for good flexibility) Perimeters/Walls: 3 for extra strength around the joint areas. Supports: Not needed. I hope it will be useful to you :)

model_name: Minimal Filament Respooler for AMS Lite V2
description: This is a filament respooler that uses the structure of the Bambu Lab AMS Lite. It is an improved and updated version of my previously released model. A Bambu Lab AMS Lite is required to use this model. The printed parts cannot be used on their own. By utilizing the AMS Lite’s structure, filament can be transferred to another spool smoothly and reliably with only a small number of printed parts. The complete set requires approximately 90 g of filament to print. It supports manual operation with the included hand crank, as well as electric screwdrivers, electric drills, and ratchet wrenches. A dedicated storage case is also included to keep all the parts neatly organized when not in use. All parts can be printed on an A1 mini. Instructions 1. Assemble the Hand Crank The hand crank is assembled from three printed parts. The small hexagonal adapter is used when respooling with a ratchet wrench and a 10 mm socket. 2. Install the Holder on the AMS Lite Remove one rotary spool holder from the AMS Lite. Insert the printed inner holder onto the exposed AMS Lite shaft. This holder does not rotate, so the fitting is intentionally designed to be tight. 3. Install the Spools Screw the respooling core into the empty spool and tighten it securely. Install the empty receiving spool on the side fitted with the printed inner holder. Install the spool containing the filament on another spool holder of the AMS Lite. Pull out the filament and secure its end to the empty spool. 4. Respool the Filament For manual operation, attach the hand crank. When using an electric screwdriver, insert the hex driver bit fully into the drive socket. When using an electric drill, attach a 10 mm hex bit. When using a ratchet wrench, insert the included adapter and then attach a 10 mm socket. Important Notes An AMS Lite is required to use this model. This respooler does not include a mechanism for automatically distributing the filament evenly across the spool. Guide the filament from side to side by hand while respooling to prevent it from accumulating in one area. When using a power tool, always operate it slowly at a low speed.

model_name: Ultimate Top Layer Calibration (No Ironing Needed)
description: Tired of waiting hours for "Ironing" to finish, or dealing with the rough, inconsistent top surfaces on your prints? This comprehensive Top Layer Calibration Matrix helps you systematically find the perfect balance between Top Surface Line Width and Top Surface Speed for any filament. Dial in a flawless, smooth, and shiny top finish purely through optimized extrusion mechanics! This test utilizes a grid layout (Columns 1–5 and Rows A–K) featuring both flat rectangular sections and concentric circular test pads (as previewed in the slicer toolpath view). This allows you to evaluate how different settings handle straight infill lines versus tight, curved perimeters. How It Works (The Matrix Grid) The model is divided into a 5x11 grid matrix. Each cell modifies two critical variables to let you visually and texturally pick your winner: Columns (1 – 5): Top Surface Line Width 1: 0.30 mm 2: 0.35 mm 3: 0.40 mm 4: 0.45 mm 5: 0.50 mm Rows (A – K): Top Surface Speed A: 25 mm/s B: 50 mm/s C: 75 mm/s D: 100 mm/s E: 125 mm/s F: 150 mm/s G: 175 mm/s H: 200 mm/s I: 225 mm/s J: 250 mm/s K: 275 mm/s How to Use This Model Download & Slice: Open the provided .3mf file or arrange the model flat on your build plate. Apply Settings: Ensure you use a multi-modifier layout or a calibrated project file where each block/cell is mapped to its respective speed and width coordinates listed above or just hit SLICE without changing any parameters . Print & Inspect: Once printed, run your finger across the bed and tilt it under a strong light source. Look out for gaps between lines (under-extrusion/too narrow). Look out for rough ridges or scarring (over-extrusion/too wide or too fast). Save Your Profile: Find the single cell that looks perfectly smooth, flat, and uniform. Note its column and row values, and apply those exact settings to your favorite slicer profile!

Regular PLA can warp or sag under heavy heat. Because of this, I highly recommend using industrial-grade structural filaments from SUNLU . For ultimate outdoor durability and UV protection (crucial if you troop in sunny weather), use SUNLU ASA Filament . It resists yellowing, handles the heat, and leaves a gorgeous professional matte finish that hides layer lines beautifully. If you want high-toughness, impact resistance, and an easier overall print profile, go with SUNLU PETG Filament . Explore all options on the SUNLU Official Filament Store . 🛠️ Structural Assembly: Skip the Glue, Weld Your Prints! For multi-part prop builds like the helmet visor, utility belt, and large chest plates, conventional superglues are a weak point waiting to snap on the showroom floor. Instead, I highly recommend plastic welding your seams together. By using a hot stapler / plastic welder kit, you can melt metal reinforcing staples directly across the interior seams of your prints, followed by smoothing the plastic over with a hot iron attachment. This creates a permanent, structural plastic bond that will survive the stresses of walking and moving around in full kit. description: Want a realistic life-size V40 Mini Grenade with a flying handle? This model is 100% brand new from the ground-up with stronger parts, easy screw-on assembly, and enhanced realism. What is the v40 Mini Grenade? The V40 Mini Grenade is an unusually compact fragmentation hand grenade developed in the Netherlands that is roughly the size of a golf ball. Weighing just 4.8 ounces, it allowed soldiers to carry the weapon in much greater quantities than standard fragmentation grenades. It gained historical fame for its utilization by U.S. special operations units during the Vietnam War. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu Filaments used Metal Iron Gray black Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Bambu Matte Dark Green is the closest Bambu filament Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the peg into the grenade topper as you see below. 2. Then insert a metal spring int the same way. 3. Lastly, screw the topper onto the body of the grenade – it helps to do this upside down or sideways so the spring doesn't fall out. Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Insert the printed plastic spring into the grenade topper as you see below. Make sure the peg at the top of the spring is sticking out the top, rotate it until it pops out if not. 2. Lastly, screw the topper onto the grenade body – its easiest if you do this upside down or sideways.

The Legacy of the Dark Lord Darth Vader remains one of the most recognizable figures in modern mythology. Originally Anakin Skywalker, a gifted Jedi Knight, his tragic fall to the dark side of the Force transformed him into a fearsome cyborg enforcer for the Galactic Empire. Clad in his signature black life-support armor and mask, Vader serves as a symbol of absolute power and ruthless authority. model_name: Iron Man Helmet A1 Mini | All Printers Compatible
description: Wearable Iron Man MK3 helmet , fully optimized for printing on all 3D printers, including the A1 Mini. Stop wasting your time and start printing this masterpiece! The model dimensions are designed based on what I consider the international standard: Budwin's Sizing Head No. 3 , whom I deeply thank for making it available and making everyone's life easier. Main Features & Smart Cutting No Harsh Cuts: The cuts follow the helmet's design lines, making the joints invisible from the outside for a clean look. No Circling: Dividing the model into pieces eliminates the "stair-stepping" effect on the dome typical of single-piece prints, ensuring a smooth surface with no sanding needed. Easy Printing: Splitting the project reduces individual print session times and the risk of failures, making it accessible to anyone with any printer. Multi-Color Without AMS: The black and gold parts are separated from the main body, allowing you to print them directly with the correct color filament even without an automatic material system. Improved Ergonomics and Fit: The back section has been modified for a complete design, the ears have been hollowed out to increase width, and the eyes are perforated to ensure visibility. Custom Display Stand: In the last photo, you can see this fantastic stand custom-made for this helmet to display it at its best! Magnetic Mechanics (No Electronics!) By following the video instructions and watching the uploaded GIFs, you can achieve a fully functional mechanical opening without the need for complex circuits. Magnetic Back: The first GIF shows you how to implement a magnetic closure that improves fit when wearing the helmet. On plate number 9, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed to close the back of the mask. Magnetic Faceplate: The second GIF shows you how to implement magnets that allow the mask to open and lock onto the upper section. High-quality magnets are recommended for a stronger hold. On plates number 10 and 11, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed for this purpose. Hidden Magnet Clips: The front and back clips have a different design. The front ones are specifically engineered to completely hide the magnets from view; however, they require a stronger magnet grip, so feel free to use the clips from plate 9 for both purposes. However, you still need Plate 10 because it has the taller clips used to keep the faceplate open! Maximum Freedom: By separating the magnet holders from the main structure of the helmet, the final choice is up to you: you can use this magnetic system, implement your own motorized electronic mechanisms, or simply weld all the pieces together. 🛠️ Assembly Guide The pieces must be joined after printing. Among the uploaded photos, you will also find a visual diagram explaining how to pair them. You can use glue, but for the best results, a permanent bond, and high mechanical resistance, I recommend using a soldering iron or a 3D pen to carefully melt and weld the joints from the inside . I welded the entire helmet myself without any problems, as you can see for yourself from the photos of the finished project! Pro-tip: I recommend starting by joining the top and back-top pieces. Since they are the largest parts, they are the trickiest, join them by gently pressing the two parts together to ensure there is no gap. All of this makes this mask a masterpiece! Happy printing! - GB

model_name: Frodo's Sting sword The Lord of the Rings
description: This is the elven sword Sting , Frodo's sword from The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. The sword is designed in a full-scale 1:1 size and has an overall length of 559 mm . Both the blade and the guard feature the original Elvish inscriptions. Maegnas aen estar nín – dagnir in yngyl im = "Sting is my name; I am the bane of spiders." The core of the sword consists of a 490 mm long M5 threaded rod , which mechanically connects all parts into one solid assembly without the use of glue. A safety M5 nut is embedded in the Blade_up part. A second safety M5 nut is inserted into the Grip part, which is designed for two-color filament printing using an AMS system. A standard M5 nut is embedded in the Pommel_A part. The assembly procedure and part layout can be seen in the exploded_view drawing located in the gallery of this model. For an impressive effect, the blade is printed using fluorescent PLA filament that glows blue in the dark after being exposed to light, just as Sting glowed blue in the movies when orcs were nearby. For the blade, I used Spectrum PLA Glow in the Dark Blue filament. To further enhance the display and allow the sword to be hung on a wall, I also designed a dedicated wall mount. The wall mount features beautiful golden ornaments and the inscription from the One Ring: The base of the wall mount is printed in two separate parts, which are fastened together using three M5×30 socket head screws and nuts . A separately printed ring featuring the inscription from the One Ring, along with the golden ornaments, is glued into the base. The sword itself is supported by two M6 L-hooks with a length of 60 mm . The assembly and all individual parts can be seen in the exploded_view image located in the gallery of this model. The threaded rod, screws, nuts, and L-hooks can be purchased at any Hobby market. The print profile is well-tuned and easy to print, making this project suitable for everyone. I hope this sword brings you joy, and enjoy its blue glow during the evening hours—it is truly an impressive sight, just like in the The Lord of the Rings movies. Happy printing!

description: Want a life-size replica of the Laser Guided APKWS Rocket used by the US, Ukraine, NATO, and many other militaries? This is around ~6ft / ~2m long and can be assembled in seconds just by screwing the printed parts together, no glue is required. It comes with moving fold-out fins for extra realism. You can also print optional wall mounts to place it on the wall. It is designed to use as little filament as possible while still being strong and sturdy. Note: this new model is completely interchangable with my other Hydra rocket models (the screw-together version, not the peg assembly version). So you can print any parts from this model and combine it with other hydra rockets you've printed. Bambu filaments used Warhead at the top Basic Yellow Silk+ Titan Gray Overture Silk Copper ( Amazon link ) Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Rocket Body Basic Light Gray A white filament would work as well Silk+ Red Silk+ Silver (for the mid-body fins) Polymaker Metallic Silver ( Amazon link ) Basic Silver would work great too Engine Metal Iridium Gold Silk+ Gold would work too Assembly is super easy The parts simply screw together, so if you make a mistake you can just unscrew and re-screw in seconds, no problems. Make sure you don't over tighten – they are quite strong, but all plastic screws can eventually break under enough pressure – you should be able to screw them until they feel snug. 1. Screw the main body together, which includes 4 longer white/gray segments, one shorter red segment, and one short white/gray segment. 2. Then take each of the silver fins and connect all 4 to a base by sliding them together. It may take a little bit of forcer, pushing down on a table can help. 3. Now the assembled fins and clip them into the tall gray section. They should snap in easily if you line it up right. If you can't get the fins to snap in, try a different (probably lower) angle. 4. Next begin screwing on the other parts one by one to the far right end (the end with the red strip). 5. Then, assemble the warhead portion at the tip with the pegs provided like you see below and screw it onto the top of the rocket. 6. Lastly, begin connecting the rocket motor by connecting the top threaded piece to the bottom piece with the two long pegs provided. 7. Then the final step is to attach the fins to the rocket motor – the will snap into place with little force. Note that they must be facing clockwise , not counter clockwise. If you insert them counter clockwise you will find that they don't fold all the way.

Check out all of my Fortnite Guns! 2026: Fortnite Twin Mag SMG Electric Water Gun 2026: Fortnite Wrecker Revolver 2025: Fortnite P90 Compact SMG 2025: Fortnite Mammoth Pistol 2025: Fortnite Holo Twister Rifle 2025: Fortnite Scoped Burst SMG 2025: Fortnite Havoc Shotgun 2024: Fortnite Gatekeeper Shotgun 2024: Fortnite Scar After many many hours spent modeling, testing, printing, remodeling, and retesting, I am proud to release the Twin Mag SMG Water Gun. This model uses two items from the Bambu Store - their Electric Spray Kit #02 and steel 5x35mm pins. 100% PETG Highly Recommended for this model! You can print stress free using my custom profiles organized by color. Every piece has been carefully individually sliced: Blue Parts: Top Rail Black Parts #1: Small Black Pieces Black Parts #2: Large Black Pieces Brown Parts: Handguard and Bracket Red Parts: Accent Pieces Blue Parts No Watergun/No Holes: This is the top rail without dowel holes if you want to glue things shut without the water gun kit. You could probably combine the two black plates if you try, but I wanted to split up the main long print and a bunch of small pieces just in case. This model will push the limits of what your 3D Printer can create. By the end, you will have a product that make you forget it started as a roll of filament. Every millimeter of this model has been considered and designed for 3D printing. You will need several items that are not 3D printable: Electric Water Spray Kit #02 (~$11 per kit from Bambu) (2) 5mm x 35mm Pins (~$1 for 5-pack from Bambu) Gel Super Glue Short Piece of Filament Scissors or Flush Wire Cutters Refer to the assembly PDF for easy instructions! The Glue Help piece is not part of the final product, it is to help align the brown handguard horizontally when upside-down on a table during assembly only. No glue ever touches the Glue Help piece. This model can also be assembled without the electric spray kit or dowels; you just need to use glue to connect the top rail to the body and print the blue rails with no holes. You can also print the normal blue rails, there will just be visible holes for the dowels. Please keep in mind you are not printing one model - you are printing 20 models and a couple may require a skip/reprint/re-do. Hopefully not though! I know there will be plenty of people that will click print on each plate and have zero problems with their perfectly dialed in printer and filament just like my other models! I put a lot of effort in these uploads to make printing as smooth as possible and easy to assemble. These easy to print and easy to assemble uploads are not necessarily easy or quick to design! description: Instant Ronin Double Tanto - Magnetic Knives Channel your inner samurai with the Instant Ronin - Double Tanto (Magnetic Edition) ! This isn't just a pair of sleek 3D-printable props—it's a fully mechanical, dual-sword ecosystem. By utilising a precise arrangement of 5-off 6mm x 3mm magnets per sword, these Tantos completely ditch traditional metal springs for solid-state physics. But here is the real kicker: One sword acts as the activator for the other. Mating the companion sword into the other triggers the magnetic mechanisms, releasing the internal locks and allowing for an instant, seamless locking - and the reverse when withdrawing. Absolutely zero glue required. Every magnet pocket has been engineered for a perfect, satisfying, push-fit. Print two, link them up, and prepare to lose hours of your life to the ultimate fidget experience. Features Triple-Action Magnetic Mechanics: Uses opposing and attracting magnetic fields to safely lock the blades closed, assist the deployment, and lock them open. 5-Magnet Precision Layout: Optimised specifically for standard, high-strength 6mm x 3mm cylinder magnets (5-off per sword). 100% Glue-Free Assembly: Meticulously tuned tolerances mean every magnet snaps tightly into place. Save the superglue for fixing the things you break with the Tanto. Zero Mechanical Springs: No metal springs to find, bend, fatigue, or lose tension over time—magnetism doesn't wear out! Dual-Tanto Blade Profile: A sleek, aggressive geometric aesthetic that looks as sharp as the mechanism feels. Maximum Fidget Factor Magnet Assembly Guide ⚠️ Crucial Tip: Because these are a push-fit, double-check your magnet orientation before you press them home. Getting a backward magnet out of a tight 3D-printed pocket is a special kind of pain you don't want to experience. Use a spare magnet as a reference tool! Follow this exact sequence to ensure the polarity works flawlessly, see my sectioned CAD image and assembly pictures to help with the below: The Master Slider Magnet [1]: Push a magnet into the bottom pocket of the Blade Slider . This can face any direction you like. Once it’s in, this magnet is the "Master" that dictates the rest of the build. The Extended Lock [2]: Press a magnet into the lower forward pocket of the Handle . This magnet must REPEL Magnet #1. (This repelling force is the secret sauce that lifts the slider up into the notch to lock the blade open!) The Retracted Lock [3]: Press a magnet into the bottom rear pocket of the Handle . This magnet must ATTRACT Magnet #1, snapping the blade securely closed so they doesn't slide apart when closed. The Kinetic "Spring" Caps [4]: Press one magnet into each of the two Circular Caps at the top hilt. Both of these magnets must REPEL each other, creating that crisp, snappy detent.

Supports: None required. All parts are designed to print cleanly in their default orientation. The Tube & Caps: Standard settings. The Darts (CRITICAL): Print the darts standing straight up on their wide base. Set your infill to 100% so the nose prints completely solid for forward-weighting. model_name: Mandalorian Grav Charge With Lightup Mod (Breach)
description: This is my version of the Grav Charge and holder from the show The Mandalorian. I designed it looking at pictures from the show to be as accurate as I could but also be a light up prop. To that end I designed it around these little magnet operated light up warning lights: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMTJQRYX . The lights have a reed sensor in them that when the magnet is on the back they don't do anything but when you remove the magnet they light up. And the pattern is similar to the actual grav charge, close enough without needing expensive electronics or wiring anything. The back of the holder has some indents of 15mm magnets. Glue some magnets to the back and that will be strong enough to keep the light off. When you pull the grav charge off the holder the reed switch turns the unit on and the lights start to flash then after about 10 seconds go to the circular pattern. I added magnets on the bottom of the grav charges themselves also so you can still stick it to something like in the show but without affecting the light. Place it back on the holder and it turns back off. I went with these lights because they also turn themselves off after a couple minutes so they won't kill the battery if you leave them out. Print Details I printed the body and holder in Bambu ABS - Silver. The body has scarf seam turned on in its object settings which leaves less of a seam on the outside but does sometime affect the color slightly in that spot. If you are going to paint them leave scarf seam on, if you are going to leave them as is you may want to turn that off so the color is more consistent but the seam will be more noticeable. The cover is Bambu PETG Translucent Clear that I then used a red Sharpie oil based paint pen on because I couldn't find a good clear red filament. The combination ended up looking really good so that's what I would recommend or even possibly just a red marker. For printing the cover I have the speeds set to 20mm/s and a custom Bambu Transparent PETG setting that turns off cooling. It's the only way to get a mostly clear lens but you can of course use standard settings, the lens just might not be as clear and the LEDs won't be as distinguishable. Or you can buy a after market clear lens sized for about 28mm. I tried to optimize the print so no supports are required and the 2 x 4 magnets on the bottom should be press fit although I'd add a dab of glue behind them. The holder for the light also is press fit but you can also glue that in to be more secure. Since the lights turn themselves off the batteries should last for years so personally I glued them in.

description: Wax seals are fantastic at adding a level of class to letters, in sealing envelopes, or for attatching tags to brithday and christmas presents. Personally I plan on using them for creating immersive TTRPG props for my D&D game, so that I can hand them printed notices ( like these free ones ). Unfortunately, having a wax seal stamp design for every occasion, affiliation, or character can get expensive… so why not design and 3D print them? This is my first attempt at creating a design using one of my illustrations for Fantastical Geographic's debut . This design uses measurements taken from a proper wood and metal wax seal stamp so that the proportions of your seal will be similar, but also so that you can simply swap out the head and handle as you see fit as these are modeled separately. Or if you have a lot of metal stamp heads already you could simply want some fancy handles to accompany them instead of swapping things out. The head design and print profile have been optimized for 0.2mm nozzles as my experiments showed this yielded the best results. The head prints face up and uses ironing to create a smooth stamping surface for easy release, however, it is IMPORTANT to note that your ironing settings may need adjusting as this varies depending on printer, filament type, filament brand, and filament color! I've opted for PLA as it's the most accessible for many printers. If you are interested in reading my experiments I will be uploading a full write-up on my website of how I achieved the cleanest wax seal and release of the stamp (link to come). The TLDR is: 0.2 mm nozzle Head printed face up with ironing on 0.08mm layer height. 50% Infill 100% cooling Release Agent - A thin layer applied with an old brush Pre-cooling - Place the stamp in the freezer for 10-15 minutes (make sure to apply release agent first) Wait - Leave the stamp in the wax for about 1 minute before gently peeling off Additional Notes: I have included a 0.4mm nozzle profile, however, I was not able to get the ironing as smooth as the 0.2mm. It is there primarily for printing the handle, which doesn't require the high detail. These results were achieved with a tuned PLA filament profile for my machine. Your mileage may vary.

Fully assembled it is almost 24 inches long. Features: Working picatinny rail with attachments. Sights can be quick swapped with each other or a scope if you go with 8x2 magnets. 2 different threaded muzzle options 2 sight options 1 scope option 1 under barrel “flashlight / laser combo” (2 parts held together with magnets) 1 under barrel grip Most parts are separated out for easy color printing. I'll provide an AMS profile for some of the main parts & accessories if you want to go that route. (Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. If not using magnets you can print our 8mmx4mm plugs. I'm probably missing something but will update notes as needed. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HELLDIVERS SWAG o7

description: This one is for Squidward who relentlessly pushed for me to make the model, and then was so grateful when I got started! I hope you enjoy it! If you would prefer to print it all in one color (to save time and money), you should be able to easily paint the mesh portion black with some black acrylic paint. I also experimented with how the horns are printed and attached to the head to make them more integrated into the design and also to avoid needing supports on them. In this version I tweaked the hole size for the head and flattened the bottom of the print a bit to improve printability and eliminate some of the supports. I believe this should fit any head pretty easily now. One under appreciated part of my work is figuring out how to get a model absolutely maximize the space of a p1s sized printer. In this case of this print, lots of adjustments were made to get it just right. For this hobby (designing and 3d printing models) I certainly go through phases. After filling up all the wall space in a room with Hollow Knight masks, I prioritized new areas. This was a nice break from my current phase which has been pond fountains, I think I have one more of those left in me before switching again. description: So I’ve been working on this for a bit, and I finally have my crate-style Steam Machine case ready to share! All ports remain open and accessible, so cables and accessories can stay plugged in without removing the cover. The power button is also easy to reach, but it is disguised as a nail head in the bottom-right corner of the crate. This keeps the front of the case looking clean while blending the button naturally into the design. The result is a decorative Steam Machine case that adds character to a gaming setup without blocking the console’s everyday features. How To Assemble Step 1: Remove designed support areas and brims Step 2: Connect top and bottom halves of the box Step 3: Push all decorative nail heads into the corners Step 4: Put final power button nail into bottom right hand corner Step 5: Place over top of Steam Machine --- and game away!!!

description: Disclosure Day Device - Movie Accurate Replica This is the most geometrically accurate 3D printable replica of the Disclosure Day Device available online. While other models found on the internet often simplify or misunderstand the complex shapes of this prop, this version was designed completely from scratch in Fusion 360 using meticulous reverse engineering. Instead of just tracing an outline, I spent hours analyzing individual movie frames and reference images to decipher the exact design logic used by the original prop makers. The Geometry & Design Process By studying how light and shadows interact with the device's facets across different film frames, I uncovered the underlying mathematical structure of the prop. The entire body is generated by lofting and transitioning between three distinct geometric profiles : 1. Top and Bottom Profile: A precise, uniform Heptagon (7-sided polygon). 2.Center Profile: A sharp Square/Rectangle that forms the wide midsection. This specific combination creates the unique, shifting facets that give the device its iconic look—a detail that other creators completely miss because they don't take the time to figure out how the original designers actually constructed the figure. Screen-Accurate Details The Glyphs: The symbols engraved on the upper facet were fully recreated from scratch using high-resolution reference images, ensuring every line, dot, and proportion is completely true to the screen. Print-Optimized: Designed with structural durability in mind, guaranteeing a flawless print that captures the sharp edges and dramatic transitions of the prop. If you are looking for a true, movie-accurate replica born from genuine engineering and deep analysis rather than a rushed approximation, this is the model for you.

description: Model for Thor's Hammer from Thor: Love and Thunder. Hammer head splits into different pieces like in the movie and are held together using magnets. Print orientation in the .3mf matches the orientations I used when I printed it, but you might need to test printing in different orientations if the fit between two of the hammer head pieces isn't lining up well. The magnets used are 10x2mm and are superglued into the holes. You'll need around 210 magnets. Depending on the infill percentage and what you intend to do with the hammer (display vs carry around), you might need to adjust the strength of the magnets. I used 20% infill for a display build and the hammer stays together, but the pieces can come apart come apart when yanked. 20% infill gives the hammer a nice weight to it, but 10-15% might be better for balancing with the magnet strength. I printed all the pieces on an Ender v2 with a smooth plate. I used Cura to slice it so it just had straight supports. I used a generic coffee brown PLA for the handle and generic silk silver PLA for the hammer head pieces. The Bambu filaments selected below should match the generic ones I used. I tested some of the prints on my Bambu P2S and they printed fine. I used tree supports on the starting textured plate to test the prints. I would recommend a smooth plate since most of the head pieces print on one of the hammer faces so smooth will look better. I transferred all the settings I used in Cura into the .3mf, but did slow down the print settings for the P2S with silk. Leather strap was found at craft store and cut to fit the hole in the hammer hilt.

If future images reveal inaccuracies, I'll update the design where practical. 🖨️ Print notes - Single-colour print - No AMS required - Designed to print cleanly as a display piece For the most screen-accurate appearance, I recommend printing in a metallic or silk filament. description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

The neon sign outside his shop flickered three times before it died, the hum of corporate enforcer hovercars rumbles past the alley, getting closer by the second. Kael shoves the dagger into the sheath strapped to his boot, touches the back of his neck where the implant was already starting to fester, and finds smooth cool skin instead of oozing rot. He squints at the faint ancient galactic script carved along the edge of the blade, and realizes this wasn’t a lost cargo—it was a lure, and he just took the bait that the last void hunter left behind. model_name: Caine from The Amazing Digital Circus
description: Cosplay Caine the Ring Master from The Amazing Digital Circus (TADC) Printed in white PETG, with 2 walls, 2% lightning infill (basically hollow) to make it was light as possible. These files are for printing the teeth/jaws. They're split into 3 segments for each jaw; front, left, and right. And should fit on an Ender 3, or any 220 printbed or larger. The segments dovetail together, but I still recommend glue or plastic welding for the strongest attachment possible. It is designed to clip onto the brim of a baseball cap, and the aliceband isn't meant to sit it normally would on your head, but add better stability to the brim, because the center of gravity is farther forward than you would expect. I ultimately glued some nickels to the back to bring the center of gravity farther back for balance. However, if I were to do it again, I would add strategic infill to the farthest back section (in the slicer) for counterweight and to reinforce the clip connector holes, which I broke. I also recommend adding springs to the back of the jaws to space them apart, and keep them from hitting each other. I played around with various 3D printed springs, which I included. However, I ultimately broke the connectors while switching them, and just 3D printed a straight, flat rectangle piece that I plastic welded to them. Really, anything will work, as long as you attach something to them to keep them apart. I also recommend connecting the front of the jaws using fishing line. I included some small holes where fishing line may be attached, however they came out too small in my print, perhaps do to my printer settings in the slicer. I ultimately tied the fishing line around the seems where the segments meet, where it would be completely hidden. I would also recommend using a touch of hot glue on the knots, to absolutely make sure they stay. And of course you can adjust the length to choose how open the mouth hangs open, just make sure both lines are the same length. I choose to space them so that the bottom jaw doesn't rest on my shoulders, so it all turns with my head, but it also closes if I shrug my shoulders. For my cosplay, I used contact cement to glue a large stripe of red craft foam around the "gums" for texture and to hide the seams, and then I sealed it with Mod Podge for toughness and luster. A hair dryer can also be used to help shrink wrap the foam to the print, but be careful not to let the plastic get too hot or it could warp. I just painted the inside gums red, since they're less visible, and I was very concerned about weight since I was going to be wear it for long hours.
